The methodology was compared with state-of-the-art approaches with three-criterion recognition quality assessment and resource consumption evaluation. The results indicate that the proposed method is competitive with reference approaches in stationary environments and performs best when concept drifts occur.

authors.name: Joanna Komorniczak
authors.institution: Wrocław University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Local fluctuations, majorization, and nontransitivity in cube tilings of $\mathbb{Z}^d$
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ into translates of the discrete unit cube $\{0,1\}^d$. For a uniformly chosen $\varepsilon\in\{0,1\}^d$, we count the cubes of $\mathcal{P}$ entirely contained in the observation window $[0,3]^d+\varepsilon$. The resulting score has mean $(3/2)^d$ for every partition, while its distribution reflects the geometry of the tiling. Comparing two such scores, with the shifts chosen independently, defines a game in which the larger score wins. In dimension $d=4$, we construct a geometric realization of the Steinhaus--Trybu{\l}a paradox: three periodic partitions form a cycle in which each beats the next with probability strictly greater than $1/2$. We describe local configurations by finite cube tiling codes and prove that every resulting list of counts is majorized by that of the simple code $C_d=\{0,2\}^d$. Nevertheless, every non-simple code differing from $C_d$ in only two coordinate directions beats it, with a sharp lower bound on the winning margin. We also show that the ratio of wins to losses of $C_d$ has limit superior at most $1$ as the dimension tends to infinity, uniformly over opposing codes. For $4\mathbb{Z}^d$-periodic tilings, changing the window size can repeatedly reverse the winner, but the winning margin eventually stabilizes separately for side lengths $4m+1$ and $4m+3$.

authors.name: Andrzej P. Kisielewicz
authors.institution: Wrocław University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Spiking neuromodulation: a linear control perspective
papers.abstract: Neuronal excitability is a nonlinear phenomenon, and the complexity of spiking experimental traces sometimes looks defeating. The present paper takes the view point that excitability is a neuromodulated property, and aims to demonstrate that the neuromodulation of spiking is amenable to the classical linear analysis tools of control theory. We illustrate the value of linear feedback analysis as an alternative to bifurcation analysis in the simple yet classical example of spiking modulation by the A-type potassium current.

papers.title: Characterization of the Frequency-Current Curve of First-Order High-Pass Neurons
papers.abstract: A spiking model, called the High-Pass (HP) model, has recently been proposed as a minimal excitable primitive. This model is composed of a static activation function, usually a sigmoid, in positive feedback with a high-pass filter. The HP model enters a tonic spiking regime whenever its input lies in the high-gain zone of the sigmoid, where the sigmoid's slope exceeds 1. In neuroscience, the frequency-current (FI) curve is the standard way of characterizing the tonic spiking regime of a neuron. So far, the FI curve of the HP model has been characterized analytically only for specific sigmoids, and has otherwise been computed through simulation. These simulations are computationally heavy, since simulating neurons requires solving a stiff system of differential equations. This paper bridges this gap by analytically characterizing the FI curve of the HP model with a first-order high-pass filter, for a broad class of sigmoid functions. The FI curve of the first-order HP model can be computed by solving two input-independent equations and evaluating two input-dependent integrals, with no need to simulate the model itself. A spiking primitive is said to be Type I (resp. Type II) if tonic spiking starts at a zero (resp. non-zero) frequency. This paper also shows that, for the HP model, the type depends solely on the local shape of the sigmoid at the outer edges of its high-gain zone. A sharp corner, where the derivative approaches a value strictly smaller than 1 from the outside, yields a Type I primitive. A locally twice differentiable corner, with a bounded second derivative and a derivative approaching 1 at the edge, yields a Type II primitive.

papers.title: New persistent chain spaces: identifying and computing the relevant persistent Laplacians of a filtration
papers.abstract: Persistent homology (PH) summarizes the topological features of data that persist across scales, but it is insensitive to many geometric properties. Persistent Laplacians (PLs) address this limitation: for a pair of simplicial complexes in a filtration, the kernel of the persistent Laplacian recovers the persistent Betti number, while its non-zero spectrum carries additional geometric information. However, PLs are defined for individual pairs of filtration values, so analysing a whole filtration requires evaluating many operators that largely contain the same information, and the result is hard to summarize and interpret. In this paper, we show that this redundancy has a precise structure. For each pair of filtration values, we decompose the space of chains underlying the persistent up-Laplacian into the contributions inherited from the neighboring pairs and a remaining part, which we call the new persistent chain space. We show that the new persistent chain spaces of all earlier pairs form a direct sum decomposition of this space, so that every persistent up-Laplacian in the filtration is determined by them. Moreover, the new persistent chain spaces are non-trivial only at pairs given by the persistence pairing in the same and in the next homological dimension, so that the persistence pairing determines exactly where the persistent up-Laplacian can change. Experiments on several types of point clouds show that evaluating persistent Laplacians only at these pairs reduces the computation time, both for our implementation and for existing software.

papers.title: Learning Generative Dynamics for 3D Molecule Generation via Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constraints
papers.abstract: Diffusion models have recently emerged as a powerful paradigm for generating 3D molecules. Despite showing remarkable promise, they learn atomic distributions implicitly from data, without explicitly encoding physicochemical rules into their generative dynamics. Consequently, generated samples can be statistically plausible yet chemically invalid. To address this problem, we propose Sequential Neuro-Symbolic Constrained Diffusion (SensDiff), a framework that integrates symbolic rules into generative modeling, enabling the model to internalize scientific priors during training. Central to SensDiff is the observation that the diffusion trajectory of 3D molecule generation exhibits a coarse-to-fine evolution: valid molecules arise by first mitigating macroscopic geometric conflicts and then refining structures toward microscopic chemical consistency through iterative denoising. Accordingly, SensDiff mirrors this dynamic by sequentially enforcing constraints with adaptive weighting during training, progressively steering generation toward valid molecular geometries. Moreover, SensDiff translates domain knowledge into interpretable generative controls, grounding opaque neural denoising in scientific principles. Experiments on molecular benchmarks and real-world constrained generation tasks confirm that SensDiff consistently improves chemical validity while adhering to physicochemical rules and user-specified targets. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/NeurIPS2026_SensDiff.

authors.name: Xu Sun
authors.institution: Jiangsu Key Laboratory for Chemistry of Low-Dimensional Materials

papers.title: Controllable Molecule Generation via Sparse Representation Editing: An Interpretability-Driven Perspective
papers.abstract: Controllable molecule generation is crucial for diverse scientific applications, such as drug discovery and materials design. While large language models (LLMs) show great promise, their dense and entangled representations impede precise control over the generation of molecules with bespoke substructures or properties. To address this, we propose Sparse Representation Editing (SpaRE), an interpretability-driven framework for fine-grained and precise control in LLM-based molecule generation. The crux of SpaRE is to learn an overcomplete sparse feature space that disentangles LLM representations into a compact set of latent features corresponding to chemically meaningful concepts. Within this space, we can directly manipulate these concept-aligned latent features to achieve (1) local control, by generating target atoms and functional groups at specified positions; and (2) global control, by customizing the overall structural and physicochemical properties within defined ranges. In this way, our framework advances interpretability from post-hoc analysis to actionable generative control. Experiments show that SpaRE can generate chemically desirable molecules under complex constraints in real-world scenarios, while offering mechanistic insights for quantitative structure-property analysis. The code and demo are available at https://github.com/WanyuGroup/ICML2026_SpaRE.

authors.name: Xu Sun
authors.institution: Jiangsu Key Laboratory for Chemistry of Low-Dimensional Materials

papers.title: ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation
papers.abstract: Language-model agents use experience through external retrieval and parameter learning. Consolidating stored experience into model weights requires deciding both which experience to train on and when its external records can leave retrieval. Admission based solely on student mastery can exclude useful teacher demonstrations, while removal immediately after training can discard guidance that the model still needs. We introduce ENGRAM, a framework that separates training admission from memory release. A demonstration-aware gate admits skills based on student mastery or sufficient successful teacher demonstrations. The student learns from selected action traces with context from an Engram Trace Graph (ETG). A verification gate then compares the updated model without episodic retrieval against the base model with retrieval on reserved probes. Release requires valid training participation and scores meeting both relative and absolute criteria; records for skills that fail verification remain retrievable. Experiments across interactive and reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains over frozen-weight ETG controls, with ablations supporting demonstration-aware admission and selective adapter activation. A controlled held-out comparison shows that verified release substantially reduces the retrievable footprint while remaining close to retain-all performance and outperforming immediate and budget-matched random release. ENGRAM also improves task performance while reducing input-token usage and model calls. Skill-level verification further reduces retrievable experience through selective archival, retaining external guidance for skills that do not meet the release criteria. Code is available in anonymous.4open.science/r/engram-anonymous.

authors.name: Lihuan Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Challenges, Opportunities, and Misconceptions in Neurosymbolic AI
papers.abstract: We examine opportunities for neurosymbolic AI alongside increasingly powerful neural models, particularly with regards to efficiency, safety and interpretability. We identify two major challenges: ensuring semantic alignment between neural and symbolic components, and managing the computational cost of symbolic inference and learning. We discuss representative methodological approaches to these challenges and address several common misconceptions concerning differentiability, independence assumptions, and scalability. This paper synthesizes perspectives developed through discussions in the Neurosymbolic Programming and Reasoning (NPR) working group at the 2026 CNRS workshop Neurosymbolic Methods and Their Applications in Data Science, rather than providing an exhaustive survey.

authors.name: Pierre Geneves
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université Grenoble Alpes

authors.name: Meghyn Bienvenu
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Thomas Schiex
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

authors.name: Sylvie Thiebaux
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Decoupled Mode Connectivity for Base-to-Novel Generalization in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract:
Prompt learning adapts vision-language models such as CLIP by optimizing a short learnable prompt. The cross-entropy objective pulls this prompt toward
  base-class specialization, whereas generalization to unseen classes benefits from staying close to CLIP's zero-shot feature space. Because both objectives
  act on the same prompt, their gradients conflict at convergence, and in our experiments no single-prompt loss design clearly improves on the cosine
  baseline. We propose Decoupled Mode Connectivity (DMC), which gives each objective its own prompt. Starting from a base-trained prompt, DMC trains a
  specialization prompt and a generalization prompt, and merges their text features with a fixed coefficient at test time, at the inference cost of a single
  prompt. A linear mode connectivity (LMC) corridor in text-feature space keeps the classification loss low for every classifier interpolated between the two
  endpoints, and a Visual Anchor KL term preserves CLIP's zero-shot class-similarity distribution of each image during specialization. We further argue that
  such regularizers should satisfy class-permutation invariance (CPI), and show via Fano's inequality, in an idealized model, that violating CPI
  lower-bounds the drop in novel accuracy by a term proportional to the mutual information between the prompt and the base-class labels. Across 11 datasets,
  DMC improves the average harmonic mean of base and novel accuracy over MergeTune for both CoOp and KgCoOp, and its interpolation curves pass beyond the
  single-prompt operating point, shifting the base-novel frontier rather than trading along it. Code is available at https://github.com/IemProg/DMC.

authors.name: Enzo Tartaglione
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Stephane Lathuiliere
authors.institution: Centre Inria de l'Université Grenoble Alpes

papers.title: Practical Non-Stationary Graph Gaussian Processes
papers.abstract: Gaussian processes on graphs provide a principled framework for prediction and uncertainty estimation, but modelling heterogeneous networks often requires balancing flexibility against parameter complexity. Variability at a node may reflect useful signal that should propagate through the network, unreliable measurements whose influence should be suppressed, or a mixture of both. We introduce Variance-Coupled Gaussian Processes (VCGPs), which use a positive auxiliary signal to modulate graph interactions through a single learned coupling exponent. The exponent controls how strongly high-variability nodes propagate or attenuate information, while a cluster-wise extension accommodates different regimes within the same graph. Under stated structural assumptions, we characterize the unique stationary-rescaling point of the basic family, where correlations match those of a stationary graph kernel while node-dependent variances remain. Experiments on traffic, air-quality and weather datasets show competitive prediction and uncertainty estimation relative to stationary and per-node non-stationary baselines, with the largest gains on networks requiring multiple coupling regimes. Stationary correlations after variance rescaling remain sufficient on some data, and performance depends on the auxiliary signal and model selection.

authors.name: K. S. Sesh Kumar
authors.institution: Vallurupalli Nageswara Rao Vignana Jyothi Institute of Engineering and Technology

papers.title: Safe Circumnavigation on Heterogeneous Orbits: A Range-Only HOCBF-QP Framework for Nonholonomic Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Circumnavigating a stationary target with a team of robots requires each robot to hold its own standoff distance, to stay evenly spaced from its neighbours, and to avoid collisions with the target and with each other at every instant. The task becomes arduous when the robots are assigned different orbital radii, as their sensors or roles may demand. This paper presents a safety-critical control framework for this problem. Each robot commands both its acceleration and its turn-rate, measures only its distance to the target, and exchanges information only with its two ring neighbours. The design has three features. First, a structural property of the model lets one control law serve every robot regardless of its assigned radius. Second, the acceleration drives each radius exactly to its target, while the turn-rate balances the formation with the neighbours. Third, a higher-order control-barrier-function quadratic program enforces target, geofence, and inter-robot safety on both inputs at once; it leaves the nominal controller untouched away from the constraints and stays valid while the unmeasured range rate is still being estimated. Simulations confirm these guarantees. In a comparison, the closest existing multi-orbit design, even with full state information, violates both the target standoff and the inter-robot margin, whereas the proposed controller does not.

authors.name: Anand Singh
authors.institution: Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University

papers.title: Optimal robust comonotonic risk sharing under operational constraints
papers.abstract: Risk-sharing arrangements such as reinsurance programs and catastrophe pools must satisfy operational constraints, including capacity limits, attachment bands, retention rules and cession limits. Under distortion risk measures, the unconstrained optimum assigns each loss layer to the participant for whom that layer is least costly, but operational constraints break this layerwise rule, and there is no general method to compute the constrained optimum. We show that, for comonotonic allocations, the participants' distortion risk measures and the operational constraints are linear in the amount of each loss layer held by each participant, so the constrained risk-sharing problem on a discretized loss is a linear program that standard software can solve. Its dual gives supporting prices for the loss layers and the marginal value of relaxing each operational constraint. Where the set of binding constraints changes, the constrained optimal value can have a kink, and the smallest and largest optimal multipliers then give the one-sided effects of relaxing and tightening a constraint. To protect the allocation against disagreement between loss models, we also consider the robust version of the risk-sharing problem, that is, minimizing the worst-case total risk assessment over finitely many probability scenarios. This robust problem is again a linear program, and we quantify the cost of protection against model uncertainty from its optimal value. We illustrate the approach with a catastrophe reinsurance tower.

papers.title: Predicting fitness from genomic offset: a multivariate latent-trait framework
papers.abstract: Genomic offset methods quantify the genetic consequences of environmental change using genotype environment associations (GEA), but the conditions under which they predict fitness remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a theoretical framework linking genomic offset to relative fitness loss through multivariate latent adaptive traits under stabilizing selection. We show that squared genomic offset is linearly related to expected log relative fitness loss when averaged over genetic architectures, provided that direct environmental effects are absent. However, this relationship does not necessarily hold for a realized genetic architecture. We identify two complementary mechanisms that can explain high predictive accuracy of genomic offset statistics. First, when effective adaptive dimensionality is sufficiently large, the genetically mediated fitness response concentrates around its marginal expectation, reducing the dependence on the particular genetic architecture. Second, even with few adaptive traits, accurate predictions can arise from geometric alignment between the complete fitness loss matrix and the GEA metric. This second mechanism also encompasses direct environmental effects and their interactions with genetically mediated responses, which may preserve or weaken predictive accuracy depending on their alignment. We further derive bounds on predictive accuracy that characterize these effects. Our results clarify the assumptions and limitations underlying genomic offset predictions and suggest that genomic offset is best interpreted as a measure of genetically informed adaptive mismatch, rather than a direct predictor of realized fitness or any particular phenotypic trait.

papers.title: TRGB Distances to the Andromeda Dwarf Satellites from the INT Monitoring Survey
papers.abstract: We measure tip of the red giant branch (TRGB) distances to 17 dwarf satellites of M31 from Sloan $i$-band photometry of the Isaac Newton Telescope (INT) monitoring survey of Local Group dwarf galaxies, and add the distances of And I, And VII and And IX from earlier papers of the survey. We locate the tip with a Sobel edge-detection filter applied to the luminosity function of stars within two half-light radii of each galaxy. The distance moduli range from $23.38 \pm 0.06$ mag (And XVI, 474 kpc) to $25.35 \pm 0.06$ mag (And XVIII, 1177 kpc), and 15 of the 20 satellites lie between 650 and 850 kpc. For most galaxies, our distance agrees with at least one published value. Compared with Conn et al. (2012), our tip is brighter for 12 of the 18 galaxies in common, by up to 0.39 mag, possibly because of crowding in the central regions. And XII lies at $844^{+40}_{-38}$ kpc, about 60 kpc behind M31, consistent with a first infall into the Local Group. And XXII lies at $753^{+28}_{-27}$ kpc, closer than all earlier estimates, and about 59 kpc from M33 in three dimensions (for an M33 distance of 794 kpc), consistent with an association with M33. And XVIII lies about 400 kpc behind M31, too far for a secure association with M31.

papers.title: Hausdorff dimension of planar box-like self-affine sets with rotations
papers.abstract: We study the Hausdorff dimension of proximal planar self-affine sets whose defining maps have diagonal or anti-diagonal linear parts, with both types present. Such systems are irreducible but not strongly irreducible. Under a projective exponential separation condition, we show that the Hausdorff dimension equals the minimum of $2$ and the affinity dimension, thereby extending the dimension formula of Hochman--Rapaport to all proximal irreducible planar systems. When the affinity dimension is at most an explicit threshold determined by the Lyapunov exponents, the formula holds assuming only that there are no exact overlaps. Above the threshold, it holds under the strong open set condition. These dimension formulae are proved by approximation with finite diagonal subsystems. Assuming projective exponential separation, we also determine the pointwise dimensions of the coordinate projections of the equilibrium state. Below the threshold, the projections are not exact-dimensional: the pointwise dimension of each exists almost everywhere and takes exactly two values, each on a set of positive measure. At or above the threshold, both projections are exact-dimensional with dimension one.

authors.name: Karoly Simon
authors.institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics

papers.title: From PAC bounds on the generalization error to PAC bounds on the parameter estimation error
papers.abstract:
Probably Approximately Correct (PAC) bounds on the generalization error (the difference between the empirical prediction error computed on the training data and its expectation) are an established tool in statistical machine learning, and there have been several extensions of these bounds to dynamical systems. In parallel, in recent years, there has been growing interest in finite-sample bounds for parameter estimation error in system identification. The latter bounds tend to be algorithm-specific, relying on reformulating the identification algorithm as a least-squares regression problem. This is in contrast to classical PAC bounds, which are algorithm-agnostic and can be applied to any identification algorithm based on minimizing a cost function involving the empirical loss.
  In this paper, we show how oracle bounds derived from PAC bounds can be used to derive finite-sample bounds for dynamical systems. As an illustration of this approach, we present finite-sample parameter-estimation bounds for linear and bilinear systems with bounded inputs and noise. These bounds apply to identification algorithms based on minimizing a regularized empirical loss function.
  The key ingredient is to establish an oracle inequality, i.e., an inequality between the true prediction error of the learned model and the minimum achievable true prediction error, and then use either the convexity of the true loss or system-theoretic properties of the loss function to derive bounds on the parameter estimation error. We also analyze the rates of the obtained bounds and compare them with those of classical asymptotic results.

authors.name: Mihaly Petreczky
authors.institution: HUN-REN Institute for Computer Science and Control

authors.name: Balint Daroczy
authors.institution: HUN-REN Institute for Computer Science and Control

papers.title: DC-Link Voltage Regulation in a Single-Isolation-Stage Multioutput Solid-State Transformer for Wide-Range DC Outputs
papers.abstract: Single-isolation-stage solid-state transformers with balancing circuits eliminate an additional downstream dc--dc conversion stage. However, the remaining isolated converters must directly accommodate a wide output-voltage range. This paper investigates variable dc-link voltage operation of a single-isolation-stage multioutput SST to ease this requirement. Coordinated cascaded H-bridge modulation and embedded four-switch balancing circuits support intentionally unequal submodule dc-link voltages, allowing the isolated-converter input voltages to be adjusted according to the output requirements. The achievable voltage range is determined by relating the required balancing power to the BC transfer capability within the available CHB switching windows, subject to modulation and peak and rms current limits. The analysis quantifies the range extension provided by BC operation beyond modulation alone. For a single-phase-shift dual-active-bridge converter, input-voltage following within this range reduces the calculated peak current and extends the ideal zero-voltage-switching region compared with fixed input. Experiments on a six-submodule SST prototype demonstrate unequal dc-link voltage operation and inter-submodule power exchange. Experiments result on DAB demonstrate reduced current stress and improved efficiency with voltage following.

papers.title: An Optimal Power-Flow Grouping Topology for Single-Isolation-Stage Multi-Output Solid-State Transformers
papers.abstract: Electric-vehicle dc fast-charging stations and data centers require multiple high-power dc outputs with independently varying demands. Conventional multi-output solid-state transformers typically establish a common dc bus and use downstream dc/dc converters for port-level regulation and, where required, galvanic isolation. A single-isolation-stage solid-state transformer can eliminate this additional high-power interface stage by directly forming multiple isolated outputs from its submodule dc/dc stages. However, because one submodule is generally insufficient for an individual output port, multiple submodules must be connected in parallel, while inter-submodule balancing circuits redistribute power under unbalanced loading. The submodule grouping therefore determines the internal balancing-power paths. Sequential grouping can create long transfer paths and accumulated balancing power, increasing current stress and losses. This paper proposes an optimal power-flow grouping topology that interleaves submodules assigned to different output ports, thereby localizing power redistribution and reducing the power processed by the balancing circuits. Analytical models quantify the required balancing power and its reduction relative to sequential grouping. A coordinated submodule-bypass strategy is also developed, and the remaining output-power capability under different fault scenarios is evaluated. A six-submodule prototype validates the proposed topology. Under the same highly unbalanced operating conditions, the proposed topology reduces the maximum submodule dc-link voltage difference by 63\% and the peak balancing current by 14.5%, while improving the measured efficiency by approximately 5.6% at rated power. Stable post-fault operation is also experimentally demonstrated.

papers.title: Beyond the Pseudo-Inverse: GIM Precoding for Per-Antenna Power Minimisation in MU-MIMO
papers.abstract: We study linear precoder design for multi-user MIMO downlink under per-antenna power constraints (PAPC), which arise naturally when each antenna port has its own power amplifier. While the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse is the unique optimal generalized inverse for zero-forcing precoding under a total power constraint [1], we prove this optimality does not extend to the MMSE/RZF case under PAPC. Any precoder in the Generalized Inverse Matrix (GIM) family shares the same effective channel and per-user SINRs as the pseudo-inverse baseline, while its null-space component reshapes the per-antenna power profile. This separation principle enables minimising peak per-antenna power at fixed SINR targets with zero SINR penalty. We characterise the convex peak-power problem over this family and its active-set optimality, establish MRT and ZF asymptotic limits, and provide a convergent first-order subgradient algorithm. Simulations with 8-64 antennas confirm gains of 1.9-3.7 dB over pseudo-inverse RZF, with GIM-MMSE eliminating essentially all PAPC violations up to 20% per-antenna budget imbalance. The framework applies directly to fully-digital massive MIMO. Cell-free and hybrid analog-digital arrays are promising extensions.

papers.title: High-Volume Wurtzite MnSe in MnSe/CdSe Superlattices: Structure, Magnetism and Optical Response
papers.abstract: Polymorphism in Mn-based chalcogenides offers access to magnetic semiconductors with distinct crystal symmetries, polar structures, and different magnetic orders. In particular, wurtzite MnSe exhibits an appealing interplay of electric polarization and several competing magnetic phases including altermagnetic order. However, stabilizing metastable polymorphs, such as wurtzite MnSe, in experimentally useful volumes remains challenging. Here, we show that a nanoscale-period MnSe/CdSe superlattice stabilizes wurtzite MnSe over micrometer-scale total thickness while suppressing the formation of the thermodynamically favored rock-salt phase. The increased magnetic volume enables bulk-sensitive characterization of this polar polymorph. The room-temperature lattice parameters of wurtzite MnSe are studied by independent experimental techniques and determined to be $a = (4.18 \pm 0.03)\,\mathring{A}$ and $c = (6.78 \pm 0.03)\, \mathring{A}$. SQUID magnetometry reveals antiferromagnetic ordering with $T_N = 62\,\text{K}$, which is accompanied by an anomaly of the MnSe lattice parameter, as oberved by temperature-dependent X-ray diffraction. Optical measurements reveal excitonic transitions pointing to the band gap at around 3.4 eV. These results highlight the utility and importance of heterostructure engineering for detailed studies of metastable phases of magnetic semiconductors, in particular wurtzite MnSe.

authors.name: Anna Kaleta
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Safe Reinforcement Learning via Probabilistic Option Shielding
papers.abstract: Shielding is a safe reinforcement learning technique that provides safety guarantees while learning, by blocking unsafe actions. Traditional shielding relies on a complete model of the environment to provide long-term guarantees. Probabilistic logic shielding (PLS) lifts the requirement of having such model, but only considers safety in the short term, typically looking only one or few steps ahead. We propose Probabilistic Option Shielding (POS), which extends PLS to the option level, recovering long-horizon safety without reintroducing the need for a complete environment model. POS learns a model-free critic directly from one-step PLS signals, to estimate the probability that an entire option will complete safely under uncertainty. We evaluate POS on safe navigation tasks in the LogiCity environment, and show that it achieves considerably safer training while matching the task performance of standard step-level PLS and other safety related reinforcement learning baselines.

papers.title: Joint modelling of financial cost and carbon footprint in motor insurance claims: a BINAR(1) decision framework for circular auto parts adoption
papers.abstract: Motor insurance claims management increasingly faces a dual objective: controlling claim costs while reducing greenhouse-gas emissions associated with vehicle repair decisions. This paper proposes a bivariate, discrete-time modelling framework that links the dynamics of financial claims and repair-related carbon footprint inspired by a BINAR(1) dependence structure, allowing for temporal persistence, cross-dependence and a positive/negative correlation between the two dimensions. Using externally sourced emission factors and cost information for replacement parts, we operationalise the carbon footprint of claims under two repair pathways: new parts versus circular-economy reused parts (PIEC). We then conduct scenario analyses in which the acceptance rate of reused parts varies, and we quantify the joint implications for expected monetary outlays and CO 2 -equivalent emissions. Results show that higher PIEC acceptance can simultaneously reduce expected emissions and average claim cost, and the magnitude of the joint benefit depends on the dependence structure and persistence captured by the BINAR(1) process. The proposed framework provides a transparent, reproducible tool for insurers to evaluate repair-policy levers and to align claims operations with decarbonisation targets while retaining an explicit stochastic risk perspective.

authors.name: Stephane Loisel
authors.institution: Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers

papers.title: Non-asymptotic First- and Second-Order Tail Brackets for the Kostlan-Shub-Smale Field and Spherical k-Spin Complexity
papers.abstract: For the Kostlan-Shub-Smale field $X$ of degree $k\ge3$ on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, we prove the two-sided bound $(1-\varepsilon(u))\,\delta_{*}(u)\le\mathbb{P}\{\sup X>u\}\le\delta_{*}(u)$ at every finite $(k,d)$, where $\delta_{*}(u)$ is the expected number of critical points above $u$, halved when $k$ is even, and $\varepsilon(u)$ is explicit for $\rho u\ge\min\{d-1,\frac32\sqrt{2(d-1)}\}$. The gap is therefore at most of order $e^{-(1+\rho^{2})u^{2}/2}$ with $\rho^{2}=k/(2(k-1))$. We also give $\delta_{*}$ itself in closed form, as a finite sum of Hermite polynomials, together with a two-term envelope that is asymptotically sharp and a single-monomial relaxation of the form $Cu^{d-2}e^{-u^{2}/2}$. As an application we bracket the annealed complexity of the spherical $k$-spin Hamiltonian at every finite $(k,d)$: the upper bound holds at every energy, a lower bound of the same form at every energy above $9/4$ times the spectral edge $\sqrt{2(d-1)}/\rho$, above twice the edge when $d\ge10$, and is consistent with the Auffinger-Ben Arous-\v{C}ern\'y complexity function as $d\to\infty$.

authors.name: Federico Dalmao
authors.institution: Universidad de la República de Uruguay

papers.title: The Logic of Factor Portfolios: Boolean Rules, Interactions, and Trading Costs
papers.abstract: Investors turn signals into holdings through decision rules: buy the top decile, hold stocks with high momentum and low volatility, exclude stocks that fail a screen. Many such rules are Boolean functions of threshold statements about signal ranks, and writing them this way shows both what a rule holds and how often it trades. A Walsh decomposition splits the return of any rule into exposures to individual signals and to interactions among signals; an intersection and a union of the same two screens, for example, have opposite interaction exposures. The same coefficients, together with the persistence of the underlying statements, determine turnover. Interactions are less persistent than their components, so rules that load on higher-order interactions trade more, and thresholds discard information, so at equal risk threshold implementations of interactions trade more than smooth ones. In U.S. stocks from 1973 to 2024, these predictions hold closely: predicted and realized persistence have correlations of at least 0.999, predicted turnover matches realized turnover with a slope of 1.02, and the same interactions are more persistent as products of ranks than as threshold rules. Trading costs rise with order, and because premia fall with order, 58% of single-signal portfolios have absolute premia above their quoted-spread costs over 1995-2024, against 24% of two-signal and 6% of three-signal interaction portfolios. Out of sample, interaction portfolios raise the Sharpe ratio of single-signal tangency portfolios, and over 1995-2024 they reject a six-factor model that conventional sorts on the same signals do not reject.

papers.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring
papers.abstract: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.

papers.title: An Educated Guess: Deriving Statistically Aligned Gradient Estimates for Zeroth-Order Optimisation
papers.abstract: As novel hardware architectures are explored for the purposes of machine learning, including neuromorphic chips, asynchronous systems, and ASICs, effective learning algorithms are highly desirable. While backpropagation is the standard for differentiation on standard hardware, its requirement for global synchrony and exact differentiability limits the exploration of exotic algorithms on non-traditional substrates and devices. Zeroth-order (ZO) optimisation methods, such as SPSA and weight perturbation, offer a compelling alternative by estimating gradients through inference-only passes; however, these methods have historically suffered due to the `curse of dimensionality', where random perturbations become increasingly misaligned with the true gradient in high-dimensional spaces. In this work, we move beyond blind random noise by deriving zeroth-order search directions from activation geometry available during the forward pass. This leads to a family of Spectral Zeroth-Order methods, SZO-$\kappa$, whose directions solve local response-based gradient-guessing objectives under explicit stochastic assumptions. These methods explore feature-supported directions that are more likely to produce informative loss responses. Using multilayer and convolutional networks, we analyse gradient alignment, bias-variance structure, and training stability of these methods relative to standard perturbation baselines and backpropagation.

authors.name: Nasir Ahmad
authors.institution: National University of Sciences and Technology

papers.title: AudioSphere: Towards Self-Supervised Spatial Audio Representation Models
papers.abstract: Recent audio embedding models learn representations that transfer across clip- and frame-level tasks, yet they operate almost exclusively on single-channel signals and are blind to spatial structure. Spatial audio models capture that structure but rely on clip-level supervision or contrastive objectives, yielding embeddings unsuitable for frame-level tasks like sound event detection and localization (SELD). We argue this dichotomy is not fundamental: patch-level spatial self-supervision can jointly learn acoustic and spatial features at both temporal granularities. We introduce AudioSphere, a multi-channel masked autoencoder trained on Ambisonics recordings that reconstructs both spectral content and directional cues via a joint spatiotemporal masking strategy that masks both time-frequency patches and intensity vectors. AudioSphere supports frame-level predictions while producing strong clip-level representations via aggregation. Alongside the model, we release RealSELD, a standardized benchmark for evaluating frozen backbones on real-world multi-channel SELD. AudioSphere enables, for the first time, SELD with a frozen self-supervised backbone, while matching or exceeding prior self-supervised audio embedding models on clip-level classification tasks spanning environmental sound, speech, and music, and on frame-level sound event detection. All code and data are available at https://github.com/labhamlet/AudioSphere and https://huggingface.co/labhamlet.

authors.name: Goksenin Yuksel
authors.institution: Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition and Behaviour

papers.title: A Real-Space Framework for the Bare and Interacting Longitudinal Susceptibility of Solids
papers.abstract: We present an implementation of the bare and interacting longitudinal susceptibility in a full-potential linear muffin-tin orbital code. The bare susceptibility is built in real space from Matsubara sums of Kohn-Sham Green's functions and is resolved by site, spin and orbital degrees of freedom; the spin and charge susceptibilities follow from a Dyson equation, with an on-site exchange-correlation kernel. After testing the solver on the Stoner-like instability of bcc Fe, we apply it to four density-wave materials. The bare susceptibility peaks at H in bcc Cr, where the nonmagnetic state is close to a Stoner instability, and at the stripe vector M in FeSe. In LaTe3 the response of the Te nets peaks close to the observed charge-density-wave vector, at its image in the neighbouring Brillouin zone; which of the two equivalent vectors carries the response is set by the phases of the sites in the cell. In 2H-NbSe2 the response is weakly modulated, and the observed vector lies on the flank of a broad maximum, consistent with the known importance of electron-phonon coupling there. Antiferromagnetic order reduces the bare longitudinal response at the ordering vector by ~8% in Cr and about half in FeSe. The orbital decomposition of the bare susceptibility shows which orbitals contribute the most for the nearest-neighbor bonds.

authors.name: Olle Eriksson
authors.institution: Futurum - Akademin för Hälsa och Vård

papers.title: Chromospherically Active Stars in the MeerKAT Galactic Plane Survey
papers.abstract: Stellar magnetic activity has long been established to occur in subsets of late-type main-sequence stars and manifests itself in the form of chromospheric and coronal activity. This activity is driven by magnetic fields generated by dynamo mechanisms associated with stellar rotation and convection, which channel and dissipate magnetic energy to the outer atmospheric layers. Optical spectroscopic follow-up was carried out for 99 radio-X-ray coronally active stars of G-, K-, and M-spectral types in the SARAO MeerKAT Galactic plane survey point sources. There are 46 stars that exhibited chromospheric activity. Specifically, 39 stars show Ca II H&K emission lines, whereas 18 show Ca II IRT, 11 show both H&K and IRT lines. Of the 39 stars displaying H&K emission, 37 show activity levels greater than the Solar minimum activity. Their X-ray to bolometric luminosity ratios are within the coronal thresholds of > -4.5. In addition, we explored optical photometry to investigate the rotation information and found that these stars show short rotation periods; in comparison with activity levels, the activity levels dampen as the rotation periods increase. We also analysed optical light curves for a subset of stars, and they show flaring behaviour at the same epoch as enhanced chromospheric activity, indicating the flares and chromospheric emission are manifestations of the same underlying magnetic activity process.

papers.title: Scalable BLE Channel Sounding Localization with Ranging-Assisted PDoA
papers.abstract: Bluetooth Channel Sounding (CS) enables accurate phase-based ranging, but multi-anchor localization requires sequential ranging exchanges that limit scalability and increase measurement latency. This paper proposes Ranging-Assisted Phase Difference of Arrival (RA-PDoA), a scalable BLE localization architecture combining one active anchor performing a standard two-way CS exchange with multiple passive receive-only anchors observing the same transmissions. A channel-recovery framework is derived that enables passive anchors to reconstruct a channel response suitable for super-resolution delay estimation, allowing multipath-robust ranging without participating in a two-way exchange. Coarse arrival-time information is further used to bound the position estimate and reject inconsistent range solutions. A comprehensive evaluation characterizes the impact of multipath propagation, body shadowing, synchronization requirements, oscillator impairments, anchor placement, and deployment inaccuracies, thereby quantifying the practical infrastructure requirements for scalable BLE localization. Simulation results in modeled indoor environments show that RA-PDoA reduces the 90th-percentile localization error from 175.3 cm to 95.5 cm under body shadowing while maintaining an airtime requirement independent of the number of anchors. The results demonstrate that a single active ranging link enables scalable and multipath-robust BLE Channel Sounding localization.

papers.title: A Novel Algorithm to Simulate Conductance-based Neuronal Networks
papers.abstract: Conductance-based models are central to neurophysiology and neuromorphic engineering, yet their simulation scales poorly to large networks. We study and analyze an iterative solver that operates in signal space. Each iteration reduces to $N$ decoupled scalar linear time-varying differential equations, one per neuron, which are solved in parallel and in closed form. The solver admits two complementary interpretations: a variable metric forward-backward splitting method, rooted in operator theory, and a waveform relaxation quasi-Newton method, rooted in circuit simulation. We prove uniform and superlinear convergence, with a bound that reflects the conductance structure of the dynamics. The algorithm is illustrated on the classical Hodgkin--Huxley neuron and on networks of up to 5000 neurons.

papers.title: comfort-db: A Python toolkit to access, preprocess and explore the oceanographic COMFORT dataset
papers.abstract: comfort-db is a Python library that facilitates working with the COMFORT SQLite dataset, version 2. The dataset assembles global oceanographic measurements from ten datasets and contains a total of 458,724,734 in situ measurements from the years 1772 to 2020. comfort-db enables easy access to the database and provides preprocessing and exploratory analysis utilities. Preprocessing supports variable scaling and filtering by space, time and quality. Unit conversions can be applied during data loading or separately via a converter object. Gridding is supported and optionally works with bathymetry data to exclude grid cells on land. Moreover, the library supports general and field-specific exploratory data analysis through plotting functions, an interactive Dash app and functions to compute oceanographic profile and water mass statistics. comfort-db is open source (MIT license) and available from PyPI and GitHub.

authors.name: Boris Peter Koch
authors.institution: Alfred-Wegener-Institut Helmholtz-Zentrum für Polar- und Meeresforschung

papers.title: Payload-Blind Bistatic Delay-Doppler Sensing with Phase-Injected Chirps in CE-OFDM
papers.abstract: Constant-envelope orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CE-OFDM) preserves a unit-magnitude sample envelope, but its Hermitian-symmetric structure makes dedicated sensing pilots costly, and additive pilots disrupt this envelope. We show that injecting a known chirp, here a Zadoff-Chu (ZC) sequence, into the CE-OFDM phase enables payload-blind bistatic delay-Doppler sensing without dedicated sensing frames or an explicit pilot power split: the residual carrier, given by the ensemble mean under the adopted payload model, becomes an implicit superimposed pilot for a receive-only node. A Doppler-aligned receiver integrates this reference coherently across frames while the payload residual averages down. In contrast, phase-domain injected training (PIT) frame averaging, designed for quasi-static channel estimation, loses about 32 dB for the simulated target with 16 averaged frames. Closed-form approximations characterize the payload-induced floor, known-cell detection probability and direct-path tolerance. In the noise-limited simulations, the receiver incurs a 2.8 dB detection gap relative to a payload-aware matched filter without interference cancellation and matches a dedicated-pilot benchmark of equal reference energy without its 53% frame overhead.

papers.title: Metric Dimension Parameterized by Bag-Connected Treewidth and Bag-Connected Pathwidth
papers.abstract: The metric dimension of a graph is the minimum size of a set of vertices whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices of the graph. We prove that \MetricDimension{} is NP-complete on planar graphs of treewidth and bag-connected treewidth exactly three. The graphs in our construction have no induced cycle longer than four and have (prefix-connected) pathwidth at most four. In particular, the problem admits no XP algorithm parameterized by bag-connected treewidth unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$. This answers questions of Bonnet and Purohit and of Bousquet, Deschamps, and Parreau. We prove that the problem is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by bag-connected pathwidth.

papers.title: Controlled Excitation for Identification of Nonlinear Systems with Saturated Outputs
papers.abstract: We consider nonlinear systems whose measured output is the product of an unknown matrix and a known saturation function of the unmeasured state. Generating excitation that allows the matrix to be recovered from the output is challenging when the dynamics are largely unknown. We exploit saturation to construct this excitation. Under a geometric accessibility condition, we derive explicit open-loop controls that drive the state into regions where the saturation takes prescribed values. For componentwise saturations, this condition holds generically with as few as two independent control directions. The controls require no state measurement and only partial knowledge of the dynamics, with no information on the structure of its nonlinear part. The resulting regressor is known in advance, and the unknown matrix is recovered exactly by a closed-form regression. Under stronger structural assumptions and with sufficiently many independent outputs, an output feedback tracks prescribed reference trajectories within the unsaturated region to arbitrary accuracy and permits exact state recovery. Suitably chosen references then also enable exact identification of linearly parameterized (nonlinear) dynamics. We analyze robustness to measurement noise and illustrate the method numerically in the presence of both measurement and dynamical noise.

authors.name: Adel Malik Annabi
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Dario Prandi
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: The N/O-O/H relation across large-scale environments
papers.abstract: The large-scale structure (LSS) of the Universe shapes galaxy evolution through its intricate web-like morphology, yet its specific influence on gas-phase chemical abundances remains uncertain. Particularly, a homogeneous comparison of the N/O$-$O/H relation, a tracer of the mass assembly and baryonic cycle, across distinct LSS environments has been lacking. In this study, we analyse a local SDSS galaxy sample curated within the framework of the CAVITY project -- dedicated to studying void galaxies -- in which galaxies are classified by their LSS environment into three groups: clusters, voids, and non-cluster/non-void (NCNV). We extract spectroscopic emission line fluxes from the central SDSS spectra and analyse how different galaxy properties affect the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation. For that, we subtract the main N/O$-$O/H relation from the data and study the dependence of the resulting residuals ($\xi_\text{N/O}$) on a set of parameters, including stellar mass ($M_\star$), $g-r$ colour, and star formation rate (SFR). We find that $M_\star-$related variables are the best predictors of the scatter in the N/O$-$O/H relation, with little influence of the recent star formation history. Regarding the LSS comparison, no significant differences are found for void and NCNV galaxies. Cluster galaxies, however, present a N/O$-$O/H relation systematically lower (with $\xi_\text{N/O} \sim -0.02$). Consistent with this shift and with $M_\star$ as a good predictor of N/O$-$O/H deviations, we find that environmental dependences are also reflected in fundamental scaling relations: both the MZR and N/O$-M_\star$ relations are different for cluster galaxies. These combined results point to mechanisms in the dense intracluster medium (such as strangulation or re-accretion of metal-enriched gas) as the primary drivers of these chemical offsets for galaxies in cluster environments.

papers.title: Probing injection locking of an integrated nanolaser pair through RF beating
papers.abstract: We demonstrate simultaneous optical injection locking of an integrated pair of photonic-crystal nanolasers coupled to a common silicon waveguide. Due to fabrication-induced disorder, the two nanolasers exhibit distinct emission wavelengths, allowing their individual locking ranges to be resolved as a function of the injection-laser detuning and power. We identify a region where both nanolasers are simultaneously locked to the master laser. To probe this collective locked state, the two nanolasers are independently pump-modulated at distinct radio frequencies. A beat note at the difference frequency appears only within the overlap region, providing a direct RF signature of simultaneous locking. These results establish RF beating as a compact diagnostic of common-master injection locking in integrated nanolaser systems.

papers.title: Adaptive Depth Aggregation in Graph Transformers for Long-Range Graph Reasoning
papers.abstract: Graph Transformers improve long-range node-to-node communication through global or structure-aware interactions. However, improving cross-node communication does not determine how computations produced at different depths should be combined. Standard residual streams accumulate successive computations with fixed unit coefficients shared across nodes. This fixed aggregation is a residual-interface constraint: once intermediate contributions have been produced, the interface cannot explicitly reweight them by node. We hypothesize that this constraint can create a depth-wise aggregation mismatch when the relative utility of these intermediate contributions varies across nodes and structural contexts. To study this hypothesis, we formalize Graph Transformer residual computation as a causal node-wise history of graph-propagation and feed-forward network (FFN) contributions, making depth aggregation an explicit interface choice. We realize node-adaptive aggregation over this history with Attention Residuals (AttnRes) while preserving the backbone's graph-propagation and auxiliary-state machinery. Block AttnRes reduces the routing cost of long histories relative to Full AttnRes by pooling consecutive contributions. We instantiate the interface in GPS and GRIT and evaluate it on all five ECHO tasks. Both variants achieve lower mean absolute error (MAE) than their independently tuned backbones on every task, and at least one obtains the lowest mean among all compared methods in each task. Routing-only donor-swap interventions support the mismatch hypothesis, while additional ablations examine the key design choices. Together, these results support node-adaptive depth aggregation as a useful complement to cross-node communication in long-range graph reasoning.

papers.title: Relic and Gumi: Governing Memory, Safety, and Continuity in Diegetic Relational Agents
papers.abstract:
Longitudinal relational agents rely on memory for continuity, but remembering can lead to intrusion, clinical overconfidence, emotional manipulation, and opacity. We present Relic, a governance architecture for diegetic relational agents, and Gumi, a subject-specific companion agent initialized and governed through Relic. The architecture separates what the system can observe, what researchers can review, what Gumi can remember, and what Gumi can say.
  We describe three mechanisms. Relic represents sensitive safety signals as researcher-facing governance objects rather than user-facing explanations or agent memories. Shared Continuity Memory organizes relational markers around subject-confirmed wording, corrections, explicit follow-up permissions, and recall limits. We specify a runtime mediation layer for delivery, proactivity, session identity, output transformation, and platform allowlists; adoption across live paths remains partial. These mechanisms aim to preserve relational continuity without turning Gumi into a clinical assistant, mood tracker, general-purpose assistant, or opaque profiling system.
  We contribute the architecture, object model, researcher workbench design, and a proposed evaluation framework for governed relational memory. An exploratory pilot involved the author as P1 and one external participant as P2. Weekly self-reports from P1 and researcher-led interviews with P2 provide descriptive observations of early use and perceived naturalness. The pilot does not support claims about clinical efficacy, diagnosis, therapeutic outcomes, general usability, or deployment safety. Relic provides research infrastructure intended to make relational memory, safety constraints, and agent behavior inspectable and testable.

papers.title: MetricPose: Flexible 3D Human Pose Estimation with Depth and Geometric Cues
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a 3D human pose estimator that predicts metrically accurate human joint positions in the camera coordinate frame. This task requires recovering the configuration of the body joints, scale, and metric camera-local placement. In monocular images, body size and camera distance are coupled through perspective projection and therefore cannot be determined uniquely from image alone. This ambiguity can be reduced by combining three complementary sources of information: learned RGB priors, direct depth measurements, and geometric constraints (e.g., ground contact) from the environment. We extend a pretrained full-body estimator with optional metric depth and geometry-processing modules that improve camera-distance estimation and depth-guided body refinement while preserving RGB-only operation. The resulting unified model supports RGB, RGB-Ground, and RGB-D using shared learned parameters. Unlike pelvis-relative error, camera-local error also measures placement relative to the camera. Compared with the existing foundation model SAM 3D Body, our methods with RGB, RGB-Ground, and RGB-D modes reduce camera-local joint-position error by 12.16%, 31.00% and 54.61% respectively.

papers.title: Does Reasoning Improve Psychological Depth in Large Language Models?
papers.abstract: Benchmark gains from reasoning-enhanced large language models encourage the assumption that these models should broadly perform better on complex generative tasks, but this remains underexplored in open-ended, creative domains shaped by nuances of reader experience. We tested this assumption through the lens of psychological depth in short stories. We compared DeepSeek-R1 vs. DeepSeek-V3, our closest available contrast for reasoning-oriented post-training, and GPT-5 vs. GPT-4o, through 60 blinded pairwise evaluations in which seven human annotators and an ensemble LLM-as-a-Judge rated prompt-matched story outputs. Human evaluations showed no universal reasoning advantage: GPT-5 was slightly preferred over GPT-4o (60.0-62.9% across two reasoning-effort settings), whereas DeepSeek-R1 fell behind DeepSeek-V3 (42.9%). Although this pattern was marked by low inter-annotator agreement (Krippendorff's $\alpha = 0.070$), our annotation-quality checks suggested genuine evaluative subjectivity, plausibly reflecting distinct annotator decision schemes rather than annotation failure. In contrast, the LLM-as-a-Judge showed a strong pro-reasoning bias (98.3% of pairs vs. 55.2% of human votes), consistent across its five configurations and partly tracking sentence length. These findings suggest that, at the frontier, reasoning-related quality differences are small enough to be dominated by reader subjectivity, and that LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators can obscure this subjectivity in nuanced creative-generation tasks.

papers.title: Semantic Extraction Framework for Goal-Oriented V2X Communication Supporting Safe Intersection Passage
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a transmitter-side semantic extraction framework for goal-oriented Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communication supporting safe intersection passage. Instead of transmitting raw sensory data, roadside infrastructure extracts task-relevant semantic information from video and traffic-signal sequences and organizes them into compact semantic packets for low-latency driving-decision assistance. The intersection-passing problem is formulated as a set of traffic tasks under Japanese traffic regulations, and the proposed pipeline generates perception and intent semantics through object detection, object tracking, region-of-interest (ROI)-based semantic extraction, and recommended-action generation. The framework is implemented and evaluated on a self-constructed, CARLA-based single-vehicle dataset collected under clear weather conditions. Experimental results show high recommended-action accuracy within the tested task set, while the mean processing latency remains below the frame interval of the 15~fps input video.

papers.title: Higher Holonomy for Higher Lie Algebroid Connections on Graded Vector Bundles
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a Riemann--Hilbert $A_\infty$-functor from the curved dg-category of $\mathscr{A}$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\mathscr{A}$ is a higher Lie algebroid, to the curved dg-category of $\Pi_\infty(\mathscr{A})$-connections on graded vector bundles, where $\Pi_\infty(\mathscr{A})$ is the homotopy groupoid of $\mathscr{A}$. When restricted to the sub dg-categories of flat objects, it induces an $A_\infty$-functor from the dg-category of representations up to homotopy of $\mathscr{A}$ to the dg-category of representations up to homotopy of $\Pi_\infty(\mathscr{A})$, which recovers the one from arXiv:1011.4693 and arXiv:0908.2843 when $\mathscr{A}$ is a Lie algebroid. The key ingredient for defining such functors is a non-abelian Stokes's theorem for endomorphism-valued differential forms. Furthermore, for a graded vector bundle $E$, we introduce the notion of its higher general linear groupoid in such a way that $G$-connections on $E$, for a higher Lie groupoid $G$, become smooth functors from $G$ to the higher general linear groupoid of $E$. We combine this with the Riemann--Hilbert functor to define higher parallel transport functors for $\mathscr{A}$-connections. Finally, we use these functors to define the higher holonomy groups of $\mathscr{A}$-connections and endow them with the structure of augmented simplicial Lie groups.

papers.title: A Generalized Bayesian Approach to Clustering with Dimension Reduction
papers.abstract: Generalized Bayes product partition models provide a probabilistic counterpart to loss-based clustering. They update a prior over partitions through an exponentiated clustering loss rather than a likelihood, so allocation uncertainty can be quantified without a full generative model for the data. However, their performance depends on the space in which the loss is evaluated. For high-dimensional observations, a squared Euclidean loss on the raw features can be dominated by irrelevant coordinates or fail to reflect cluster structure lying near a nonlinear low-dimensional manifold. We propose an extension in which an autoencoder and the partition are learned together, so that the space in which the clustering loss is evaluated is shaped by the clustering itself. Our generalized posterior combines a reconstruction loss, which keeps the low-dimensional representation faithful to the observed data, with a within-cluster sum of squares in the latent representation, which encourages cluster separation. Posterior computation alternates between Gibbs sampling over partitions and gradient-based updates of the autoencoder network, with the learning rate estimated jointly. We illustrate the approach through simulation studies and applications to four benchmark datasets.

papers.title: A sharp weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for partial derivatives on the unit ball
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp constant in the weighted $L^2$ Bernstein inequality for coordinate derivatives on the unit ball with a Jacobi weight and the strengthened derivative factors introduced by Beberok and Xu. The constant is expressed in terms of the largest zeros of Jacobi polynomials, and all extremal polynomials are characterized explicitly. The proof uses an orthogonal polynomial decomposition that gives diagonal formulas for both the squared norm and the weighted derivative integral. We also obtain two-sided bounds for the sharp constant and determine its leading asymptotic behavior as the polynomial degree tends to infinity.

papers.title: Sanctions, Evasion, and Deterrence: Evidence from Speeding Enforcement
papers.abstract: The design of sanctions plays a central role in shaping reoffending behavior. We study the effects of fixed monetary fines and accumulating penalty points on speeding recidivism and liability transfer. Exploiting a large increase in sanctions in Queensland, Australia, we estimate the causal effects of these sanctions on subsequent offending and nomination of other drivers. Higher demerit points increase fine renomination, consistent with strategic blame shifting. Estimated reductions in reoffending are small among offenders facing higher fines alone. Reoffending falls by a substantial 4.6 percentage points when higher fines are accompanied by additional penalty points.

papers.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
papers.abstract:
Dallard, Milani\v{c}, and \v{S}torgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor.
  We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Benchmarking of Unified Multimodal Models for Shallow-Water UAV Image Distortion Assessment and Restoration
papers.abstract: Shallow-water UAV imagery provides centimeter-scale observations of benthic environments, but water-induced distortions complicate interpretation. To our knowledge, we present the first systematic zero-shot benchmark of unified multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for both assessing water-induced distortions and restoring shallow-water imagery within the same model framework. We evaluate five open-weight unified MLLMs with frozen pretrained weights and without access to paired reference images or descriptions of the true seabed. The benchmark contains 1,000 image pairs: 600 semi-synthetic UAV scenes created by applying synthetic water distortions to real shallow-water imagery and 400 fully synthetic through-water scenes. Three independent human annotations cover five distortion types. We evaluate four assessment prompts (P0-P3), from direct instruction to structured task decomposition, on all 1,000 images and four diagnosis-guided restoration prompts (R0-R3) on a common 100-image subset. Assessment varies substantially by model and prompt, with systematic prediction biases and a best pooled balanced accuracy of 0.654 for distortion presence. The best pooled PSNR gain is +0.255 dB, no unified MLLM improves pooled LPIPS, and some outputs alter scene structure or hallucinate content. Two restoration-only baselines also show limited transfer: InstructIR achieves a pooled PSNR gain of +0.040 dB, while PromptFix degrades all four pooled metrics under every prompt. These results show that recognizing shallow-water degradation does not imply reliable physical restoration and provide a reproducible baseline for future work.

papers.title: Unraveling square and kagome lattice frustrated magnetism by scalable tensor networks
papers.abstract: We extend the scalability of variational infinite two-dimensional tensor network methods with application to investigate frustrated magnetism of the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model and kagome-lattice Heisenberg model. In the sign-problem-free limit of the square-lattice model, we achieve high ground-state energy precision comparable to quantum Monte Carlo methods. With no obstruction beyond this limit, our method obtains direct estimates of order parameters. For the square-lattice $J_1$-$J_2$ model, we determine isotropic plaquette order in the valence-bond solid region. For the model near $J_2/J_1=0.5$, and the kagome lattice Heisenberg model, our data indicate linear-dispersion gapless states. To probe the candidate spin-liquid nature of the highly frustrated cases, we go beyond inferring the absence of symmetry-breaking orders and analyze susceptibilities that characterize gapless spin liquids. By estimating scaling dimensions, our data indicate a stable gapless spin liquid on the kagome lattice, and competing scenarios for the intermediate regime of the square-lattice model. Our developments include parallelization and randomized low-rank methods and largely expand the frontier of high-precision variational numerics for quantum phases of matter.

authors.name: Yuchi He
authors.institution: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Refer-CityFlow and M3Track: A Benchmark Dataset and Reference Framework for Language-Driven Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking
papers.abstract: Referring multi-object tracking enables users to specify targets through natural language, but existing Refer-MOT benchmarks primarily focus on single-camera settings. We formalize Referring Multi-Target Multi-Camera Tracking (Refer-MTMCT), where free-form queries specify identity-consistent trajectories to be recovered across a network of sequential, sparse-overlap cameras. We introduce Refer-CityFlow, a benchmark built on CityFlow's global cross-camera identity annotations and augmented with language queries requiring joint language grounding, cross-camera association, and spatio-temporal reasoning. Refer-CityFlow covers 96 videos from 40 roadside cameras with 660+ identity-consistent cross-camera trajectories, 4,362 trajectory-level descriptions, and 7,699 queries, including 1,699 real-user queries collected from 50 participants. Reference experiments on the four-camera Scenario 02 show that single-camera referring trackers reach 14.95-18.28 HOTA on real-user queries, while the evaluated cross-view method achieves about 0.05 HOTA in direct transfer. To establish reference performance, we provide M3Track, a modular multimodal reference framework in which a large language model (LLM)-based agent orchestrates interchangeable detection, tracking, and cross-camera association modules. M3Track reaches 44.10 HOTA and 65.40 IDF1 on the same real-user query set. The project repository is available at https://github.com/phuongnguyen194/Refer-CityFlow-and--M3Track.

papers.title: Local contraction of stochastic affine recursions of $\mathbb{R}^d$
papers.abstract: We consider affine stochastic recursions $X^x_{n+1}=A_{n+1}X^x_n+B_{n+1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $(B_n,A_n)$ are i.i.d. in $\operatorname{Aff}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ with strongly irreducible and proximal linear part. In the critical regime where the top Lyapunov exponent vanishes, we show that the recursion is locally contractive in every direction, yielding uniqueness, up to a positive multiplicative constant, of the $\mu$-invariant non-zero Radon measure. This extends to every dimension $d\geq 2$ a result of Babillot-Bougerol-\'Elie (1997) in dimension one. The proof is based on the study of the asymptotic behaviour of the "joint process" $(X^x_n,X^y_n)$, using geometric and measure-theoretic properties of the diagonal affine action. A key ingredient is an abstract criterion for the total dissipativity of semigroup actions, which we apply to this process.

papers.title: Vertically-coupled microring resonators for lithium niobate on insulator integrated photonics
papers.abstract: We propose and demonstrate lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) microring resonators that are verticallycoupled to index-matched silicon-rich silicon nitride (SiN x ) access waveguides as an alternative to conventional lateral coupling schemes for integrated photonics applications. The wafer-scalable fabrication process involves a planarization step exploiting a single-step and reproducible spin-coating of a SU-8 epoxy spacer layer which allows a controlled separation to be established between the resonator and its access waveguide. The resulting multimode and single-mode microring resonators exhibit, for their fundamental TE 0 mode, intrinsic quality factors of 4.0 x 10 5 and 3.4 x 10 5 , respectively.
