papers.title: Hierarchical Signal Temporal Logic Control of Continuous-Time Systems
papers.abstract: For linear continuous-time systems, we solve the signal temporal logic (STL) control problem by translating it from continuous to discrete time such that a solution to the discrete-time problem guarantees a solution to the original continuous-time one. We split control synthesis into three hierarchical tasks. First, we discretize the continuous-time STL formula into a discrete-time one by sampling the temporal behavior it specifies. We accordingly discretize the continuous-time system by constructing a discrete-time model such that the input-state trajectories of the continuous-time system can be characterized as piecewise polynomial interpolations of the input-state trajectories of the discrete-time model. Second, we exploit this characterization to formulate mixed-integer linear constraints on the discrete-time trajectories that allow for planning a trajectory whose piecewise polynomial interpolation satisfies the continuous-time STL formula. In fact, system discretization and trajectory planning are performed in such a manner that any feasible solution to these constraints gives a discrete-time trajectory that can be transformed into a continuous-time one guaranteed to satisfy the original STL formula. Third, we propose a step-by-step algorithm to construct the control input that realizes such continuous-time trajectory.

papers.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070. The bispectral maps show QPO-related ridge--hypotenuse structures broadly consistent with the model, with qualitatively opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. In particular, the biphase map provides a complementary diagnostic that reveals weak coupling structures that are difficult to identify from the bicoherence alone. We also compare the measured bispectral modulus with the predictions for isolated ridges and hypotenuses. These predictions broadly reproduce the observed frequency dependence, while localized deviations remain near the fundamental-QPO and second-harmonic frequencies, where different bispectral structures overlap. Our results provide a simple mathematical framework in which the web-like pattern in the bispectrum could arise naturally from multiplicative coupling between a QPO-phase-locked modulator and the underlying variability.

papers.title: "I had nobody to turn to": Why LGBTQ+ People Choose (Not) to Use AI Chatbots for Personal Health and Relationship Advice
papers.abstract: While there is an abundance of research into large language model (LLM) biases against LGBTQ+ communities, far less research has examined how and why LGBTQ+ people choose to make use of AI chatbots. In this work, we examine how LGBTQ+ people choose (not) to use AI chatbots across three domains in which LGBTQ+ users have unique needs: relationship support, mental health support, and gender or sexual health support. We surveyed 73 people (60 LGBTQ+; 13 non-LGBTQ+) on how they interact with AI chatbots and find that participants' access to external resources, privacy concerns, and perceptions of chatbot capabilities shape whether and how they choose to make use of AI chatbots. For instance, some LGBTQ+ participants felt that chatbots might actually be less biased against LGBTQ+ people than the people they know offline. We also find that LGBTQ+ participants report using AI chatbots less frequently than non-LGBTQ+ participants across 15 specific personal health and relationship advice scenarios, citing concerns about AI sycophancy and adverse cognitive side-effects. Recognizing AI chatbots as vital (albeit imperfect) resources for LGBTQ+ people, we recommend researchers consider systemic issues that drive users to AI chatbots and design technologies (AI or otherwise) that prioritize privacy, anonymity, and real human connection.

papers.title: FlexRL: an R package for Flexible Record Linkage and Linked Data Quality Assessment
papers.abstract: FlexRL is an R package for probabilistic record linkage and inference on linked data. It provides a method to link observations from the same entities across two data sources that lack a unique identifier but share partially identifying variables. This method fits a hierarchical latent variable model of the data generation process, rather than classifying pairs of records from the comparison of their values, and accommodates registration errors and variables changing over time. Since linkage may affect subsequent analyses, the package also provides tools to assess the linked data quality as functions of the linkage decision rule. Two false discovery proportion estimators are implemented: a probabilistic approach contingent on the record linkage model and an augmented approach relying on an auxiliary estimation using synthetic data. Several measures of divergence of the linked sample from the source population are provided. These tools are agnostic to the underlying record linkage model and can be applied to any method. Together, they connect the output of the linkage to the validity of the subsequent analyses. The implementation combines standard R functions and S3 methods with Rcpp computations, resulting in fast execution times and a low memory footprint.

authors.name: Michel H. Hof

papers.title: A State-Variable Theory of Evolving Material Symmetry
papers.abstract: Material architecture can evolve during loading, yet its mechanically expressed symmetry depends on both the structural state and the constitutive coupling. We connect these quantities through one parent-invariant free energy with a symmetric traceless internal tensor $\mathbf Q$. Its stabilizer distinguishes isotropic, uniaxial, and biaxial states, and projected gradient kinetics satisfies the structural dissipation inequality. Parent invariance generally guarantees only symmetry inheritance. For an explicit two-coupling elastic potential, we derive a stiffness-contraction reconstruction of $\mathbf Q$ and prove equality of the structural and tangent rotational symmetries for every nonzero coupling pair. The associated acoustic tensor links residual symmetry to protected transverse degeneracies. For a small uniaxial state, the leading squared-speed gap is $|\gamma_2s|\sin^2\vartheta/(2\rho_0)$; coupling selectivity and residual protection can suppress this term. We also derive a directional acoustic-trace reconstruction and state calibrated and nuisance-aware inverse conditions. Dimensionless structural-field, acoustic, transient finite-element, and synthetic inverse examples illustrate the predictions. The framework connects state evolution, mechanically expressed symmetry, and conditional observability without assigning independent dynamics to a group label.

papers.title: Data-driven representation of continuous-time linear time-invariant behaviors via Hankel integral operators
papers.abstract: We present a data-driven representation of the finite-horizon behavior of deterministic controllable continuous-time LTI systems. We first introduce a notion of persistency of excitation for continuous-time signals that does not require the signal to be differentiable. We then show that, when the input is persistently exciting in this sense, the closure of the range of a Hankel integral operator built from a single input-output trajectory equals the behavior of the system over a finite time horizon. This result provides a nonparametric representation of system trajectories directly in terms of measured data, without requiring an explicit parametric model of the system.

papers.title: TurtLES: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Turbulent 3D Neural PDE Surrogates
papers.abstract: Machine-learning surrogates are increasingly used to accelerate computational fluid dynamics, yet progress is limited by the lack of benchmarks capturing realistic, time-dependent turbulent flows. We introduce TurtLES, a 14 TB dataset of 3D turbulent cylinder wakes in the shear-layer transition regime, computed via high-fidelity implicit large-eddy simulations. The dataset contains 400 trajectories of 400 time steps each, with 3-11 million points per frame, spanning variations in geometry, Reynolds number, and angle of attack. Unlike existing datasets, TurtLES combines (i) physically realistic turbulence with an active energy cascade driven by vortex stretching, (ii) dense irregular meshes, and (iii) long-horizon temporal dynamics. We benchmark state-of-the-art neural operators on autoregressive rollouts and identify key failure modes, including temporal instability, loss of small-scale energy, and challenges in learning on large irregular domains. TurtLES provides a new benchmark for evaluating surrogate models on 3D turbulent wakes at industrially relevant mesh resolution.

papers.title: CO gaps in cold transition disks around low-mass stars
papers.abstract: Transition disks with large inner dust cavities are promising targets to study planet formation, as these disks are likely hosting massive planetary companions. The structure of gas and dust inside the cavity are crucial for understanding the potential of planet formation in the regions. We investigate the structure of gas and dust in a sample of three cold, inclined transition disks around K and M stars without evidence for an inner dusty disk. We present new high-resolution ALMA Band 6 data of both 230 GHz continuum at 0.02" (~3 au) resolution and the 12CO 2-1, 13CO 2-1, C18O 2-1 isotopologues at 0.12" (~20 au) resolution. We analyze the radial profiles, compute the brightness temperatures, and derive estimates of the gas and dust content of the inner disk at 1 au. All three disks show dust cavities of 30-40 au in radius. The CO emission extends inside the cavity with progressively smaller CO cavity radii for the more abundant isotopologues. The 13CO brightness temperature profile is similar to that of other transition disks and full disks. No inner dust disk is detected in the ALMA continuum, consistent with the lack of near-infrared excess. Considering the accretion rates, the gas-to-dust ratio in the inner disk at 1 au is estimated to be as high as 10^5. No significant differences in the brightness temperature or in the gas-to-dust ratio are found between our disks and other transition disks around more luminous stars, contrary to expectations. This highlights the importance of individual-target studies through thermochemical modeling or multi-transition analyses to constrain the dust and gas structures in the cavity. The observed disk structures could be explained by super-Jovian companion on eccentric orbits, but further modeling is needed to confirm this conclusion.

papers.title: From Geometry to Function: A Multi-Task LiDAR Benchmark Dataset for Semantic and Functional Parsing of Urban Facades
papers.abstract: Understanding building facades is central to urban digital twins, heritage modelling, and sustainable city analysis, yet existing LiDAR benchmarks stop at geometry and semantic segmentation and offer little support for reasoning about the functional role of each architectural element. We introduce HFX3D, a large-scale urban facade benchmark of approximately 492 million LiDAR points from 26 buildings in Halifax, Canada, captured across four seasons, day and night, and varied weather. Each facade is annotated at three tiers, semantic, instance, and per-instance functional attributes, making it, to our knowledge, the first facade dataset to pair geometry and semantics with functional labels. Annotations are produced by a semi-automatic pipeline that combines geometry-guided heuristics with expert validation. We benchmark representative point-based, graph-based, convolutional, and transformer architectures and find that semantic segmentation is already challenging under severe class imbalance, while instance separation of repetitive structures and functional reasoning from geometry are substantially harder. The benchmark establishes a new foundation for function-aware 3D urban understanding. Project page: https://jijup.github.io/hfx3d-benchmark/ ; code: https://github.com/jijup/hfx3d-benchmark

papers.title: The existence of small defining polynomials for number fields, II
papers.abstract:
We prove that every number field of odd degree $n\geq 3$ and absolute discriminant $D$ has an integral defining polynomial whose coefficients are $O_n(D^{(n-1)/(2n-1)})$ in size. This strengthens, in odd-degree cases, the recently established bound of $O_n(D^{1/2})$ for all degrees $n$, which was conjectured in 1998 by Ruppert and is now known to be optimal in even degrees. More generally, we prove that this strengthened bound holds for all degree-$n$ fields having a real embedding and no subfield of index two. The proof makes use of the lattice shapes of the ring of integers and its trace dual, the inverse different.
  Assuming the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Dedekind zeta functions, as recently announced by Cureton and Thorner, we obtain an exponent smaller than $1/2$ for every field with no index-two subfield, of any signature. In the case of primitive fields, we obtain the exponent $(n-1)/(2n)$. In particular, we prove that the optimal exponent for cubic fields is $1/3$.

papers.title: Domain-Adapted Deep Optical Flow for Multiphase Velocimetry in Unsteady Cloud Cavitation
papers.abstract: Time-resolved velocimetry inside cloud cavitation remains a fundamental measurement problem. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) requires uniform tracer seeding and undistorted particle images, and cavitating flow violates both, because tracers do not penetrate vapor structures and refractive index mismatch across deforming interfaces produces spurious vectors. We present a domain-adapted deep optical flow framework for two-phase velocimetry, built on a Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms (RAFT) architecture fine-tuned on synthetic image pairs rendered from multiphase OpenFOAM simulations (RAFT-CloudCav). It is evaluated against a pre-trained generalist RAFT model, Farneb\"ack and OpenPIV on 130,000 frames/s recordings of a Venturi test section at 30 and 48 L/min. As no experimental ground truth exists, validation uses three quantities that require none, namely the integrated flow rate against a turbine meter, the liquid-phase velocity divergence, which mass conservation requires to vanish, and the station-to-station spread of the flow rate. RAFT-CloudCav recovers 47.75 L/min against a metered 48.0 $\pm$ 0.5 L/min, the closest of the four methods, and its flow rate varies by 2.0% across four streamwise stations, versus 6-7% for the classical methods. It returns a coherent near-wall reverse flow of -0.71 m/s, the time-averaged signature of the upstream-propagating re-entrant jet, where OpenPIV returns none. In the non-cavitating control, at 51 $\mu$m/pixel only three grid points fall inside a 0.68 mm boundary layer and the peak wall-normal gradient is under-predicted more than thirtyfold, while 13 and 19 $\mu$m/pixel agree with each other. The mean field is recovered without tracer particles at roughly three times the per-frame uncertainty. Uncertainties are estimated a posteriori from the image residual and propagated conservatively.

papers.title: Region-aware error triage for medical image segmentation with groupwise conformal risk control
papers.abstract: Segmentation masks are increasingly reviewed rather than redrawn, which requires knowing where a mask is likely wrong. Learned error maps rank pixels by risk, but the number of pixels to warn is chosen ad hoc, and calibrating one warning threshold over all error pixels may leave errors far from the predicted contour under-flagged. We propose RACE-Triage, a post-hoc error triage framework that leaves the segmentation mask unchanged. A risk network is trained on out-of-fold predictions from backbone-independent inputs. The predicted contour partitions each image into a boundary band and a non-boundary region, and conformal risk control is applied separately in each region to bound the expected fraction of missed errors among cases with errors there. On ISIC 2018 dermoscopy and BUSI breast ultrasound (where patient identifiers are unavailable, so independence across images is assumed), pooled control met its overall target but missed on average 31.8% and 36.4% of non-boundary errors. Regional control reduced these fractions to 19.3% and 20.9% and raised the recall of size-filtered false-negative components from 0.722 to 0.818 and from 0.611 to 0.763. The mean warned area grew by 1.6 and 4.9 percentage points, and its 95th percentile reached 23.5% and 38.5%. The effect held across three seeds and a second backbone, and area-matched heuristics did not reproduce it. On the external PH$^2$ set, frozen thresholds exceeded both targets, whereas recalibration with 100 local images brought the mean over repeated splits below them. Regional calibration improves non-boundary error coverage at a measured increase in warned area.

papers.title: Composite witness sieves, Kneser--Plancherel containers, and the exponent $5/7$ for the Erd\H{o}s--Straus conjecture
papers.abstract:
For the Erd\H{o}s--Straus equation $4/n=1/x+1/y+1/z$, Vaughan's unconditional bound on the exceptional set $E(N)$ has stood at $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c(\log N)^{2/3})$ since 1970. We harness composite divisor witnesses at growing depth to cross this $2/3$ barrier unconditionally. On the full exceptional set $E(N)$, we prove the unconditional bound $|E(N)|\ll N\exp(-c'(\log N)^{5/7}/(\log\log N)^{2/7})$, improving the exponent to $5/7$ (with an intermediate stage at $7/10$). On the structured component $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))$, an algebraic and spectral container hierarchy combined with a generating-polynomial large sieve reaches the exponent $1-o(1)$: $|E_2^{\mathrm{small}}(N;J(N))|\ll_\kappa N\exp(-(\frac{1}{40960}+o(1))\frac{\log N}{(\log\log N)(\log\log\log N)^{\kappa}})$, matching the CRT capacity scale.
  These results resolve the obstructions to composite-witness sieving at growing depth. First, we replace subgroup generation by Kneser's stabilizer $K(M)$, which embeds into a $2$-primary character kernel, reducing container counts from $2^{\Theta(J^{4})}$ to $\exp(\mathcal{O}(J^{2}\log\log J))$. Coupling this with a generating-polynomial large sieve, Markov $1/2$-popular symmetry containers, and Pontryagin--Plancherel character containers yields the exponent $1-o(1)$ on $E_2^{\mathrm{small}}$. Second, to bypass unlocalized diffuse divisor sheets without subset enumeration, we construct a semi-composite congruence sieve $s=pq\equiv-1\pmod{12ua}$ ($p\in(Z^{9/10},Z]$, $q\le Q$ rough). Conditioning on $n\bmod M_{\mathrm{small}}$ yields CRT mutual independence while decoupling the modulus $12ua\le 12Z^{1/4}$ from $q$; a Bonferroni majorant and the Bombieri--Vinogradov theorem then yield the unconditional $5/7$ exponent on all of $E(N)$. Finally, we study bilinear dispersion on $4uavw-4u^{2}v-w=n$ and difference sets $D(K_c)$.

papers.title: Maximizing Reaction via Spatial Localization: The Reaction-Flux Landscape and Maximizing Sequences
papers.abstract: We continue our study of a PDE-constrained variational model for maximizing the total reaction flux by optimizing the spatial distribution of catalytic materials, such as enzymes. The total amount of enzyme is fixed, and the substrate concentration is governed by a reaction-diffusion equation with prescribed boundary values. We consider both linear and nonlinear Michaelis-Menten reaction kinetics. In previous work, we constructed a maximizing sequence, computed the first and second variations of the reaction functional, and established the nonexistence of local maximizers. Here, we conduct a more comprehensive analysis. We prove that the functional is strictly concave for linear kinetics but need not be concave or convex for nonlinear kinetics. We also show that no critical points exist. We then characterize maximizing sequences and identify all their possible limiting measures. Our analysis reveals the mechanism of reaction maximization through spatial localization: maximizing sequences concentrate enzymes near the portion of the boundary where the substrate concentration is largest. Moreover, the landscape of the functional defining the total reaction differs between the linear and nonlinear cases, a point less emphasized in applications. Consistent with existing biophysical studies, these findings motivate the development and analysis of regularized models.

papers.title: Rhythmic Fitness Beat 'Em All using Real-Time Monocular Human Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Short and frequent physical activity exercices mitigate the health risks of sedentary behavior. Yet, the lack of motivation remains a critical barrier to adoption. Exergames gamify physical activity, but most rely on dedicated hardware, and outside dance and rhythm games they rarely use the musical beat. We present a work-in-progress beat 'em up exergame played with the whole body in front of a single smartphone, which runs the entire pipeline: an off-the-shelf real-time 3D human mesh recovery model on the phone's neural processing unit, gesture recognition, and the game, shown on any TV through a USB-C to HDMI cable. Our contributions are (1) a 3D recognition of five shadow-boxing moves (guard, punch, slip, squat, jump), each defined by one metric measure in a body frame aligned with gravity and one threshold with hysteresis, personalised during a tutorial; (2) a rhythm stage whose discrete cues are placed on the song's kick drum and judged on the movement's capture time, with a delay learned for each player; and (3) a phone-only architecture, running at 30 frames per second, that turns a phone and an HDMI cable into an exergame console.

papers.title: AUTEUR: Acoustic Plan Learning for Red-Teaming Text-to-Audio Models
papers.abstract: Automated red-teaming of text-to-audio models requires test prompts that pass textual screening and expose harmful acoustic content. The central challenge is to connect the sounds produced by the target model to both reusable test generation and prompt revision. Our key idea is to represent test descriptions as structured acoustic plans that organize foreground sounds, context, and vocal attributes. To this end, we propose acoustic plan learning, a framework that learns and refines these plans using waveform feedback. We train the plan generator through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with audio feedback while keeping the target audio model fixed. At inference time, the same trained model generates initial plans and uses feedback to revise their context and vocal attributes while preserving the foreground. Experiments across four target systems show attack success rates of 79.4% on TangoFlux and 95.6% on Kling. The resulting test prompts also transfer across open-source and closed-source models, indicating shared acoustic vulnerabilities.

authors.name: Zhiyuan Zha
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Yi Yu
authors.institution: Laboratoire de Physique des 2 Infinis Irène Joliot-Curie

papers.title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.

authors.name: Yipeng Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: Optimal Contention Resolution from Samples
papers.abstract:
Contention resolution schemes convert random sets which are ex-ante feasible for some constraint into sets which are feasible ex post, and their online variants have broad applications in Bayesian and stochastic optimization, including prophet inequalities and stochastic probing. In many such applications, however, full distributional knowledge is an unattainable requirement. This motivates the study of contention resolution schemes which employ a limited number of samples from the underlying distributions.
  We study sample-based contention resolution for $k$-uniform matroids, for both uniformly random and adversarial arrival orders, and compare their balance guarantees to the best possible with full distributional knowledge. For a single-item constraint, we show that one sample per element suffices for an optimal $(1-1/e)$-balanced ROCRS. For adversarial arrivals, however, we prove that no single-sample OCRS can be $1/2$-balanced, even for known arrival orders, separating contention resolution from prophet inequalities in the single-sample setting. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that two samples are necessary and sufficient for the optimal $1/2$ guarantee. We also present a single-sample $0.48$-balanced scheme.
  For general $k$, we give a simple single-sample ROCRS that achieves an optimal balance ratio of $1-e^{-k}k^k/k!$. In adversarial order, we obtain a single-sample $(1 - O(1/\sqrt{k}))$-balanced scheme, matching the optimal asymptotic dependence on $k$.
  Finally, we complete the picture by characterizing the minimum number of samples needed to match the optimal balance ratio achievable with full distributional knowledge. For random arrivals, one sample suffices for $k = 1,2,3,4$, and zero samples suffice for $k \geq 5$. For an adversarial arrival order, even known in advance, and any $k \geq 2$, we show that no constant number of samples suffices to achieve optimal balance.

authors.name: Vasilis Livanos
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
papers.abstract: First proposed by Milgrom in 1983 as an alternative to the standard Cold Dark Matter (CDM) paradigm, Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) has gained renewed momentum in light of persistent non-detections of exotic dark matter particles and growing tensions facing CDM on galactic scales. While MOND perfectly reproduces galactic rotation curves, it encounters notable challenges in explaining the equilibrium of galaxy clusters. Although it reduces the overall dark matter budget in these massive systems, an unidentified mass component remains required. This paper investigates the hypothesis that this missing mass is baryonic: composed of non-radiating ordinary matter such as stellar remnants, gas too diffuse to initiate star formation, or compact, ultra-dense clouds of cold molecular gas with low volume filling factors. Using a sample of 106 clusters mapped in X-rays, emitted by the hot intra-cluster medium (ICM) composing most of the visible mass, we derive first the total mass within the Newtonian dynamics, assuming hydrostatic equilibrium and spherical symmetry. Then, with the modified Poisson equation, we reconstruct the spatial distribution of the invisible missing matter within the MOND framework. In the sample, the relaxed systems harboring cooling flows, known as cool-core clusters, have the highest peaks of dark missing mass. Its density profile reveals a pronounced central concentration bounded by a steep truncation immediately beyond a core radius of 20-30 kpc, confirming previous studies. MOND reduces the necessary dynamical mass by a factor of 4 to 10. The residual missing mass is proportional to the total gas mass, being roughly twice lower.

authors.name: Francoise Combes
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Learning from How Users Interpret: Personalizing Recommendation Explanation Order
papers.abstract: Personalized explanations typically adapt their content or presentation based on preferences, interaction histories, or other user characteristics. We examine whether regularities inferred from prior textual interpretations can support personalization of explanation organization. In a controlled within participant study with 122 participants, prior interpretations were represented along three dimensions: information selection, relative salience, and relational organization. The relational dimension was partially operationalized through co mobilization. These representations were aggregated into fixed historical profiles and used to organize otherwise identical explanation sentences. Participants encountered four organization procedures: the OWN historical profile, the DONOR historical profile, a population profile called POP, and a language model procedure using the historical profile called PROFILE LLM. Post exposure objective comprehension was the primary outcome. OWN achieved 86.5 percent correct responses, compared with 66.0 percent for DONOR, 63.9 percent for POP, and 73.0 percent for PROFILE LLM. Mixed effects analyses showed higher comprehension with OWN than with each alternative procedure. No reliable overall condition effect was detected for recommendation acceptance. These findings indicate that historical profiles derived from prior interpretations can provide an actionable signal for personalizing explanation order while keeping explanatory content and wording fixed.

authors.name: Deo Munduku
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Elsa Negre
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: An improved isodiametric inequality for convex surfaces
papers.abstract: Alexandrov conjectured that every closed convex surface of area $A$ and intrinsic diameter $D$ satisfies $A/D^2\leq\pi/2$. Using an averaging argument over the curvature measure, we prove that every closed convex surface satisfies $A/D^2\leq2\pi/3$, improving the best previously known bound.

authors.name: Matej Stehlik
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Global Solar Siting from Geospatial Embeddings
papers.abstract: Global solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity is rapidly growing, helping decrease our emissions and dependence on fossil fuels. However, optimally siting a solar plant remains challenging, requiring anticipation of geographical, urban, and infrastructure needs. Current methods rely on multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA) using hand-picked geophysical layers and solar-resource products, however these strategies are not geographically transferable and do not capture the practical requirements of solar sites. We use geospatial embeddings, dense vectors representing geophysical properties of a location, to analyse 38,591 existing solar sites and the land they were built on to learn the latent solar suitability signal. We assess a set of linear and non-linear models and select a soft-voting ensemble of a random forest and a multilayer perceptron (RF+MLP ensemble), chosen for accuracy and large scale deployability. Validated against future installations in thirteen countries, the ensemble separates existing solar sites from random land with a median ROC-AUC of 0.90. Compared with published MCDA strategies, the ensemble increases ROC-AUC by 0.06-0.30 in every country. The ranking also concentrates real deployment: the most-suitable 20% of land holds 84% of estimated generation (annual energy yield) and 67% of installed capacity (potential power output). After applying standard siting constraints, 5.6% of global land (9.8% if cropland is permitted) remains highly suited to solar. The global 10 m resolution solar suitability dataset and code can be found here: https://github.com/Abdullahr29/Global-Solar-Siting.

authors.name: Quentin Paletta
authors.institution: Organisation de Coopération et de Développement Economiques

papers.title: Jaeger conjecture and Jaeger-Zhang conjecture
papers.abstract:
We prove that every signed planar graph $\widehat G$ of negative girth at least $\ell\geq 3$ satisfies $\chi_c(\widehat G)<\frac{2\ell}{\ell-2}$. As a consequence, for every integer $k\geq 1$, every planar graph $G$ of odd girth at least $4k+3$ satisfies $\chi_c(G)<\frac{2k+1}{k}$ and hence admits a homomorphism to $C_{2k+1}$.
  Our proofs build on recent results of Jafari on circular flows. In particular, Jafari proved that every $(4k+2)$-edge-connected graph has circular flow number strictly less than $2+\frac{1}{k}$. We revisit his theorem, providing an alternative proof that emphasizes the underlying graph-theoretic ideas. We also extend the result to signed graphs and weaken the connectivity assumption by imposing a lower bound only on the size of negative cuts.
  The key step is a small-correction lemma associated with a distribution on spanning trees. A splitting argument first gives the required correction in an even-degree graph; doubling the edges removes the degree-parity assumption. Plane duality then gives the coloring theorem. We discuss tightness of bounds in the end.

authors.name: Reza Naserasr
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Robust Readout of Cross-Point Resistive Arrays via Time-Domain Optimization
papers.abstract: Cross-point resistive arrays are attractive for high-density tactile sensing because they reduce wiring complexity. However, conventional frequency-based readout methods can become inaccurate in robotic sensing environments, where long interconnects and measurement and environmental noise degrade the observed signals. We propose a time-domain optimization method for robust readout of cross-point resistive arrays. The method determines resistance values by fitting a time-domain observation model to the measured waveform over the interval, rather than relying solely on spectral amplitudes. By exploiting the full waveform, the proposed method improves robustness under noisy observation conditions. In simulations of a 16 x 16 array, the proposed method reduced the mean readout error by 20% compared with the baseline method. Furthermore, validation over 1,000 trials showed that the proposed method achieves more robust estimation than the conventional method, reducing the mean error and standard deviation by 24.6% and 77.6%, respectively. The improvement was also confirmed in cross-point array simulations with resistance distributions emulating tactile sensor responses.

authors.name: Hiroshi Kaminaga
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Elastic Wave Imaging via Kirchhoff Migration: Resolution Analysis and Inclusion Identification
papers.abstract: We consider the inverse problem of determining the location, orientation, shape, and material parameters of a small elastic inclusion embedded in a homogeneous medium from full-aperture measurements of the scattered field. Using a small-volume expansion, we derive explicit leading-order expressions for four Kirchhoff migration imaging functionals, denoted by PP, PS, SP, and SS, corresponding to the four combinations of pressure (P) and shear (S) waves used for receiver- and source-side backpropagation. The resulting point-spread functions quantitatively characterize the resolution of each mode and show that the SS mode achieves the highest spatial resolution. For an elliptic inclusion, we show that the PP mode uniquely determines the elastic moment tensor (EMT) within the leading-order asymptotic model, thereby enabling the reconstruction of the material and geometric parameters of the inclusion. For a general small scatterer, the reconstruction may instead be interpreted as an effective elliptic representation determined by its leading-order EMT. For a disk, the parameter-identification problem is underdetermined; nevertheless, explicit upper and lower bounds on its volume are derived. We further analyze the model error arising from neglected cross-mode contributions when the distance from the center of the measurement configuration is not sufficiently large relative to the elastic wavelengths. Numerical experiments support the theoretical predictions and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed imaging and reconstruction methods.

authors.name: Zetao Fei
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Josselin Garnier
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Analyzing Code Provenance in LLMs for Programming Education
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) play an increasing role in programming education, challenging traditional assessment methods as they can generate fully functional code instantly. This disrupts the reliability of student submissions as indicators of learning and effort. To address this issue, code provenance is essential for tracing the origins of code and distinguishing student-authored, AI-generated, and externally sourced components. We extend the Min-K% probability approach by incorporating synthetic non-member code generation and apply it to Python code for membership inference and provenance tracking. Evaluations cover free LLMs such as GPT-2, DistilGPT-2, and DialoGPT, as well as state-of-the-art commercial models including GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, Mistral, DeepSeek, and LLaMA 3.3. Before evaluating our approach on higher-education student assignments, we validate its feasibility using Stack Overflow data. The results show that free models enable more sensitive code memorization detection than commercial models. By systematically comparing these LLMs, we assess trade-offs between detection accuracy and privacy protection, taking an initial step toward effective assessment of AI-assisted programming education through combined provenance detection and process visibility.

authors.name: Omar Boucelma
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: InstantHMR : Real-Time Human Mesh Recovery on Your Phone
papers.abstract: Real-time 3D human mesh recovery from a single image on mobile devices is a challenging problem with many applications, including robotics, biomechanics, AR/VR, and exergames. Current state-of-the-art models are either too slow to run efficiently on mobile devices or sacrifice accuracy for speed. We present InstantHMR, a family of open-source single-image regressors suited for mobile inference, based on the Momentum Human Rig (MHR) parametric model and trained exclusively on publicly available annotations from the SAM 3D Body dataset. Our approach achieves remarkable performance on a Samsung Galaxy S23 NPU, recovering a 6,890-vertex body mesh in 5.5 ms per person, and 0.98 ms on an NVIDIA RTX 4070 GPU. This speed surpasses all existing methods we evaluated. On mobile, it is 12x faster than the single mobile-compatible method that slightly outperforms ours in accuracy, while achieving competitive accuracy with 40.0 mm PA-MPJPE on 3DPW, 48.8 mm on EMDB and 41.7 mm on RICH. To ensure fair comparisons, we re-evaluate 11 state-of-the-art methods under a unified protocol aligned with the closest MHR-based competitors, including Meta's official MHR-to-SMPL conversion, and report their reproduction results. Additionally, we measure latency across eight different targets, ranging from desktop TensorRT to two phone NPUs. Code and models are available at https://github.com/Naturalpad-studio/InstantHMR.

authors.name: Kahina Chalabi
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Vincent Bonnet
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Integrating MBSE Principles with AI to Improve the Quality of Requirements in SMEs Context
papers.abstract: Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) is a promising approach to improve systems engineering practices, particularly by enhancing requirement management, traceability, and early validation and verification (V\&V). However, its adoption remains challenging, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), which often lack structured processes and solutions adapted to their scale and constraints. Our goal is to propose a lightweight MBSE methodology tailored to the needs and constraints of SMEs. This paper focuses specifically on requirements refinement, traceability, and early V\&V. The approach integrates MBSE principles with artificial intelligence-assisted analysis to improve requirements quality while remaining compatible with existing tools and practices. A proof of concept is developed and applied in an industrial case study to evaluate the feasibility of the approach. The results demonstrate how early V\&V activities can be supported within an SME context, while improving traceability across engineering artifacts. These findings highlight the potential of a lightweight, integrated MBSE approach to support the progressive adoption of MBSE in SMEs, thereby improving overall engineering efficiency.

authors.name: Claude Baron
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Jean-Michel Bruel
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: On the convergence of Lattice Boltzmann method for advection-diffusion equation with intermediate scaling
papers.abstract: The purpose of this article is to study the convergence of a lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) for a simple diffusion equation. The LBM is proven to be stable and consistent in some sense, so that convergence results may be obtained. The approach is similar to asymptotic analysis in the literature, although the schemes are also studied for intermediate time scalings. Usually, LBM are used in the range of acoustic regime, where $\delta$t ___ $\delta$x, or in diffusive scaling, with $\delta$t ___ $\delta$x 2 . In this work, we study any intermediate scaling $\delta$t ___ $\delta$x 1+r with r $\in$]0; 1]. The goal is to prove that this scaling is capable of approximating an advection-diffusion equation, provided the relaxation rate is chosen in accordance with $\delta$x. Convergence results are established and match the previously known results in the diffusive regime. The second objective is to prove that several choices for the initial condition are suitable for convergence. In particular, the usual choice of equilibrium distribution at initial time guarantees that the LBM scheme yields an accurate approximation of the macroscopic quantities.

authors.name: Francky Luddens
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A Compact High-Repetition-Rate Intense THz Source for Atomic-Scale Materials Characterization
papers.abstract: High-intensity terahertz (THz) sources combining high repetition rates, strong field amplitudes, and long-term stability are key enabling technologies for next-generation ultrafast photonics. However, simultaneously achieving these characteristics in a compact and practical architecture remains a major challenge. Here, we report a high-performance tabletop THz source delivering intense single-cycle pulses at 100 kHz, generated by optical rectification in lithium niobate using an optimized echelon-based tilted-pulse-front scheme and driven by an industrial-grade ytterbium laser. The source achieves optical-to-THz conversion efficiencies exceeding 0.13% at room temperature, peak electric fields of several hundred kV/cm, and excellent long-term stability, establishing a robust platform for high-average-power strong-field THz applications. As a proof of concept, the source was integrated into an atom probe tomography (APT) instrument. APT reconstructs the three-dimensional chemical composition of materials through field-induced ion emission from a sharp nanotip. While THz-assisted ion emission has been shown to improve analytical performance by reducing thermal effects, previous demonstrations were limited to low-repetition-rate THz sources, restricting throughput and accessible analysis volumes. Using an aluminum nanotip, we demonstrate efficient THz-assisted APT at 100 kHz and benchmark its performance against conventional voltage- and laser-assisted operation. The high repetition rate enables rapid large-volume acquisition while improving mass resolving power, reducing thermal tailing, and preserving high-quality three-dimensional reconstructions. Beyond APT, this work establishes a compact and scalable high-repetition-rate THz platform for strong-field physics, nonlinear THz photonics, ultrafast spectroscopy, and material characterization at the nanoscale.

authors.name: Ammar Hideur
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Natural potentials for TT tensors, divergence-free symmetric tensors and linearised relativistic initial data
papers.abstract: Let $N$ be a natural tensor which vanishes at a metric $g\_0$. By diffeomorphism invariance, $DN(g\_0)^*$ takes values in divergence-free symmetric $2$-tensors, and in TT tensors if moreover $DN(g\_0)$ kills conformal directions. Such operators are local potentials, which we call machines: they produce smooth compactly supported tensors with the required property and, on closed manifolds, all of them up to a finite-dimensional space when their symbol is injective. On Einstein manifolds of every dimension, the linearised Bach tensor gives the operator $P$ of an earlier paper, which factorises on TT tensors into the massless and partially massless spin-$2$ operators; we also construct machines on Bach-flat, conformally flat and Ricci-parallel metrics. Replacing the diffeomorphisms of $M$ by those of the vacuum development, we obtain potentials, with a Fredholm property, for the linearised Einstein constraint equations on arbitrary spacelike hypersurfaces of Minkowski, de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes.

authors.name: Erwann Delay
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Suppression of water-ice UV photodesorption on cosmic dust analogs
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) photodesorption regulates the partitioning of water between interstellar ice mantles and the gas phase, yet laboratory yields are generally measured on planar substrates rather than on surfaces representative of cosmic dust. We investigate how grain morphology affects UV photodesorption from thin H$_2$O ice films of 2-6 monolayers deposited on planar gold and olivine, soot nanoparticles, and olivine microparticles. Samples were irradiated at 12 and 60 K with a microwave-discharge hydrogen lamp, and ice depletion was monitored by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy and reflection-absorption infrared spectroscopy. On planar gold, the photodesorption yield increases approximately linearly with ice coverage, from $\sim5\times10^{-4}$ to $\sim2\times10^{-3}$ molecule photon$^{-1}$ between 2 and 6 monolayers, consistent with increasing UV absorption in optically thin ice; planar olivine gives comparable yields. In contrast, photodesorption is suppressed on particulate olivine and, more strongly, on soot, where yields are up to a factor of $\sim40$ lower than on gold at 12 K. Both experimental techniques confirm the strong suppression of ice depletion on soot. These results show that UV photodesorption depends not only on ice coverage but also strongly on grain morphology. The pronounced suppression on soot may reflect heterogeneous ice growth and altered energy redistribution within nanoscale ice domains, implying that yields measured on planar substrates may substantially overestimate photodesorption from the thin ice mantles of cosmic dust.

authors.name: C. Laffon
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Physics Informed Priors for Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials with Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: Standard uncertainty quantification methods for machine learning interatomic potentials often fail to quantify the effects of model misspecification despite its prominence as a source of error. To combat this, misspecification-aware uncertainty schemes have been gaining attention, pointwise optimal parameter set regression (POPS-Regression) among them. However, no guarantees on the physicality of the posterior distribution are given and uncertainty estimates can be conservative compared to the true error. To combat this, we present a model misspecification aware scheme that builds on POPS-Regression by allowing users to specify physical priors that are enforced across the obtained ensemble of models. This allows the user to incorporate misspecification-aware uncertainties without compromising on physical properties. The scheme is applicable to any physical quantity that can be represented by a convex set of parameters and so is robust for a wide variety of static properties which can help inform dynamical simulations. Here, we demonstrate the scheme for phononic vibrations and elastic properties. The scheme is also applied to both linear and message-passing neural network potentials by exploiting the linearity available in both architectures; for neural network potentials we approximate the readout layer as a linear model based on fixed non-linear features. The versatility of the method provides an alternative to hand-crafted or active learning approaches to data-set construction to correct physical failures by adding data thus reducing the computational overhead for designing potentials for specific applications.

authors.name: Thomas D. Swinburne
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Stable, High-Charge, Laser-Driven VHEE Beams for Preclinical Applications
papers.abstract: Laser-driven plasma accelerators (LPAs) are promising sources of very-high-energy-electron (VHEE) beams for medical applications, but increasing charge per pulse while maintaining pointing stability remains challenging. We demonstrate laser-accelerated beams with total charge per pulse reaching (559 $\pm$ 56) pC using an 80 TW laser system. The spectra have a dominant component at 40-60 MeV and a high-energy tail extending to approximately 200 MeV. Pointing jitter measured in air at the irradiation target plane reaches as low as 0.7 mrad. The beams were used for VHEE irradiation experiments involving a 10 mm region of interest through a 40 mm depth at 400 $\pm$ 20 mGy/pulse. Spectral reproducibility is quantified over fixed-setting shot sequences. Particle-in-cell simulations produce a peak-and-tail spectrum through acceleration in successive bubbles associated with a strongly modified plasma wake, providing a plausible mechanism for maintaining substantial accelerated charge despite strong beam loading. Dose-weighted time-of-flight calculations indicate an effective pulse dose rate of $10^{12}$ Gy/s and average dose rates of tens of Gy/min. These results establish an LPA operating regime relevant to preclinical VHEE irradiation.

papers.title: Isomorphic classification of the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups $\mathrm{SL}_2$
papers.abstract: We classify, up to isomorphism, the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups SL 2 .

authors.name: Thi Hoa Emilie Nguyen
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy
papers.abstract: In the classification context where revealing the label of a sample is costly, we propose a new Active Learning (AL) strategy named k-Volume (kVol). It randomly selects a sample to be labeled according to the volume of the smallest ball containing its k nearest neighbors. kVol is highly versatile: it can be applied either in the input space or in the output space, and it enjoys the desirable properties of the three main families of AL strategies: density, diversity, and (when performed in the output space) uncertainty. From a theoretical perspective, we establish that kVol is asymptotically equivalent to uniform sampling over the support of the (input or output) data distribution. Based on experiments on various synthetic and real-life tabular datasets and images, we observe that kVol is surprisingly stable: whatever the classifier or the experimental setup, it still lies among the best AL strategies unlike other competitors that fail dramatically. In particular, kVol outperforms state-of-the-art competitors such as CoreSet, TypiClust or Uncertainty on several real-life datasets, at a low computational cost.

papers.title: Symmetry Breaking over Multiway Channels
papers.abstract: Identical users running the same algorithm must often break their symmetry and agree on distinct roles, as in leader election, naming, and resource allocation. We study anonymous symmetry breaking over a discrete memoryless multiway channel invariant under permutations of its $J$ users: each user observes only a private output and must choose a number in $\{1,\dots,J\}$, and the symmetry is broken if the $J$ numbers are distinct. Using a R\'enyi change of measure, we derive a finite-blocklength converse on the error probability of every symmetric causal protocol, including adaptive and randomized ones. For achievability, block coding with random names reduces the problem to all-source multicast, for which we derive a Gallager random-coding exponent for every fixed $J$, and a cut-set bound that limits the exponent of the probability that two names coincide or are decoded wrongly. Interactive role controllers instead let the users contend for identifiers directly: we give their exact error probability, an achievable exponent given by a spectral radius when some outputs certify a role, and a floor for finite-state controllers when every output has positive probability, and we introduce generalized musical chairs. On a noisy bandit channel motivated by multiplayer multi-armed bandits, with noiseless collisions and arms of a common mean below one, interactive schemes provably exceed the limit of name decoding, and numerical estimates suggest the same with noisy collisions. For two users, noiseless collisions, one informative arm and a silent arm, the optimal error probability is determined up to a factor of two.

authors.name: Richard Combes
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Interface-driven second harmonic generation in indium tin oxide/gold nanolayers: density and mass discontinuities matter
papers.abstract: Second harmonic generation from transparent conductive oxides and metals is traditionally attributed to Coulomb, magnetic Lorentz, and convective sources. We show that this picture is incomplete in deeply subwavelength indium tin oxide/gold bilayers. Measurements reveal two robust spectral features, a broad maximum near 1000 nm and an epsilon-near-zero peak near 1350 nm, that persist across wide variations in material and excitation parameters. Hydrodynamic-Maxwell simulations identify an interface-specific convective mechanism activated by freeelectron density and effective-mass discontinuities at the oxide-metal boundary. As electronic homogenization develops across the bilayer, the response evolves toward one described by conventional Coulomb, Lorentz, and leading convective terms. These results establish second harmonic generation as a sensitive probe of interface-driven nonlinearities and suggest a broader role for electronic discontinuities in shaping nonlinear optical processes at surface and buried material interfaces.

authors.name: C. Cojocaru
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Stacking, symmetry and exciton fine structure in boron nitride bilayers
papers.abstract: Engineering of two-dimensional material heterostructures offers a broad range of degrees of freedom through the selection of type and number of layers and their relative stacking configurations. In these compound materials, the stacking sequence plays a central role in determining electronic, mechanical, and optical properties. Here, we present a theoretical study of its signature on the excitons of hexagonal boron nitride bilayers based on first-principle calculations within the GW approximation and the Bethe-Salpeter equation. We explain how stacking-dependent symmetry variations lead to distinct electronic structures, particularly near the band edge around the K high-symmetry point, and consequently to markedly different excitonic landscapes. Indeed, we analyze the symmetry-governed character of the low-lying excitonic states, identifying their bright or dark nature for each stacking configuration and performing a systematic comparison. Our results clarify how van der Waals interlayer coupling reshapes excitons in hexagonal boron nitride bilayers and outline prospects for twist-controlled exciton engineering in this material.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Lorenzo Sponza
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Coresets for Capacitated Clustering via Dual Concentration
papers.abstract:
We study coresets for clustering problems, focusing on the classical $k$-median and $k$-means objectives. A coreset is a small weighted summary of the input data that approximately preserves the clustering cost for every choice of centers. Such summaries are a central tool for scaling clustering algorithms to large datasets.
  In this work, we consider the capacitated setting, where the clustering is subject not only to choosing centers but also to respecting prescribed cluster-size constraints. This model is a natural generalization of standard clustering and has been widely studied, but its coreset complexity is less well understood. For finite metric spaces, we obtain optimal-size coresets; surprisingly, these match the best-known bounds for unconstrained clustering. We also give improved coreset bounds in Euclidean space, notably the first coresets with near-linear dependence in $k$ while being independent of the dimension and input size.
  The main new technical ingredients are concentration bounds for the dual solutions of min-cost flow problems, which allow for both significantly simpler and tighter analyses of the underlying sampling distribution used in the coreset construction.

papers.title: Know What You Need: Efficient Activation Checkpointing
papers.abstract: Large Language Model training is increasingly constrained by memory capacity. Activation Checkpointing reduces activation memory by avoiding storing selected activations during the forward pass and rematerializing them during backpropagation, thereby trading memory savings for additional computation. Although this technique is essential for scaling model training, rematerialization can be prohibitively expensive, particularly for Transformer linear layers. Approximate computation could reduce this overhead, but conventional approaches either introduce errors that accumulate over the backward pass or fail to exploit information available from the initial forward pass. We introduce a novel approximate rematerialization method that can yield unbiased gradient estimates: using information collected during the initial forward pass, the method selectively recomputes only the most important layer components, either through greedy selection or randomized sketching. Ablation studies show that the resulting gradients closely match the exact gradients. When applied to feed-forward layers, attention layers, or both, our method can recompute only two-thirds of the layer components in a Llama-488M model, while increasing perplexity by just 1.7%, 1.2%, and 2.5%, respectively.

authors.name: Danyal Ahmed
authors.institution: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland

authors.name: Edouard Oyallon
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: RainFlow: Flow Matching for Infrared-Only Quantitative Precipitation Estimation
papers.abstract: Geostationary infrared imagers observe precipitating systems every 10 to 15 minutes over large areas, but they sense cloud tops rather than the rain beneath. Their brightness temperatures constrain surface rain only weakly, so retrievals trained by regression return a smooth estimate that misses heavy rain and carries no measure of uncertainty. We treat infrared-only retrieval as conditional generation and introduce RainFlow, a flow-matching model that generates ensembles of rain fields from MSG/SEVIRI infrared observations, in a direct and a residual variant. Evaluated against radar over metropolitan France for a full year, the generated members are realistic rain fields, with the observed dry areas, heavy rain and spatial structure, and the ensemble mean is as accurate as a deterministic baseline. Used as probabilities, the ensembles locate heavy rain at scales where the baseline has no skill, and their spread captures most of the retrieval error, with only slight underdispersion. Trained with a time-sampling density that favours the noise end of the generative trajectory, the two variants reach similar skill. The direct variant depends strongly on this choice of density, whereas the residual variant is nearly insensitive to it. Evaluating the generated rain as a function of brightness temperature shows that the ensembles reproduce how rain depends on it over most of the range. It also isolates the remaining gap, an underestimate of both the amount and the variability of rain under the coldest cloud tops, which scores computed over all pixels do not reveal.

authors.name: Matthieu Meignin
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Cecile Mallet
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Nicolas Viltard
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: A Regular First-Order Calculus for the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao Geometry
papers.abstract: We introduce a notion of intrinsic differentiability for functionals on the space of finite nonnegative measures equipped with the Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao (WFR) distance, also known as the Hellinger--Kantorovich (HK) distance. The resulting static first-order calculus accounts simultaneously for spatial transport and mass reweighting. We characterize regular barycentric logarithms through optimal semicouplings and measurable selections at the transport threshold, and prove their tangency at arbitrary finite source measures. The defining expansion extends to non-optimal semicouplings, with remainder of smaller order than the square root of their cost. This yields differentiation formulas for simultaneous transport and reweighting and uniqueness of the gradients. We also give a sufficient criterion in terms of regular flat derivatives. We characterize differentiability of one half the squared WFR distance by a common optimal Monge transport--growth representation with no target mass created from the cone vertex. Equivalently, the regular barycentric logarithm is unique and its norm equals the distance; the gradient is minus this logarithm. Finally, we formulate the corresponding calculus on probability measures. On $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^d)$, WFR differentiability implies intrinsic Wasserstein differentiability, with the transport component of the WFR gradient coinciding with the Wasserstein gradient. Whenever a flat derivative exists, one quarter of the reaction component agrees almost everywhere with its centered representative. As a byproduct we obtain a Wasserstein differentiability result for the squared $\mathrm{WFR}$ distance.

authors.name: Enrico Sartor
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Percolation on grandparent graphs of Bienaym\'e trees
papers.abstract: We consider Bernoulli bond percolation on the grandparent graph of a Bienaym\'e tree, obtained by adding to the tree an edge between every vertex and its grandparent. We show that the critical parameter $p_c$ is the unique solution of an explicit equation involving the generating function of the offspring distribution, and we study how $p_c$ depends on this distribution beyond its mean $m$. When $m\geq 1.569$, the offspring distribution concentrated on the (one or two) integers closest to $m$ is the unique maximiser of $p_c$ among all offspring distributions with mean $m$, and its critical parameter is $\frac1{m^2}-\frac1{m^3}+O\left(\frac1{m^4}\right)$ as $m\to\infty$; more generally, for two distributions that are comparable in the convex order, $p_c$ is larger for the smaller of the two distributions under the condition that its support bounded some explicit $N(m)$ of order $m^4$. These restrictions cannot be removed: the convex order alone does not determine the order of the critical parameters, even among distributions with support bounded by $O(m^4)$, and the extremal property fails for $m$ close to $1$. Finally, for every $m>1$, the critical parameter $p_c$ can be arbitrarily close to $0$ for general offspring distributions with mean $m$. If we only consider offspring distributions that do not charge $0$, so that the obtained tree is almost surely infinite, this remains true if and only if $m\geq 2$.

authors.name: Laurent Menard
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Delphin Senizergues
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Assessing the Impact of Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Algorithmic Problem-Solving
papers.abstract: Competitive programming problems pose distinctive challenges for Large Language Models, as they demand not only proficient code generation but also advanced algorithmic reasoning. This study presents a Retrieval-Augmented Generation approach specifically designed to enhance the capacity of Large Language Models to address such problems. Our approach integrates an embedding-based retrieval mechanism and a similarity search algorithm to identify analogous problems within a knowledge database, employing a dynamically adjusted threshold to mitigate retrieval noise. We conducted an evaluation using the CodeContests dataset, focusing on the test split problems that exhibit similarity to instances from the training split. The experimental framework considered three conditions: (i) problems provided solely with their original descriptions, (ii) problems supplemented with randomly selected examples from the training split, and (iii) problems augmented with similar examples retrieved through the proposed method. In addition, we incorporated a Min-K membership inference analysis to examine whether the generated code solutions were influenced by potential memorization of training data within the evaluated Large Language Models. This complementary perspective enables a deeper understanding of model behavior by distinguishing genuine generalization through retrieval from implicit recall of pretraining samples. Performance was assessed using both pass rates and the CodeForces Elo rating of the problems. The results provide empirical evidence that similarity-based retrieval substantially enhances Large Language Models performance in competitive programming scenarios, offering an scalable framework for improving code generation in algorithmic problem-solving contexts.

authors.name: Jose Palazzo Moreira de Oliveira
authors.institution: Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Sul

papers.title: An Efficient Synchronization Scheme for Distributed Bandits
papers.abstract: We study the problem of synchronizing two players in a \emph{distributed multi-armed bandit} setting. The probability of \emph{synchronization error} is analyzed by recasting synchronization as a \emph{communication problem}. Using a well-designed random coding ensemble, we derive error exponents for the maximum-likelihood decoder. We then introduce a \emph{universal decoder} that achieves the same error exponents as the optimal decoder. Finally, applying these results to distributed multi-armed bandits, we show an upper bound on the regret of our synchronization scheme.

authors.name: Henrique Miyamoto
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

authors.name: Richard Combes
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Blow-Up and Life-Span for Nonlinear Hardy-H\'enon Parabolic Equations
papers.abstract: We consider the nonlinear Hardy-H\'enon parabolic equation $ u_t=\Delta u+|x|^l|u|^\alpha u,$ $t>0,$ $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$ or $x\in\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}$, with $N\ge1$, $l>-\min\{2,N\}$, $\alpha>0$, with nonnegative initial datum $u_0$. We first establish new criteria for finite-time blow-up. We then derive optimal upper bounds for the life-span $T_{\max}(\lambda\varphi)$ of solutions arising from the initial datum $u_0=\lambda\varphi$. These estimates establish a precise dependence of $T_{\max}(\lambda\varphi)$ on both the initial profile $\varphi$ and the parameter $\lambda$ in the small and large-amplitude regimes.

papers.title: Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline for Multi-Instance Asynchronous Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We present the Adaptive Scheduling Pipeline (ASP), an offline rollout scheduler for multi-instance asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) of large language models (LLMs). ASP jointly reduces three sources of rollout underutilization - padding bubbles from intra-minibatch length heterogeneity, skewness bubbles from long-tail outputs, and sorting bubbles from fluctuations in training-queue occupancy induced by length-sorted dispatch - through a single offline preprocessing pass. This enables efficient multi-instance rollout that overcomes the early scaling plateau of single-instance inference while smoothing the arrival of generated samples at the trainer. We integrate the scheduler into an asynchronous architecture that decouples rollout from training while keeping policy lag observable and bounded. Complete ASP improves end-to-end throughput by up to 3.22 times and reduces iteration time by up to 76.8% relative to MindSpeed-RL, while reducing iteration time by up to 62.5% relative to verl. Within ASP, scheduling reduces mean iteration time by 10.9%. ASP also scales more robustly with additional generation resources than these baselines and shows no visible convergence degradation in the measured bounded-lag regime. ASP has since been used in an internal telecom-domain RL post-training workflow, reducing the reported training period from more than three months to about two months and producing a domain-enhanced model for knowledge answering and tool calling.

papers.title: CNVAE: Anatomically Correct Segmentation via Conditional Generative Modeling
papers.abstract: Supervised deep learning segmentation models, although unparalleled in performance, are not immune to anatomical mistakes. We develop a segmentation-by-generation paradigm extending the Nouveau VAE (NVAE) generative framework for anatomically correct cardiac segmentation. In particular, we propose a novel conditional NVAE model (CNVAE) for conditional shape generation, and explore its capabilities for image segmentation in two scenarios: (1) direct image-to-mask CNVAE for one-step segmentation; (2) mask-to-mask CNVAE for refinement of segmentation masks produced by third-party segmentation models. Both models are lightweight and return consistently anatomically valid segmentation masks (> 98% success rate, an improvement of 15% above state-of-the-art segmentation models) on the cardiac segmentation/editing tasks of interest, without loss of accuracy in segmented contours.

papers.title: A Trivalent Graph of Girth 14 and Order 372
papers.abstract: The smallest known trivalent graph of girth 14 is constructed. The graph has 372 vertices, improving the old upper bound of 384 \cite{exoo14}. The construction uses methods that may be new to this problem.

papers.title: Malliavin structure for conditionally independent random variables
papers.abstract:
We consider a countable family of random variables which are conditionally
  independent given a latent random variable $Z$. Given $Z$, the random variables are independent. Hence the Malliavin
  calculus for independent random variables applies for each value of $Z$. We show that these constructions fit
  together. We obtain the chaos decomposition, the domains of the Malliavin
  operators, the Mehler formula and the carr\'e du champ operator, with
  conditional expectations given $Z$ in place of ordinary expectations. For normal
  approximation, conditioning on $Z$ and the infinite de Jong theorem of
  D\"obler give mixed normal approximations of degenerate U-statistics, in
  Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. Working under the unconditional
  probability, we obtain a de Jong type bound for U-statistics whose kernels
  are products. In both cases, the fluctuations of the conditional variance
  appear as an additional term, which cannot be removed. As an application, we
  consider subhypergraph counts in a random $3$-uniform hypergraph built on a
  latent random graph. For the count centred at its conditional mean, we
  obtain an explicit rate in Wasserstein distance. It reduces to the known
  rate for the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi hypergraph when the latent graph is
  complete. The count centred at its mean is a pattern count in a non-uniform
  hypergraph with independent edges, which gives a necessary and sufficient
  condition for its asymptotic normality.

papers.title: Nonzero solutions for Dirichlet problems with the competing (p,q)-Laplacian
papers.abstract: The following equation is considered: $$-\Delta_p u(\boldsymbol{x}) + \Delta_q u(\boldsymbol{x}) = f\big(\boldsymbol{x}, u(\boldsymbol{x})\big)\text{ for } \boldsymbol{x} \in \Omega, \qquad u(\boldsymbol{x}) = 0 \text{ for } \boldsymbol{x}\in \partial \Omega.$$ We start by showing that the energy functional associated with the considered problem no longer has the properties typical of its non-competing counterpart, which prevents a direct application of standard variational and monotonicity methods. Using Ekeland's variational principle combined with properties imposed on the nonlinear term~$f$, we prove the existence of a nonzero generalized solution to the problem. It is also shown that in the one-dimensional case $\Omega = (-1,1)$, assuming that $f$ satisfies the symmetry conditions $$f(x,u) = f(-x,u) = -f(x,-u),$$ together with the sign condition $f(x,u) \geq 0$ for $u \geq 0$ and an appropriate growth bound on $f$, a convex relaxation of the action functional yields the existence of a positive weak solution. Furthermore, we prove that in this setting, and under a slightly stronger sign condition $$f(x,u) > 0\text{ for }u > 0,$$ all global minimizers of the action functional do not vanish in $(-1,1)$ but fail to be of class $C^1$.

papers.title: Precedence Constraint Scheduling on a Fixed Number of Machines
papers.abstract:
We give a deterministic exact algorithm for $P_m\mid\mathrm{prec},p_j=1\mid C_{\max}$ for every fixed $m\ge3$. The algorithm constructs an optimum schedule in $$
  O(L)+m^{O(m^2)}\, n^{6m^2+13m+1} \, {\log n} $$ elementary RAM operations, where $n \ge 2$ is the number of jobs and $L$ is the binary input length. Its word size is $O(m^2 \log n)$ bits. An implementation with a fixed number of tapes uses $O(L)+m^{O(m^2)} \, n^{12m^2+26m+2} \, \log^3 n$ steps. For three machines the respective polynomial degrees are $94$ and $188$, apart from the displayed logarithmic factors.

papers.title: Singular Vortex in the Large Deviation of Empirical Current for Symmetric Simple Exclusion Process
papers.abstract: We prove a large deviation estimate for singular current observables of the two-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process. In particular, the observable has a non-standard large deviation scaling $N^2(\log N)^{-1}$ due to the presence of singular vortices, whereby trajectories rotating near the origin point yield an enhanced contribution to the current observable. The proof combines the heuristics of Bodineau-Derrida-Lebowitz 2008, the averaging method of Jara-Menezes 2018, and novel cancellation and multi-scale renormalization arguments developed by this paper.

papers.title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
papers.abstract: Frontier language models are increasingly deployed as agents, and how well an agent performs depends not only on its model but also on its harness: the prompts, tools, memory, and control loop through which the model acts. When an agent is applied to a new problem, a natural question is whether it can use the feedback of the task to improve the way it works, and not merely its answer. Most existing benchmarks keep the agent's harness fixed and score the solution it produces, or target large-scale model training. We introduce Flex-RSI, a benchmark for the recursive self-improvement of agents on vision and robotics tasks under a fixed budget. In each round, an executor improves the task solution, which is kept only if it scores higher on held-out validation data, and an improver then revises the harness, including the executor and itself. Every run starts from the same general-purpose harness, and the final solution is scored on hidden test data. Evaluating closed-source and open-weight models on tasks spanning perception, reasoning, robot action, 3D reconstruction, visual creation, and infrastructure, we find that self-improvement helps most when the agent builds its own solution, that feedback recording only success or failure holds back open-weight models, and that open-weight models fall furthest behind where outputs must pass strict checks of physical stability or exact correctness. Paired runs further show that editing the harness itself contributes to the gains.
