papers.title: BOXBOX: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement for Long-Running Performance Optimization
papers.abstract: Automated harness optimization improves agents by learning from trajectories and task feedback. Existing offline methods use reference answers to optimize harnesses for reuse on held-out tasks. However, many real-world tasks are open-ended, while long runs expose new difficulties that offline-optimized harnesses may not address. To study harness optimization in these settings, we introduce PerfRace, a benchmark for long-running performance optimization of software projects, and investigate whether agents can use task-specific experience to recursively improve their harnesses during an ongoing task. To this end, we introduce BOXBOX, which enables agent-triggered harness revision and kernel-managed hot reloading while preserving execution context. We evaluate BOXBOX on PerfRace under matched test-time budgets, comparing it with Frozen Harness, offline Harness Evolution, and Harness Scaling. BOXBOX achieves higher speedup with more efficient use of task time and model cost, reaching a Speedup@4h of 1.70x, compared with 1.54x for the strongest baseline.

authors.name: Yuan Yao
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Yu Kang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Violent relaxation redux
papers.abstract: Collisionless self-gravitating systems, such as merging galaxies, have long seemed an exception to the statistical-mechanical principle that chaotic many-body systems relax to maximum-entropy states: Lynden-Bell's statistical mechanics of their "violent relaxation," constrained by exact conservation of phase-space volume -- equivalently, of infinitely many collisionless "Casimir" invariants -- has appeared not to be a good description. We propose that violent relaxation does give rise to Lynden-Bell's maximum-entropy equilibria, but that both are underpinned by gravitational turbulence, in which large-scale gravitational fluctuations drive chaotic phase-space mixing of the particles' distribution function. We derive the universal small-scale (sub-Jeans) spectra of this turbulence and show that it leads to phase-space-volume conservation being broken on a timescale only logarithmically longer, in the particle number N, than the dynamical (violent-relaxation) time. This timescale separation lets the system relax "adiabatically" through a sequence of Lynden-Bell equilibria, each corresponding to instantaneous values of the Casimirs. At long times, it approaches an equilibrium close to its "ground state": a distribution whose Casimirs have adjusted so that the system's energy is now its minimum possible energy. Thus, the system's universal tendency is toward a minimum-energy, maximum-entropy state. We corroborate this picture with 1D N-body simulations and hypothesize that it can explain the universal equilibria of galaxies and dark-matter halos.

papers.title: Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
papers.abstract: We investigate an oscillatory equation of state for dark energy that oscillates around the mean value $-1$ and includes a source term proportional to the cube of the number of e-folds. Due to this source term, the oscillation amplitude shifts towards the $w_{\rm de}<-1$ regime at higher redshifts, whereas in the future, the source term drives the oscillation amplitude towards the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime. As the equation of state enters the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime in the future, the dark energy density dilutes, causing the Hubble parameter to decrease asymptotically towards zero, so that the present acceleration is transient: the Universe transitions to decelerated expansion and approaches a static state as $a\to\infty$, without ever contracting. We compare this equation of state with BellDE, CPL and flat $\Lambda$CDM. We confront the model with a combination of datasets, including Planck, DESI BAO and three different supernova compilations: Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-Dovekie. We compare the log-evidence of each model with that of $\Lambda$CDM. The dynamical dark energy models yield $H_0$ values in the range $66.0^{+0.80}_{-0.79}$--$67.84^{+0.69}_{-0.74}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with matter density values in the range $\Omega_{\rm m}=0.3067^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072}$--$0.3271^{+0.0083}_{-0.0080}$ across all the combinations. These values are consistent with those of the baseline model, apart from a mild upward shift in $\Omega_{\rm m}$ for the Union3 combination. Among all the models, BellDE yields comparatively stronger Bayesian evidence than the other models, with weak evidence for the Pantheon+ compilation and moderate evidence for the Union3 and DES-Dovekie compilations. The sourced oscillatory model yields inconclusive evidence for Pantheon + and Union3, while weak evidence for DES-Dovekie relative to $\Lambda$CDM.

papers.title: An Analytical Model for Laser-Activated Two-Phase Choking and Microfluidic Suction on Surface Boundary Layers
papers.abstract: We present a predictive fluid mechanics model to calculate pressure drops (0.25 atm) and fluid velocities (2.50 m/s) governed by localized phase change and choking phenomena in a capillary-constrained, coaxial microfluidic actuator. Driven by near-infrared thermal absorption, the analytical framework describes how energy deposition drives vapor cavity growth and subsequent cavitation bubble collapse, inducing a transient suction force across a curved, two-radii Young-Laplace capillary boundary. Velocity drops are derived from closed-form analytical equations that explicitly couple vapor volume dynamics with non-linear flow area restriction and fluid drag. The model predicts a maximum boundary layer wall shear stress of 30.06 Pa at the target interface. Crucially, this shear magnitude matches the physical threshold required to mechanically strip surface contaminant boundary layers while remaining below the damage threshold of underlying target substrates. Finally, we formulate a closed-form expression for the maximum allowable liquid inlet temperature required to prevent thermal saturation and sustain stable, continuous microfluidic suction cycles. These equations establish direct engineering design rules for optimizing phase-change microfluidic actuators and next-generation coaxial fluidic systems.

papers.title: A combined PRIMER+MINERVA study of the evolution of $\mathbf{[O\mbox{III}]+H\beta}$ equivalent width from $\mathbf{z=3}$ to $\mathbf{z=8.5}$
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of the evolution of $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent width ($W_{\lambda}$) over the redshift range $z=3$ to $z=8.5$, based on combining the JWST NIRCam PRIMER and MINERVA imaging in the UDS survey field. We find that the combined medium- and broad-band data set reduces the photometric redshift outlier rate to $\eta = 4.7\%$ at $m_{\rm F444W}\leq28$, a $42\%$ reduction compared with PRIMER imaging alone. We also demonstrate that the combined data set facilitates the accurate recovery of $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent widths in redshift bins centred on $z\sim3.2,\, 4.0,\, 5.0,\, 7.2,\, 8.3$; corresponding to the F210M, F250M, F300M, F410M and F460M filters. Based on a final sample of $N=1964$ galaxies with $M_{\rm UV}\leq-19.25$, we first provide new constraints on the bright end of the $z=7-8$ $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ luminosity function ($\log_{10}\phi^{*} = -4.3_{-0.5}^{+0.2}$, $\log_{10}L^{*} = -43.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}$), before proceeding to investigate the redshift evolution of $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent width. Using SED modelling based on non-parametric continuity star-formation histories, we find that the median $[O\,III]+\mathrm{H}\beta$ equivalent width monotonically increases with redshift, rising from $\mathrm{log}_{10}(W_{\lambda})=2.54^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$ at $z\simeq 3$ to $\mathrm{log}_{10}(W_{\lambda})=3.05^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$ at $z\simeq 8$. In tandem, the distribution of $\mathrm{log}_{10}(W_{\lambda})$ is observed to become increasingly asymmetric with redshift, producing a fraction of extreme emission-line galaxies (EELGs, $W_{\lambda}>1000\,$\r{A}) that reaches $f_{\rm EELG}=0.50\pm{0.10}$ by $z=8.3$. Our SED modelling results indicate that the physical driver of this evolution is increasingly bursty star-formation, with EELGs the result of particularly high specific star-formation rates over the 10 Myr prior to observation.

papers.title: Seeing Is Not Knowing: The Epistemic Limits of LLM-Based Mental Health Inference from Youth Social Media Conversations
papers.abstract: Adolescents increasingly use social media for private conversations, sharing experiences and seeking support. These interactions generate digital traces, prompting efforts to infer mental health and psychosocial states. As large language models become more capable of reasoning about conversations and interpersonal dynamics, a fundamental question remains nonetheless: what can models actually "know" about an individual's psychological experience from what they are able to "see"? We evaluated ten reasoning LLMs using donated Instagram Direct Messages from 80 adolescents with a history of depression or suicidal thoughts and behaviors, comparing predictions with self-reports and analyzing 204 reasoning traces. Models performed better when inferring more observable states than participants' subjective appraisals of social experience, such as perceived social support. Beyond prediction accuracy, our findings highlight the epistemic limits of digital traces for AI design and evaluation: what can be observed, what can reasonably be inferred, and what requires people's own accounts.

papers.title: HaNDF: Object-Conditioned Geometric Neural Hand Distance Fields
papers.abstract: We propose, HaNDF, object-conditional neural distance fields as data-driven priors for modeling the plausible hand-object configurations, in the product manifold of hand articulations. While recent unconditional generative priors showed success in modeling human pose, hands are versatile articulated bodies often found in interaction with other objects. This makes it crucial to develop a generative prior which can model the plausible hand poses conditioned on the object under interaction. To this end, our HaNDF proposes a geometry-aware, object-conditioned neural distance field, representing the plausible articulations in the zero-level set of a conditional field. We leverage tools from Riemannian geometry to (i) represent plausible hands in the zero level-set of an object-induced neural field, and (ii) project a given pose onto this field. Using HaNDF, we can also optimize for a plausible condition, determining the object under interaction. Our extensive evaluations demonstrate that our HaNDF provides a flexible and powerful prior for hand-object interaction, suitable for applications such as pose refinement, reconstruction under occlusion, and physically plausible manipulation synthesis.

papers.title: Turkish Multimodal Video Fact-Checking: A New Dataset and a Comparison of Zero-Shot Agentic and Fine-Tuned Systems
papers.abstract: Video-based misinformation spreads rapidly on social media, but almost all existing fact-checking systems focus exclusively on English text. Tools for low-resource languages such as Turkish are severely limited. In this work, we present TeViD (Turkish Video Fact-checking Dataset), to the best of our knowledge the first multimodal video fact-checking dataset for Turkish. We compiled the dataset from articles published by Teyit.org, an IFCN-certified organisation, and enriched it with translated Snopes articles and synthetic examples to reduce class imbalance. Building on TeViD, we develop two verification pipelines that share the same open-source base model. First, in 3MFact-TR (Pipeline 1), we adapt the multi-role 3MFact framework to Turkish with the Qwen2.5-7B large language model and the Qwen2-VL-7B vision-language model, and add three modules of our own: a semantic inconsistency checker, a 5W1H question manager, and a bilingual evidence retriever that excludes fact-checking sites to prevent leakage. Second, as our Fine-Tuned Model (Pipeline 2), we fine-tune a single Qwen2.5-7B with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to produce closed-book verdicts from the claim and the video's textual description. We report accuracy, macro F1, True class F1, and True class recall for both systems, together with ablation studies.

papers.title: Physical Sensing Verification for Cognitive ISAC against UAV Spoofing via Digital Twins
papers.abstract: As integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) lets 5G and 6G base stations detect drones, software agents will soon act on what they sense. This amplifies the threat of a relay replaying the base station's signal as a phantom drone. For such cognitive ISAC systems, this paper proposes a wall-based physical check. A digital twin (DT) predicts where a real target's wall echo must arrive; a relay can fake range, but not where its own reflections come from. The paper proves that line-of-sight beam steering cannot expose a matched relay, and that, under stated conditions, a single-antenna relay faking a wall echo leaves a telltale echo where a genuine target leaves none. In a pre-registered ray-tracing study, the twin's evidence separated genuine targets from replays perfectly (AUC 1.000) on held-out streets, and a later-registered passive check needing no extra transmission accepted every genuine target and no replay. The primary active probe was inconclusive, at 5.3\% false acceptances against a 5\% limit, for lack of threshold margin. At the evaluated relay positions, the conditional bound certifies 3 of 24 held-out streets, reproduced on fresh ones, against single-antenna relay signals meeting its conditions, adaptive or fixed, and 11 of 24 at double bandwidth.

papers.title: FishSense Lite: A Camera-Based, Single Laser Hardware Framework with Software System for In Situ Fish Length Measurement
papers.abstract: Fish stock assessments need fish lengths paired with species from far more places than trained surveyors can reach. Recreational divers already visit many of those places, but measuring a fish underwater has required trained observers or specialist equipment. We present FishSense Lite, which recovers fish length from a single photograph taken with a recreational dive camera, a dive laser pointer, and a 3D-printed mount. The diver aims the laser at a fish and takes a picture; afterward, the dot's position in the image gives the range to the fish, and the range turns the fish's size in the image into a length. A citizen-science program, trained by the system's builders, taught its own divers and collected lengths paired with species for 73 wild fish across seven open-water dives. On seven wild fish also measured by an underwater stereo-imaging system, the two instruments agreed without detectable bias (mean difference +0.8%). On rigid targets of known length, FishSense Lite recovered every target to within 1.3%, and 99% of 1,055 frames fell within a 15% error budget. From the error sources we measure, we derive a field protocol: calibrate against a dive slate on every dive, photograph fish within 15 degrees of perpendicular and beyond 1 m, and take at least ten frames of each.

papers.title: The Complex Magnetic Anatomy of a White Dwarf Chromosphere
papers.abstract: This study presents phase-resolved spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry of the DAHe white dwarf LP 705-64. Here, two apparently discrete chromospheric regions are observed to alternate in visibility and magnetic polarity with rotation, with field strengths of 9.5 and 22 MG based on the measured Zeeman splitting in H{\alpha}. As in the class prototype GD 356, emission line equivalent widths vary in antiphase with the broadband light curve. The 9.5 MG field is visible for 60 per cent of the stellar rotation and stays nearly constant, whereas the 22 MG field increases modestly during the remaining phases. Notably, the time-series transitions between magnetic regions are abrupt and transit-like in morphology, requiring at least one magnetic region to be highly localised and significantly smaller than the areas inferred for the dark surface spots. Both the intensity and the Stokes V/I spectra indicate a field configuration significantly more complex than an offset dipole, but higher-cadence data are necessary to distinguish between a global field and localised magnetic regions. All data are consistent with magnetic, chromospheric, and dark surface regions that are co-located and thus physically related. These findings support a model of chromospheric emission that is intrinsic and localised, consistent with predictions of dynamo-driven electrical currents that heat the upper atmosphere near magnetic poles.

papers.title: Conflux: Preventing Privilege Escalation with Principal Contexts and System-Level Evaluation
papers.abstract: LLM agents combine information from multiple principals while acting externally. We formalise privilege escalation (PE) as the system-level security objective: an action may proceed only if every principal that influenced it would allow it. Model-level defences remain probabilistic, so enforcement must sit outside model judgement. We present Conflux, a principal-context defence. Its kernel, ITES, derives authority from provenance and the organisation's existing access-control system and intersects the permissions of every influencing principal. We prove a conditional authority-confinement theorem: under complete mediation, no-laundering provenance, a known non-empty decision context, fresh permission checks, and action binding, the kernel admits no action that escalates privilege with respect to any recorded influencing principal. The theorem covers the represented value-influence fragment; control influence from tool, branch, recipient, or plan-step selection remains a refinement obligation. Conflux extends the kernel with independent policy ports, argument-aware authorisation, disclosure, consent, delegation, restriction, and exposure planning. We describe two system- level evaluators. SLED is a black-box evaluator: it exhaustively explores a declared finite model of a defence up to a bound. SLED-V is a white-box evaluator: it checks a serialisable intermediate representation against security and provenance properties. The evidence is bounded and partial. The appendix reports retained AgentDojo, SLED, and SLED-V results, including the limits of those runs. No result in this paper is an unbounded deployment guarantee.

papers.title: Training Stability under Adaptive Curricula
papers.abstract: Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approaches train reinforcement learning (RL) agents on diverse curricula that may evolve with their capabilities. While prior work has largely focused on how these curricula are constructed, we study whether their students remain trainable under the resulting distributions. Across multiple UED mechanisms, environment complexities, and extended training horizons, we identify recurring learner-side pathologies, including parameter growth, degraded value--outcome ordering, and loss of representational diversity, that accompany stagnation and performance degradation. These findings connect limitations in UED to optimization failures previously identified in conventional deep RL, while showing how adaptive curricula couple the learner's optimization state to its future training distribution. Controlled interventions show that mitigating selected pathologies improves learning. Stabilizing the learner improves long-horizon performance and zero-shot generalization without changing the curriculum rule or increasing environment interaction. Our results establish learner trainability as a complementary design principle for UED. Effective curricula require students that remain capable of learning from the distributions they produce.

papers.title: High-Dimensional Off-Policy Evaluation without Sample Splitting using an Onsager Correction
papers.abstract: Reward models used for off-policy evaluation (OPE) are commonly selected using held-out data. When sample size and context dimension grow proportionally, the difference in test risk between models fitted on the full sample and on a fixed fraction of it need not vanish. Held-out evaluation can therefore consistently estimate the test risk of the model trained on the smaller sample, but because the relative ranking of candidate reward models can change after full-data refitting, held-out selection can be suboptimal. We develop an Onsager-corrected, target-policy-weighted criterion that estimates the full-data reward model's out-of-sample risk under the target policy using only its training observations. This enables early stopping along the full-data gradient-descent trajectory without sample splitting. For neural networks with fixed depth and hidden width under Gaussian contexts, single-index rewards, context-dependent multi-index target policies, and known context-independent logging, we prove uniform consistency of our criterion over a fixed finite set of gradient-descent iterates and a near-oracle guarantee for the selected reward model. The same correction yields a doubly robust estimator that consistently estimates the true policy value without sample splitting, even when reward-model prediction error does not vanish. Experiments show decreasing risk-estimation error as dimension grows at a fixed sample-to-dimension ratio, and improved reward-model selection relative to held-out baselines. Empirically, our correction also reduces the root mean squared error of doubly robust value estimates computed from the same data used to fit and select the reward models.

papers.title: Growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb quantum devices
papers.abstract: We report recent progress in the growth and fabrication of advanced PbTe-Pb Majorana devices for three-terminal correlation experiments. A critical prerequisite for these devices is a continuous Pb film spanning from the PbTe nanowire to the substrate. In previous studies, PbTe nanowires were spatially separated from the substrate mask, making them unable to fulfill this requirement. To address this issue, we have developed a new growth and fabrication approach. Key fabrication steps are introduced between the PbTe growth and Pb deposition. The top facet of the PbTe nanowire is covered with a Te capping layer before breaking the ultra-high vacuum, enabling ex situ processing for subsequent steps. The mask is then removed, followed by the fabrication of shadow walls. After reloading the chip into the growth chamber, the Te protection layer is removed through thermal decomposition, and the Pb film is subsequently deposited. Notably, a pristine PbTe-Pb interface with an in-situ-equivalent quality can be achieved despite the ex-situ processing. Our technique facilitates the develop of advanced PbTe-Pb quantum devices with complex designs, paving the way toward the realization of topological qubits.

papers.title: The APL Doesn't Fall Far From The Tree: Unsupervised Artefact Prototype Learning in Histopathology
papers.abstract: Histopathology foundation models provide rich representations of tissue morphology, but technical artefacts in whole slide images introduce noise that may impact diagnostic accuracy. We introduce Artefact Prototype Learning (APL), a novel approach to detecting these artefacts that exploits the geometry of pre-trained embedding spaces without manual labels or fine-tuning. Rather than treating artefacts as isolated outliers, APL computes prototypes of out-of-distribution patches and uses them to distinguish artefact-associated patterns from tissue. Evaluation on a single-centre dataset shows that APL outperforms prior methods GrandQC and HistoART in detecting artefacts such as blur, dark spots, slide edges and pen marks, but struggles with tissue folds and blood. These results show that frozen pre-trained embeddings already carry information that allows artefact detection without expensive labels or vast computational resources.

papers.title: Bounds on Negligible Thresholds in Group Cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a field, $K/F$ a field extension with $\Gamma_K:=\text{Gal}(K_\text{sep}/K)$, $G$ a finite group, $j:\Gamma_K\rightarrow G$ a continuous group homomorphism, and $M$ an abelian group. There is an induced map of profinite cohomology $j^*:H^n (G;M)\rightarrow H^n (K;M)=:H^n (\Gamma_K;M)$. An element $u\in H^n (G;M)$ is negligible over $F$ if $j^* (u)=0$ for all such $j$ and field extensions $K/F$. The subset of negligible elements forms a subgroup $H^n (G;M)_{\text{neg},F}\subseteq H^n (G;M)$. The negligible threshold $\text{nthres}^G_F (M)$ is the smallest $N\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq 0}\cup\{\infty\}$ such that $H^n (G;M)_{\text{neg},F}=H^n (G;M)$ for all $n\geq N$. In this paper, we first establish some general bounds for negligible thresholds of arbitrary triples $(G,M,F)$ consisting of a finite group $G$, trivial $G$-module $M$, and field $F$. We then compute the negligible thresholds of an arbitrary group when $F$ is a field of characteristic $p$ and $M=\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z}$. Continuing in the characteristic $p$ setting, we compute these thresholds for $G$ a $p$-group and $M=\mathbb{Z}$, and we compute the thresholds for $G=\mathbb{Z}/\ell\mathbb{Z},M=\mathbb{Z}/s\mathbb{Z}$ for integers $s,\ell\in\mathbb{N}_{>1}$ satisfying certain number theoretic conditions. For fields containing sufficiently many roots of unity, we show that the negligible threshold of odd exponent finitely-generated trivial $G$-modules is finite. For $G$-modules of the form $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, $p$ an odd prime, we compute an explicit upper bound for the negligible threshold in terms of $p$ and $|G|$. We conclude by providing explicit computations of the negligible thresholds of elementary abelian $p$-groups with mod-$p$ coefficients, negligible thresholds of cyclic groups, and bounds on mod-$p$ negligible thresholds of general finite abelian $p$-groups.

papers.title: UniMore: Fine-Grained Supervision for Unified Understanding and Generation
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal models combine image understanding and generation within one system, creating an opportunity to improve both capabilities through paired image--text supervision. We examine the outputs of a pretrained unified model in both directions and observe a loss of specificity: generated images can contain the requested objects with incorrect attributes, while captions identify a scene without expressing its distinguishing details. These failures call for supervision that specifies both the visual content to realize and the descriptive differences to distinguish. We propose UniMore, a post-training method that derives these complementary learning tasks from the fine-grained content of image--text pairs. The generation route predicts grounded crops from their corresponding phrases, matching the scope of the condition and visual target while using the native visual objective. The understanding route combines positive-caption fitting with ranking against captions that omit or alter details, conditioned on the full image. The two routes are optimized independently, and their learned updates are combined into a single unified model without changing its inference procedure. Experiments show gains across multiple understanding and generation benchmarks.

papers.title: BMMS: Policy-Conditioned Measurement of Behavioral Compliance in Language Models
papers.abstract: Behavioral evaluation of language models fixes its dimensions in advance: hallucination, sycophancy, toxicity, over-refusal. An operator in a regulated industry needs a different question answered: does a system do what a particular rulebook requires? We introduce the Behavioral Misalignment Metric Suite (BMMS), which measures policy-conditioned misalignment by taking a policy corpus as an argument and returning a compliance profile over it, for any published policy and any system that answers in natural language. The Compliance Attainment Score (CAS) measures severity-weighted attainment over the obligations that bind the system, and the Compliance Robustness Margin (CRM) the share of that attainment surviving graded adversarial pressure; Behavioral Invariance (BIV) and the Behavioral Disposition Index (BDI) are specified and released with the suite. Dimensions enter only by passing a published admission test whose binding criterion is attribution: a quantity that moves when the judge changes, holding the target fixed, is measuring the instrument. Applying it excluded one of the quantities the suite itself reported. Across 1,003 obligations from eleven documents in five registers, the admission criterion holds 94.4% precision against blinded human judgment on vendor specifications and 50.0% on analytical guidance, extraction fidelity is 94.6%, and re-scoring under judges from two other providers leaves target ordering invariant while the absolute score of a single target spans up to 0.22. We apply it to the two most detailed published behavioral specifications. Own-specification advantage is not resolved from zero once document difficulty is subtracted, but absolute self-compliance is another matter: GPT-4o fails 70.7% of the hard constraints binding it in the Model Spec published by OpenAI, where the two Claude models fail 0.0% and 9.1% of theirs.

papers.title: Calibrated concept profiles: making the reading of a model's neurons a measurement
papers.abstract:
Interpretability has largely moved from reading a model's neurons directly to reading a second model trained on the first: a probe, a sparse autoencoder, a crosscoder. The move answered real faults -- mixed meanings, thresholds without a unit, readings that did not transfer from one study to the next -- but gave up what a direct reading alone provides: nothing trained in between, the neurons themselves named, and a reading that can be repeated and compared. Here the direct reading is made a measurement.
  A neuron's activation varies with the prompt, so its reading is a distribution over a population of stimuli. We declare that population: every factor around a target construct is drawn at its rate in a reference corpus and logged.
  From the declared distribution we generate a battery of prompts, and draw it twice. From the battery we compute the calibrated concept profile, one number per neuron, stated in units of the neuron's own spread on ordinary input; the two draws give every number a noise unit. Before the profile is read, a fixed set of checks licenses the battery on the model, and the smallest change the profile can resolve across training checkpoints is measured.
  Realised for Python on OpenCoder-1.5B and followed across checkpoints spanning two trillion training tokens, the profile gives what the alternatives do not report: a unit on every number, a chance level for every comparison, and which neurons carry a construct at every checkpoint.
  The battery, the code and the data behind every result are released.

papers.title: Representational drift in a code model: behaviour settles, which neurons carry it does not
papers.abstract: In neuroscience, representational drift is a change in which neurons carry a representation while behaviour stays the same; we measure its analogue in OpenCoder-1.5B during pretraining, for 169 Python constructs over two trillion tokens at a constant learning rate, with a noise unit on every change, at checkpoints as close as 1,000 training steps. For 16 of the 169, those whose grammar fixes a next token, the loss at those positions reaches its floor within the first 4% of training, while the model's reliance on the neurons carrying them grows to the end: removing them costs 0.06, 0.25 and 0.40 nats more than removing a random set, at 4 billion, 84 billion and 2 trillion tokens. Which neurons carry a construct never settles: for all 169 the carrier set is still changing at the last checkpoint, and an abrupt settling at any date from 84 billion to 1.5 trillion tokens, or a gradual one before 500 billion, would have been detected in 99% of injected cases. The set measured at 84 billion tokens, removed at the end, cannot be separated from a random set, so the function is carried by whichever neurons are current. Up close the change is a persisting pool and a changing sample: a neuron that leaves a construct's set returns at three times the rate of a matched neuron, and no set reassembles. The hypothesis we fixed in advance, that the carriers settle, is refuted; we discuss candidate causes and name the experiment that would separate them.

papers.title: A Stochastic Latent Variable Generalization of Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
papers.abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) predict the latent embedding of a target signal from a context signal, with an auxiliary variable z conditioning the predictor. Despite its prominent role in the original JEPA blueprint, the content of z has been carried by a fixed deterministic token in every prior instantiation, collapsing the genuinely multi-modal distribution over plausible completions to a point estimate. We present S-JEPA, which realises z as a proper stochastic latent variable for masked image prediction: a learned posterior infers z from context and target during training, while a learned context-conditioned prior approximates the distribution of plausible completions at inference, with no decoders and no reconstruction. In its deterministic limit the objective reduces to the I-JEPA loss in functional form, generalising that objective rather than strictly containing the I-JEPA model. Our central finding is that stochasticity adds capabilities, error-correlated predictive uncertainty and diverse completions, at no cost to representation quality: under matched architectures and schedules S-JEPA improves over the deterministic I-JEPA baseline and exceeds LeJEPA at matched architecture, while additionally producing spatially structured uncertainty maps and semantically diverse completions, neither of which the deterministic predictor produces.

papers.title: Successive Decimetric Bursts Associated with Breakout Magnetic Reconnection during the Decay Phase of an M-Class Flare
papers.abstract: Radio imaging spectroscopy diagnoses coronal electron acceleration and propagation by tracking energetic electron beams and locating energy-release sites. Using MUSER (0.4-2 GHz) and SDO data, we investigate decimetric radio emission during an eruption with an M1.1 flare on 17 December 2014. The eruption involves a twisted coronal structure evolving through three stages: a violent internal eruption, a rise-and-expansion phase, and a breakout eruption. The flare peaks at 01:50 UT during the internal eruption, while the cluster of successive type III-like decimetric bursts occurs in the decay phase, linked to the breakout eruption. The radio source coincides with a high-squashing-factor Q region from nonlinear force-free field (NLFFF) extrapolations, indicating a quasi-separatrix layer (QSL). We interpret the radio emission as consistent with plasma emission driven by nonthermal electrons accelerated by breakout reconnection at this QSL, between the outer envelope of the erupting structure and the surrounding corona. The successive bursts occur in the decay phase because breakout reconnection involves a larger, more energetic twisted structure at higher altitude, where an extended high-Q region, favorable acceleration geometry, and repeated sub-eruptions sustain efficient electron acceleration. Missing soft X-ray enhancement suggests most accelerated electrons escape upward or lose energy before reaching the chromosphere. The concentrated source positions of the successive radio bursts suggest pseudostreamers may act as particle accelerators, trapping electrons and directing them along a narrow layer. These results establish decimetric radio imaging as a powerful diagnostic of breakout reconnection and particle acceleration in the solar corona, with implications for energy release in pseudostreamer environments.

papers.title: ReSUM: Reasoning-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Query-Focused Summarization
papers.abstract: LLMs excel at language tasks, but long-meeting QFS remains difficult due to complex speaker dynamics, sparse key information, and limited data. Meetings involve disfluencies, long transcripts and complex discourse. QFS have high risk of information omission, hallucination, even for advanced models such as GPT-4-mini and Gemini. Existing end-to-end methods compress retrieval, evidence extraction, and summary generation into a single pass, failing to handle the complex reasoning required for targeted meeting summaries. We propose ReSUM, a modular multi-LLM framework coordinated by a planner that orchestrates retrieval and summarization agents. By distilling teacher reasoning into query- and plan-conditioned retrievers and summarizers, ReSUM enhances long-context robustness, minimizes irrelevant exploration, and generates more faithful and comprehensive query-focused summaries. Experiments show consistent gains on query-focused meeting summarization benchmarks.

papers.title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of enzyme kinetic parameters can support enzyme engineering and metabolic modeling by complementing experimental characterization. Existing prediction methods often pool residue-level protein features before combining them with substrate features. Such substrate-independent pooling cannot adapt residue weighting to the substrate during aggregation, potentially diluting information relevant to a specific enzyme-substrate pair. Since the contributions of individual residues to catalysis can depend on the substrate, substrate-conditioned aggregation offers a way to emphasize residue features relevant to the prediction. We introduce KineCouple, which uses substrate queries and residue-level keys and values in cross-attention, allowing the substrate to guide residue selection before aggregation. The model preserves the global protein representation and adds a gated correction defined as the difference between the conditioned readout and a uniform readout. ProtT5 and MolT5 remain frozen, and separate models predict kcat and Km on a logarithmic scale. In pooled out-of-fold predictions on the CataPro benchmarks, KineCouple reduces kcat RMSE from 1.333 to 1.330 and increases PCC from 0.492 to 0.496 relative to reproduced CataPro. For Km, RMSE decreases from 0.998 to 0.997 and PCC increases from 0.633 to 0.634. Spearman correlation also improves for both tasks.

papers.title: SmartBloch-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Automated MRI Sequence Design and Optimization
papers.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pulse sequences organize radiofrequency excitation, gradient encoding, and signal acquisition, determining magnetization evolution and image formation. Sequence research requires translating imaging objectives into executable protocols meeting physical and acquisition constraints, refined via physical simulation, signal reconstruction, and scientific evaluation. Sequence construction, physical verification, parameter search, and assessment involve many tools and manual decisions, limiting automation from objective to verifiable sequence. We develop SmartBloch-Agent, an integrated framework for automated MRI sequence design and optimization. Given objectives and scientific constraints in natural language, an AI agent interprets goals, plans tasks, orchestrates tools, and makes feedback-informed decisions, drawing on a construction module and optimizers for structural design and parameter search. Our GPU-accelerated SmartBloch engine supplies physical computation for both stages, so the framework configures, per sequence and objective, event validation, Full-Bloch magnetization evolution, signal acquisition, image reconstruction, and scientific evaluation, and closes the loop without external MRI simulators. Results return to the agent to guide sequence revision, parameter optimization, and candidate selection, and the design files carry simulation, reconstruction, and evaluation evidence, forming an output package for a real-scanner workflow. Experiments show the framework automatically designs and optimizes MRI sequences for varied objectives and constraints, refines candidates with physical feedback, and improves several parameter-estimation metrics and downstream quantitative reconstruction. SmartBloch-Agent unifies objectives, design, physical execution, and evaluation into a continuous workflow for end-to-end automation of MRI sequence research.

papers.title: Sparse Array-Inspired Frame Structure Design for 5G NR ISAC
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) has emerged as a promising paradigm for future wireless networks. However, the extensive occupation of time-frequency resources for sensing limits the communication capacity. To address the resource conflict, this paper proposes a novel sparse sensing frame structure aligned with the 5G new radio (5G NR) resource grid at the slot and physical resource block (PRB) levels through a predefined sensing-pattern block. Specifically, inspired by the design of two-dimensional (2D) sparse antenna arrays, we map the sparse spatial geometries onto the time-frequency resource grid. By leveraging the hole-free property of the difference coarray, we eliminate the range-velocity ambiguity and cast the sensing signals into a reconstructed higher-order tensor representation. For efficient parameter estimation, we propose a novel binary-tree-based tensor train decomposition (BT-TTD) algorithm that extracts lower-dimensional tensor train cores (TT-cores) and executes a Vandermonde-prior-guided rectified alternating least squares (RecALS) algorithm. Simulation results validate that the proposed scheme achieves competitive estimation accuracy with reduced complexity. Furthermore, we investigate the topological properties of various sparse patterns, revealing the inherent trade-off among sensing accuracy, resource occupancy, and computational complexity.

papers.title: BiLoGo: Reducing the smoothing of localised responses in Transformer-based neural operators for sheet forming
papers.abstract: Trial-and-error FE simulation of sheet forming could be computationally expensive, neural-network-based learned simulators are used to accelerate design. These simulators should accurately capture localised responses, such as thinning around sharp radii or near ribs, which determine formability. Transformer-based neural operators propagate information efficiently across the mesh but tend to smooth such localised responses. This study develops BiLoGo, a Bipartite Local-Global learned simulator with an FE-guided design that connects local node-element message passing with a Transformer-based neural operator for long-range information exchange. BiLoGo has three modules: a bidirectional node-element GraphSAGE model that learns nodal-elemental coupling on a bipartite graph and predicts each quantity on its native FE entity without interpolation; a dual-stream Transformer-based neural operator that processes blank deformation and tool contact with separate token sets, preventing localised contact information from being averaged with the whole-blank state; and a fusion and element update module that combines global and local features via gated residual fusion and updates element features conditioned on element-node kinematics. Evaluated on a dome-shaped cold forming case and two corner-shaped hot stamping cases (one with ribs), BiLoGo achieves the lowest positional and threshold-based thinning errors on all three cases compared with single-level and hierarchical graph-based models and Transformer-based neural operators. Near the ribs, the smoothing index of predicted thinning increases from 0.41-0.56 for Transformer-based neural operators to 0.94 for BiLoGo-U. Compared with the hierarchical graph network CAtt-BiUGNN, BiLoGo-T reduces mean positional error by 15.5% on the Corner case and BiLoGo-U by 8.3% on the Corner+Rib case, with 66-69% less training memory.

papers.title: Path-dependent triage: Early judgments lead conversational AI chatbots to miss mental-health emergencies
papers.abstract: People increasingly bring mental-health concerns to consumer AI chatbots. In these conversations, clinically relevant information rarely arrives all at once. Instead, it unfolds over multiple turns, often in response to the questions the chatbot asks. Recognizing risk therefore depends on how a chatbot integrates newly disclosed information (inference) and on the questions it asks on each turn to elicit this information (context-seeking). Here we evaluated the conversational triage performance of 13 frontier AI chatbots tasked with engaging in 10-turn conversations with simulated users. Simulated users were grounded in one of 112 structured mental-health case files, each with an associated clinician-validated urgency level, from routine care to emergency. Chatbots failed to recognize one in five mental-health emergencies (20.3%), nearly four times the failure rate when all relevant clinical details were presented in a single message (5.6%). This gap was not explained by missing information: by the final turn, decisive facts had almost always been disclosed, and simply re-presenting those same facts as a single message reduced emergency under-triage to 12.1%. The problem lay instead in how the conversation unfolded, a phenomenon we refer to as path dependence. Early triage dispositions increasingly anchored later ones, such that emergencies missed early were rarely recovered as evidence accumulated. Context-seeking narrowed onto a small number of stereotyped questioning trajectories, with chatbots perseverating more than human clinicians given the same transcripts. Because the chatbot's running judgment shaped what it asked next, these two biases were plausibly coupled across turns. These dynamics are invisible to single-turn benchmarks but measurable in multi-turn evaluation, and point to concrete mitigations for safer conversational triage in consumer health AI.

papers.title: Where Should Learning Live? Regret Analysis for Text, Parameter, and Joint Adaptation
papers.abstract: Language-model systems can select prompts and parameter adapters repeatedly during deployment, using feedback to guide later choices. Earlier choices may change the context or environment inherited by later configurations. We study selection among preconstructed candidates and compare cumulative loss with the best fixed prompt--parameter pair used from the beginning. This excess loss separates into three terms: selection regret within the available family, the gap from restricting that family, and the benefit or harm of the actual deployment history. Selection is evaluated using the history each candidate would have produced if used throughout, which separates candidate quality from the effects of switching. When loss functions are fixed independently of selector randomness, past choices affect loss for only a bounded number of rounds, and every candidate's own-history loss is revealed, limiting switches yields sublinear expected regret within the selected family. We also quantify the costs and additional assumptions of independent probing and deployment-only feedback. Controlled experiments show that fewer switches can either lower or raise deployed loss, depending on whether inherited histories are harmful or helpful. With Qwen3.5-9B on Spider, text-only selection has lower within-family regret than joint selection, yet produces more failures because its candidate family excludes stronger configurations.

papers.title: The Cost of Coverage: Conformalising Native Forecast Uncertainty for GB Wind Power
papers.abstract: Uncertainty bands on wind forecasts help inform reserve sizing and commitments, but often fail to deliver their stated coverage. We apply conformal prediction to native bands to see what it adds and what it costs, comparing six forecasters, from ARIMA to a tabular foundation model, at two wind farms in Great Britain (GB) under operational conditions. We show that calibration repairs empirical marginal coverage with little or no Winkler Score penalty, but this apparent success conceals under-coverage in high winds. Calibrating by forecast wind regime turns marginal coverage into regime-level coverage, cutting day-ahead out-of-band volume in high winds by over 40% relative to pooled calibration while narrowing bands overall.

papers.intro:
Wind became Great Britain’s largest source of electricity in 2024, supplying 30% of generation and marking a major milestone in the shift from fossil fuels to renewable power (National Energy System Operator (2025a), NESO). At the site level, generation volume is settled every half-hour against contracted positions with deviations cashed out at the balancing price, which rises sharply when the system is short. On the 8th of January 2025, a shortfall in forecast wind helped push prices to £2,900/MWh and contributed to a single-day balancing cost of £21M (National Energy System Operator (2025b), NESO). Prediction intervals are central to decision making under this weather uncertainty, but remain useful only if they achieve their stated coverage without becoming too wide.

Modern machine learning forecasting pipelines output native prediction intervals, yet these are often miscalibrated and routinely under- or over-cover nominal targets. Parametric and Bayesian methods rely on distributional assumptions, while quantile regression depends on fit. Conformal Prediction (CP) (Vovk et al., 2005) offers finite-sample, distribution-free marginal coverage (averaged over all forecasts) around an arbitrary base forecaster. This guarantee rests on exchangeability, an assumption wind violates through autocorrelation and seasonal non-stationarity. The literature responds through re-weighting (Barber et al., 2023), residual modelling (Xu and Xie, 2023), and online adaptation (Gibbs and Candes, 2021).

We contribute three things: (i) a native-versus-wrapped measurement, scoring six forecaster classes against their conformalised counterparts on the same held-out sample in coverage, width and Winkler Score; (ii) an open operational benchmark with two wind farms, across three horizons, purged refits and weather data delays, with the full pipeline released; (iii) an account of how missed energy varies with wind regime and direction.
