Under (C), we prove that the ordinary Diophantine exponent is at most m and, when both dimensions are at least two, that the uniform exponent is at most m^2/(m+1). Combining these bounds with known results, we determine the individual spectra of both exponents under (C), with and without the additional assumption (B). When both dimensions are at least two, imposing (B) changes neither spectrum. A key ingredient is a block lemma for consecutive best approximations lying in a fixed rational subspace.

papers.title: When is an Optical Design Problem a Mass Transfer Problem?
papers.abstract: This paper investigates whether optical design problems can be represented as Monge--Kantorovich mass transfer problems with some cost function. An optical problem is specified by a function defining a particular family of supporting surfaces for the optical element. We introduce the notion of geometric equivalence between optical and transport problems, which is directly related to the possibility of formulating an optical design problem as a mass transfer problem. A necessary condition for such equivalence is derived in the semi-discrete setting. It allows a transport representation to be ruled out without choosing a cost function in advance. The condition is applied to the near-field refractor problem and to the design of two refracting surfaces transforming a spherical beam into a spherical or collimated beam. For these problems, the necessary condition is shown to fail in physically admissible configurations. We also study an optical element with a single working surface and an arbitrary regular incident wavefront. In the far field, geometric equivalence to a mass transfer problem requires a planar or spherical wavefront, whereas in the near field with a planar target, the necessary condition fails for an arbitrary smooth wavefront.

papers.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
papers.abstract: The double and triple approaches of supermassive central black holes are a fairly common process in the hierarchical picture of galaxy formation. In this case, the ejection of a black hole is possible; it may carry the accretion disk and some amount of stars with it. The activity of the galactic nucleus can be restored after the ejection. One consequence of this activity is an ultrafast gas outflow, accompanied by a shock wave. We show that the acceleration of cosmic rays at such a shock is more effective than in the case of a stationary galactic nucleus due to the lower density of the surrounding gas and the higher velocity of the shock front. In this case, proton acceleration can occur up to energies of ~10^{19} eV, which is an order of magnitude higher than in an ordinary nucleus in the centers of galaxies.

papers.title: Tetragonal conic bundles
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the birational geometry of three-dimensional algebraic varieties admitting a conic bundle structure. The central focus is on tetragonal transformations -- a special class of birational maps between standard conic bundles that are not fiberwise and play a key role in the birational geometry of such varieties.

papers.title: Anchored Iterative Decoding of Reed-Solomon Product Codes for High-Rate Magnetic Tape Storage
papers.abstract: We present a decoding algorithm for a Reed--Solomon product code targeted at the demanding reliability requirements of modern magnetic tape storage. For a code $RS(256, 224)\times RS(175, 173)$ in a BSC we achieve post-decoding bit error rate (BER) of $10^{-20}$ at $\approx 5.3\times 10^{-3}$ raw BER while maintaining the common requirement to detect and correct 4 out of 32 dead tracks. We resolve two common problems of miscorrections and stall patterns that arise under such a high raw BER via simplified versions of anchor decoding and binary image analysis. The highest efficiency is achieved by performing an unlimited iterative decoder, which performs decoding iterations until no changes are made. We give an empirical analysis of the average number of iterations: below the raw BER of $5\times 10^{-3}$, four half-iterations are performed on average while improving substantially over a decoder that always performs 4 half-iterations. We provide a CPU implementation achieving 100-200 megabytes/s single-core throughput on a regular laptop and a design of a potential hybrid FPGA-CPU implementation of our decoder.

authors.name: Nikolay Malkovsky
authors.institution: National Research University Higher School of Economics

papers.title: Josephson current along the domain walls in Weyl fully compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl
papers.abstract: We experimentally investigate Josephson current in planar Nb-Ti$_2$MnAl-Nb proximity devices, which are formed as junctions between superconducting niobium leads and single crystal flakes of the Weyl fully compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl. We demonstrate well developed Josephson effect for 2~$\mu$m distance between the niobium contacts on the Ti$_2$MnAl surface. The measured critical current dependence on the magnetic field $I_c(B)$ shows strong anisotropy for two magnetic field orientations in respect to the Nb-Ti$_2$MnAl-Nb junction plane. For the parallel magnetic field, one can see standard Fraunhofer-like $I_c(B)$ suppression pattern. In contrast, $I_c(B)$ is qualitatively different in normal magnetic field, indicating non-trivial distribution of the Josephson current within the junction plane. From this anisotropy, long-range supercurrent and fast aperiodic fluctuations in $I_c(B)$ we conclude that Josephson current is transferred by the chiral surface states, which emerge along the domain walls in topological compensated ferrimagnet Ti$_2$MnAl. The conclusion on the domain walls is supported by magnetization data for small Ti$_2$MnAl flakes.

papers.title: Random Symbolic Boosting: A Geometric Approach to Symbolic Regression
papers.abstract: Symbolic models offer interpretability, but their construction through generational evolution can be computationally expensive. This article presents Random Symbolic Boosting (RSB), a method that constructs explicit additive symbolic models via boosting over populations of randomly generated syntax trees, eliminating the need for generational evolution. The idea combines two observations: high-dimensional spaces can be spanned by enough linearly independent vectors, and the semantics of syntax trees can be directly manipulated as such vectors. It is shown that, for Ordinary Least Squares, the boosting process guarantees a monotonic reduction of the training error for both regression and classification. Furthermore, an adaptive geometric early stopping mechanism is introduced. It is based on the angle between the prediction and target vectors, is independent of the problems scale, and requires no adjustments across tasks. Evaluated on a standard benchmark for symbolic regression, the method is located at the Pareto-optimal point between predictive accuracy and training time, ranking first on the real-world datasets. Additionally, it was tested on a large tabular classification benchmark with 200 problems, achieving competitive results.

authors.name: Leonardo Trujillo
authors.institution: Laboratório de Sistemas Informáticos de Grande Escala

papers.title: TUGB: A Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding Framework
papers.abstract: Generative modeling, particularly Decision Transformers, shows promise in auto-bidding strategies. However, it struggles with limited exploration in static offline datasets, vulnerability to dynamic environmental shifts, and a reliance on heuristic return-to-go (RTG) specifications that may yield suboptimal performance on unseen traffic. To address these challenges, we propose the Two-stage Uncertainty-aware Generative Auto-Bidding (TUGB) framework. TUGB integrates generative sequence modeling with Reinforcement Learning (RL). It employs a two-stage pipeline where a pre-trained Generative Bidding Model is fine-tuned via an ensemble-based Uncertainty-aware Environment Model. This approach quantifies epistemic uncertainty to penalize high-risk trajectories and evolves the policy from RTG-conditioning to direct bidding optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TUGB significantly outperforms SOTA baselines. Notably, full-scale deployment on JD Search Ad achieved a 2.32\% increase in cost and 3.57\% in target cost, validating its industrial efficacy, while its successful adaptation to subsequent mechanism upgrades and JD Food Delivery Ad further validates TUGB's superior generalization capability.

papers.title: The Role Of Recurrent Refinement In Medical Image Segmentation
papers.abstract: While feed-forward segmentation networks perform well on large cohorts, they degrade in constrained clinical settings with few training samples and imaging artifacts. Human vision, by contrast, remains robust under these conditions, a property partly attributed to the recurrent and feedback connectivity of the visual cortex, which refines visual information over time. Inspired by this, we append lightweight recurrent refinement blocks to segmentation backbones, namely Conditional Random Fields (CRFs), modern Hopfield networks and convolutional GRUs, and study their behaviour as the number of iterations increases at test time (including beyond the training horizon). Evaluated on two open-source datasets, Kvasir- SEG and ARCADE, our recurrent blocks add less than 1.5% parameters and yield gains on clean data (up to 1.4 pp) and under noise (up to 17 pp) while reducing HD95. Code is available at https://github.com/joaodsmarques/recurrencehelpsegmentation .

papers.title: AutoRefine: Auto-Calibrating Code Judges from Workflow Outcomes
papers.abstract: LLM judges increasingly serve as quality gates for code changes that have no test oracle, but a judge prompt must be calibrated for its task and recalibrated as the system it judges evolves, while hand labels for the calibration are resource intensive and go stale. Development workflows emit outcome labels for free (tests pass or fail, changes land or are abandoned), but these labels are noisy. We present AutoRefine, a loop that rewrites a deployable judge's prompt to reproduce outcome labels, with an informed teacher that sees the judge's input plus the outcome, explains each label it keeps, and abstains when the outcome cannot be explained from what the judge sees. On a held-out dataset with an execution oracle, calibration raised chance-corrected agreement (Scott's $\pi$) from 0.36 to 0.60. On a deployed agent's outcome labels, with 25\% flipped at random to introduce noise, the teacher set aside flipped \textsc{fail} labels at more than twice the rate of genuine ones, cutting overall label noise from 25\% to 20\%. Recalibrating that agent's judge using AutoRefine raised its agreement with merge/abandon outcomes on 17 independently held-out diffs from the current workflow ($\pi$ 0.16 to 0.51); on 16 diffs from older workflows, the previous judge stayed ahead, illustrating the need for recalibration as the agent evolves. By abstaining, the teacher not only removes noisy labels but also flags changes whose outcome the judge's input cannot explain, telling a team when a judge needs better inputs rather than a better prompt.

authors.name: James Poon
authors.institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Angular Besov Refinement of the Spherical Stein--Tomas Theorem
papers.abstract: The spherical Stein--Tomas inequality maps $L^2(\mathbb S^2)$ into $L^4(\mathbb R^3)$. We study its refinement in which the angular input is measured by the strictly weaker Besov norm $B^0_{2,4}(\mathbb S^2)$. The central separated-band inequality bounds the squared $L^2$ norm of the product of extensions from degrees $L\ll K$ by $C(L/K)$ times the squared input norms. An exact spherical-Hankel expansion controls the far field, while angular-momentum leakage and transversality handle the Fresnel region. We construct scale-separated, normalized angular bands for which the extension norm is equivalent to the $\ell^4$ norm of the coefficients. This proves that the fourth-power summation is optimal and quantitatively distinguishes the result from the classical $\ell^2$ summation. As an application, small angular Besov data generate small $L^4$ solutions to the cubic nonlinear Helmholtz equation in $\mathbb R^3$, with a smallness condition that remains sharp on multiscale data even when their $L^2$ norm is arbitrarily large or infinite. The associated on-shell nonlinear scattering amplitude has improved angular $B^0_{2,4/3}$ regularity, and its leading cubic term is quantitatively decoupled across widely separated angular bands.

papers.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.abstract: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.

authors.name: Rafael C. R. de Lima
authors.institution: Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina

authors.name: Pedro Martins Bailer
authors.institution: Universidade do Estado de Santa Catarina

papers.title: A Monte Carlo study of thermal conductivity in black phosphorene
papers.abstract: In this work the electronic thermal conductivity of black phosphorene is studied. Using the Monte Carlo method together with the Green-Kubo relations, a statistical modelling of the motion and scattering of electrons on acoustic and optical phonons is performed to estimate the electronic thermal conductivity. The scattering probability is expressed analytically. The obtained results show a pronounced anisotropy of the thermal conductivity: the thermal conductivity values along the armchair direction are an order of magnitude larger than those along the zigzag direction, in agreement with the experimental data for related materials. In addition, the modelling allowed a more rigorous justification of some results of previous theoretical works on the anisotropic thermal conductivity of black phosphorene.

papers.title: An Elementary Proof of the Binary Goldbach Conjecture
papers.abstract: We establish the binary Goldbach conjecture which asserts that every even positive integer greater than four can be expressed as a sum of two odd primes. This goal is achieved by proving that the number of ordered Goldbach pairs that add up to $2n$ is an $\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{n}{\ln^{2} n}\right)$ function. As an application, we provide a simpler verification of the ternary Goldbach conjecture that was first established in [6,7].

papers.title: Locating Contact on Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots From Tendon Measurements Alone via Constrained Moving Horizon Estimation
papers.abstract: Tendon-driven continuum robots can reach through constrained spaces, but contact along their bodies is invisible to the sensors at their motors. We show that this is a structural limitation rather than a tuning problem: the map from contact forces to tendon measurements has a null space of dimension at least seven, so no estimator that leaves the contact support free can locate contact. When the obstacle geometry is known, however, non-penetration and complementarity make the contact force locally identifiable, and we prove that the resulting system with unknown contact inputs is locally exponentially strongly detectable. We present a constrained moving horizon estimator (MHE) that encodes these conditions and runs in real time as one quadratic program per sample, and we give a local, mode-wise robust stability result for it. In a finite- element benchmark of a two-section robot pressing and sliding on a wall, the estimator located contact to 0.9 mm and estimated contact force to 0.22 N, compared with 65 mm and 0.72 N for a tuned extended Kalman filter (EKF) with state projection. The estimator tolerated millimeter- level errors in the obstacle position and unmodeled wall friction, under which the projected EKF failed. Under randomized model mismatch over 40 trials, including unmodeled tendon friction, it remained better in force and location in every trial. Without contact, the MHE offered no advantage over the EKF, which confirms that its benefit comes from the contact constraints. This report extends a letter submitted to IEEE Control Systems Letters with complete proofs and additional experiments.

authors.name: Haitham El-Hussieny
authors.institution: Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Efficient iterative methods for the nonlinear compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary condition
papers.abstract: In this study, we present a comparison of iterative methods for the compressible Reynolds equation with Navier slip boundary conditions, based on a fully compressible cavitation model for lubricated bearings. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the two-dimensional problem. We introduce the Kirchhoff transformation to reformulate the nonlinear density-pressure relationship into a quasi-linear problem. We develop an efficient numerical approach to solve the two-dimensional nonlinear problem. The methods examined are the Gauss-Seidel method, the Newton-Raphson method and parallelized nonlinear Jacobi method, applied to one- and two-dimensional slider bearing configurations. The overall solution time is shown to depend strongly on the choice of method.

papers.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
papers.abstract: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.

papers.title: Root sharing and $2$-adic interpolation for Legendre polynomials
papers.abstract: Stieltjes's conjecture on Legendre polynomials asserts that no two distinct Legendre polynomials can share a nonzero root. This question is, surprisingly, connected to a number of disparate mathematical areas. From the point of view of spectral geometry, this question concerns zero-sets of spherical harmonics. A disk counterpart to the conjecture is a famous theorem of Siegel on nonexistence of nonzero common roots of Bessel functions, proved using transcendence theory. A weak version of the conjecture is implied by the dynamical Mordell--Lang conjecture. We prove, using a $2$-adic analytic approach \`a la Skolem, that for a root $\alpha\neq 0$ of $P_l$ the set $\{n\in \mathbb{N}:\ P_n(\alpha)=0\}$ has cardinality at most $2l$. In particular, this set is finite.

papers.title: Additive $\Omega(\log^* OPT)$ Gap for Bin Packing with Three Items per Bin
papers.abstract: We prove that bin packing is NP-hard to approximate within an additive factor of $o(\ls\OPT)$, even when all item sizes are arbitrarily close to $1/3$. This gives the first lower bound for bin packing with an additive factor that depends explicitly on the optimum value. In addition, we give a polynomial-time reduction from any bin packing instance into one with item sizes arbitrarily close to $1/3$, preserving its additive configuration-LP gap up to constant factors. Thus, in the sense of additive configuration LP gap and up to a constant, we confirm the conjecture that 3-partition instances are the hardest bin packing instances. In particular, we obtain an unconditional $\Omega(\ls\OPT)$ gap for 3-partition instances. We build on the recent OpenAI construction that uses five items per bin and rules out any constant additive gap.

papers.title: Rotating Black Holes in Perfect Fluid Dark Matter: Horizons, Photon Orbits, and Shadows
papers.abstract: We investigate rotating black holes surrounded by perfect-fluid dark matter (PFDM), described by the parameter \(k\), and determine the Kerr-connected region of the \((a/M,k/M)\) parameter space that contains an event horizon. The critical value \(k_{\mathrm c}(a)\), obtained from the degenerate-horizon conditions \(\Delta(r_{\mathrm c})=\Delta'(r_{\mathrm c})=0\), defines the boundary between black-hole and horizonless configurations. We derive an exact parametric form of this extremal boundary and show that its near-Kerr behavior includes a logarithmic correction; therefore, \(k_{\mathrm c}/M\simeq2.8828(1-a/M)^{1.5377}\) is only an empirical fit over \(0.90\leq a/M\leq0.999\), not an asymptotic scaling law. For horizon-bearing solutions, we calculate unstable spherical photon orbits and the shadow's mean radius, area, and distortion, finding that increasing \(k/M\) shifts the photon region inward and reduces the shadow size. Backward ray tracing through a phenomenological optically thin disk, tested on independent \(41^2\), \(81^2\), and \(161^2\) image grids, confirms this trend: for \(a/M=0.9\) and an inclination of \(17^\circ\), the \(20~\mu\mathrm{as}\) beam-convolved ridge diameter decreases from \(42.47\) to \(37.88~\mu\mathrm{as}\) as \(k/M\) increases from 0 to \(0.08\), with the two finest grids agreeing to within \(0.5\%\). Thus, PFDM produces a consistent contraction from the horizon and photon region to the geometric shadow and image ridge, although these illustrative images do not provide an Event Horizon Telescope constraint because they lack a self-consistent emission model and interferometric likelihood analysis.

papers.title: Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories
papers.abstract: Personalized health coaching requires moving beyond retrospective wearable summaries toward quantitative, actionable behavioral prescriptions. We introduce Coachable Health Age (CHA), an interpretable health-age metric built from modifiable physiological and behavioral signals passively captured by consumer wearables. Across the WEAR-ME (N=2,780), All of Us (N=22,748), and longitudinal Fitbit (N=1,464) cohorts, CHA aligns with established cardiometabolic health constructs and improves prognostic discrimination for incident cardiovascular and metabolic disease beyond age, sex, and body mass index. To enable prospective behavioral optimization, we developed Sensor World Model (SensorWM), an action-conditioned wearable world model pretrained on over 2.2 million person-weeks of longitudinal sensor data from approximately 100,000 participants. SensorWM accurately forecasts multi-week physiological responses to candidate lifestyle changes ($R^2=0.664$), outperforming generic time-series foundation models while preserving downstream clinical signal for diabetes, hypertension, and other health outcomes. Finally, we integrate CHA and SensorWM into an agentic counterfactual coaching system to synthesize personalized 12-week coaching plans. In blinded paired reviews, certified lifestyle coaches preferred counterfactual-grounded plans over plans grounded in wearable history alone for overall quality (71.4%, P < 0.001) and anticipated adherence (71.0%, P < 0.001), and board-certified clinicians judged 99.2% of counterfactual-grounded plans to meet clinical safety criteria (vs. 97.6% of comparison plans). Automated evaluations across the full cohort (N=2,780) also favored counterfactual-grounded plans. By closing the loop between longitudinal tracking, trajectory prediction, and counterfactual coaching, our framework provides a scalable path to systematically improve cardiometabolic health.

papers.title: I Don't Care How You Hide It, I Care What You Do: Runtime Detection of Malicious ML Models
papers.abstract: Pre-trained machine learning (ML) models shared through public platforms can be weaponized to execute malicious payloads during loading or inference. Existing scanners prove inadequate for detecting malicious models as they rely on static analysis and function denylists, support limited serialization formats, and miss attacks that replace denylisted functions with equivalent alternatives, exploit unsupported loading paths, or abuse legitimate framework APIs. To address this problem, we present ModelShield, the first runtime behavioral detection system for malicious ML models that attributes observed system-level behavior to specific model operations. It combines application-level instrumentation of ML framework APIs with eBPF-based syscall tracing, tracking model behavior across spawned threads and processes to separate model-triggered activity from environment noise. Attributed syscall sequences are classified using 195 detection patterns mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques. We implemented ModelShield to support 17 ML frameworks and 36 formats. On an independent dataset, it is the only evaluated tool to achieve zero false positives, with false negatives limited to payloads that produce no malicious runtime behavior. It detected all 29 published evasion variants spanning function substitution, loading-path obfuscation, and TensorFlow API abuse, where no existing scanner achieved complete coverage. Across 145,000 models scanned from public platforms, it captured 41 malicious models on Hugging Face, including a reverse-shell payload and a payload that performed host reconnaissance and outbound exfiltration. Among these, ModelScan, PickleScan, Fickling, and ModelAudit detected only 29%, 56%, 80%, and 93%, respectively. Despite runtime overhead, ModelShield has a median analysis time of 12.3 seconds, with 90% of scans completing within 35.5 seconds, making it practical for hub-scale screening.

authors.name: Andrew Case
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Charlotte

papers.title: COMBIO: Automated Discovery of a Compact Composite Biomarker from Routine Laboratory Panels
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models based on routine laboratory panels can predict outcomes but can be difficult to interpret and operationalize. We present COMBIO, an automated pipeline that distils such a model into a compact closed-form biomarker. The composite is a product of laboratory measurements raised to integer powers from minus two to two. The sign of each exponent indicates whether higher values of the corresponding measurement increase or decrease the composite. Shapley additive explanation values from the gradient-boosted reference model rank five candidate measurements and guide eligible exponent signs. An exhaustive search over small integer exponents selects the formula on an inner validation set, before evaluation on the reserved test set. We evaluated COMBIO across six tasks: three National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey outcomes, liver-disease classification in the Indian Liver Patient Dataset, and Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV in-hospital mortality and sepsis case-finding, with external evaluation in the eICU Collaborative Research Database for the two hospital tasks. Across the six test sets, COMBIO's area under the receiver operating characteristic curve differed by at most 0.03 from logistic regression using the five candidate laboratory measurements. The hospital mortality composite had an area under the curve of 0.698 in the external database. A version restricted to widely available measurements in the source hospital database achieved an area under the curve of 0.786 in a cohort covering 92% of admissions. The multiplicative representation provides compactness rather than additional accuracy, and local validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

papers.title: Universal Decoding for Gaussian MIMO-ISI: Spherical Ensembles and Symmetric Neighborhoods
papers.abstract: We construct a universal decoder for cyclic Gaussian multiple-input multiple-output channels with intersymbol interference and unknown channel taps and spatial noise covariance. Codewords are drawn independently and uniformly from a sphere of fixed total energy. Under stated bounds on frequency variation, the decoder attains the ensemble-average error exponent of informed maximum-likelihood decoding for fixed channels and channels with growing memory. We approximate the frequency response by a constant matrix within each frequency block. For this auxiliary channel, every matched log-likelihood is affine in a common sufficient statistic. At fixed received output, we compute the statistic density of an independent competitor. The decoder selects the candidate with the smallest statistic density, equivalently minimizing a weighted sum of residual log-determinants. The density and its support volume give an upper bound on the universal competitor probability. Affinity ensures that at least half of a suitable symmetric neighborhood of the transmitted statistic has matched likelihood no smaller than that of the transmitted word. Integrating a density lower bound over this half gives the matched competitor bound. These bounds establish equality of error exponents, which a Gaussian channel comparison transfers to the original channel. The same decoder attains the matched exponent for independent frequency blocks with prescribed energies satisfying the stated conditions. For energies proportional to block length, an additional gain condition ensures that this exponent is at least that of the total-energy spherical ensemble.

papers.title: Layer-Peeling Inversion of Temporal Refractive Index Profiles from Noisy Data
papers.abstract: We introduce a direct method for reconstructing the temporal evolution of a medium from electromagnetic field measurements. A sequence of temporal refractive-index changes splits an incident wave into forward- and backward-propagating components, producing a \emph{spatial} response of finite extent. We show that this finite support, together with causality, enables sequential reconstruction of the temporal interfaces through a time-domain extension of layer peeling. For continuously varying media, we introduce a time-adjusted Goupillaud medium and, through space-time duality, establish the corresponding momentum-conservation and admissibility conditions. The method remains robust under incomplete and noisy measurements, providing a general framework for the metrology, characterization, and design of time-varying electromagnetic systems.

papers.title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
papers.abstract:
We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers.
  We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model.
  For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{\mu-1}/\mu$ for limiting average degree $\mu$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $\delta\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{\delta-1}/\delta$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $\delta\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.

papers.title: The k-Clique hypothesis is dead, for good
papers.abstract: We present an algorithm that solves the $k$-Clique problem for any large enough $k$ and any $n$-vertex graph in $n^{\left(\frac{\omega}{3}-c\right)k}$ time, where $\omega\geq 2$ is the matrix multiplication exponent and $c>0$ is a positive constant independent of both $\omega$ and $k$. This refutes the long-standing $k$-Clique conjecture, regardless of the value of the matrix multiplication constant, even if $\omega=2$. In fact, our algorithm solves the more general problem of counting weighted $k$-Cliques.

authors.name: Virginia Vassilevska Williams
authors.institution: MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory

papers.title: Supercuspidal and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}$ be a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of cardinality $q$, and let $(K_n)$ be a tower of principal congruence subgroups attached to a lattice $\mathcal{L}$ in the Lie algebra. We show that the proportion of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors carried by supercuspidal representations is $\delta_{\mathrm{ell}}(\Lambda)+O(q^{-n/4})$, where the elliptic density $\delta_{\mathrm{ell}}(\Lambda)>0$ is the probability that a random element of the dual lattice $\Lambda$ is nonzero on the Lie algebra of the unipotent radical of every proper parabolic subgroup. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$ this limit was anticipated by Howe. The error improves to $O(q^{-\tau n/4})$ with an explicit $\tau\in(1,2]$, except when $\mathrm{char}\,F=2$ and $\mathbf{G}$ has an isotropic direct factor which over $\bar F$ is a product of adjoint groups of type $\mathrm{B}_d$. We determine when $\delta_{\mathrm{ell}}(\Lambda)=1$, give an explicit bound uniform in $F$ for reductive models, and deduce a bound uniform over the completions of a global field. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis on congruence quotients, a quantitative Sard theorem for parabolic incidence maps and a Jacquet-module argument; it uses neither a classification of supercuspidal representations nor the exponential map.

papers.title: Video Stitching from Multiple Moving Cameras
papers.abstract: We address geometric video alignment for the same scene captured by multiple freely moving cameras. Existing methods, which are based on image stitching or video stabilization, are typically limited to two cameras or must assume the restrictive setting of a fixed linear ordering of the cameras. We propose MViS, a lightweight test-time optimization framework for joint multi-view alignment with temporal consistency. MViS uses a spatial-transformer-inspired net to jointly process frames from all views within a short temporal window and predict per-view, per-time homographies. Optimization proceeds in two stages: geometry-guided alignment followed by appearance-based refinement, with both stages enforcing multi-view and temporal consistency across the sequence. The method requires no scene-specific hyperparameter tuning, handles arbitrary and time-varying view-intersection graphs, and remains robust under rapid camera motion. On a standard two-view video benchmark, MViS matches or surpasses the state of the art. To facilitate evaluation in more complex scenarios, we introduce an annotated dataset with more than two freely moving cameras and establish the first benchmark for this setting. Project page: https://bgu-cs-vil.github.io/MViS-project/ .

papers.title: Stochastic AI Model Placement for AI-and-RAN Coexistence in 6G Networks
papers.abstract: This paper considers AI-service placement over geographically distributed RAN sites equipped with GPU resources partitioned into fixed, isolated multi-instance GPU (MIG) profiles. We propose C$^2$AIR, a chance-constrained optimization model that maximizes expected AI requests served while protecting uncertain RAN workloads and enforcing probabilistic capacity reliability requirements for admitted AI services. C$^2$AIR allows a service to run at multiple sites and accounts for discrete profile, memory, and GPU-slice constraints. We evaluate C$^2$AIR on a four-site deployment calibrated from NVIDIA Aerial RAN capacity figures and MLPerf Inference results, and on seven larger scenarios with up to 15 sites and 40 AI services, computing every violation and overload probability exactly from the demand distributions. C$^2$AIR keeps the RAN violation probability within its target at every hour of the day, whereas reserving for the mean RAN demand violates it in 24\% to 47\% of the intervals. The reliability condition prevents placing AI models that would be overloaded in 85\% of the intervals at an event hour, and multi-site replication serves 2.7 times more AI requests than single-site deployment. The evaluation also shows that coarse MIG instances and a heavy demand tail can make strict RAN protection expensive.

papers.title: Reconstructing intracell polarization with calibrated sapphire-window optics for collimated blue-light generation in a rubidium cell
papers.abstract: We study the polarization dependence of collimated blue light (CBL) generated near 420~nm by resonant four-wave mixing in thermal rubidium vapor in a sapphire-window cell driven at 780 and 776~nm. Sapphire windows can transform the polarization of pump light before it reaches the vapor, complicating the interpretation of polarization-dependent nonlinear emission. We measured the 780-nm pump Stokes state at an external before-cell reference plane to calibrate the common HWP/QWP preparation optics and recorded 266 off-resonant external output Stokes states after the complete sapphire-window rubidium cell at 90, 100, and 110~$^\circ$C in two propagation orientations. Direct paired-wavelength measurements show a mean before-cell 780/776 separation of $4.29^\circ$ and temperature- and orientation-specific complete-cell rotations of $22.20^\circ$--$32.02^\circ$, with rms residuals of $4.83^\circ$--$12.87^\circ$. Using this calibrated co-prepared pump description, we analyzed 2574 measurements of total spectrally filtered 420-nm CBL intensity. Across the six temperature--orientation data sets, a complete nine-coefficient second-order response yielded cross-validated $R^2$ values of 0.636 to 0.828. These paired-wavelength measurements establish, for each temperature--orientation data set, a fixed relative Stokes-space map between the two co-prepared pump trajectories, with the residual of this mapping defining the experimental uncertainty of the correlated two-pump reduction used in the response model. Thus, the resulting framework combines a reconstructed vapor-entrance polarization coordinate with direct two-wavelength calibration of the assembled cell and provides a practical basis for polarization-controlled nonlinear-optical experiments in sapphire-window vapor cells.

papers.title: Walsh Analysis in the Twenty-First Century: Convergence, Summability, Nonlinear Approximation, Universality, and Digital Applications
papers.abstract: Walsh analysis connects ordered Fourier convergence, summability, nonlinear approximation, and universal representation through a common character algebra. This survey examines developments from 2000-2026 against their classical foundations. Binary kernel geometry explains Hardy-space losses and summability thresholds; interval and packet methods control spectral selection; localized blocks produce correction and universal representations with distinct coefficient and exceptional-set requirements. Selected proofs and counterexamples compare these mechanisms and identify where an implication needs an additional hypothesis. The same distinctions organize digital integration, sparse measurements, Boolean spectra, and generalized Walsh bases. Quantitative thresholds, source conventions, and published theorem pointers are collected in comparative tables. The concluding problems separate source-listed questions, proposed refinements, and elementary obstructions. Supplementary derivations preserve normalization checks and finite covariance calculations while keeping the main exposition focused on the analytic mechanisms.

papers.title: TailDART: Compute-Efficient Foundation Models for Financial Time-Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Although time-series foundation models (TSFMs) achieve strong zero-shot transferability across high-information-density physical systems, applying overparameterized TSFMs to quantitative finance is fundamentally constrained by low signal-to-noise ratios, non-stationarity, and prohibitive autoregressive decoding latency. To reconcile representation learning with institutional operational constraints, this study presents TailDART, a dense 2.68 million-parameter foundation model engineered for financial time-series forecasting. By integrating grouped-query attention into a lightweight backbone, the architecture drastically reduces Key-Value cache memory bandwidth overhead, achieving major inference acceleration (up to 48.1%) over prevailing state-of-the-art TSFMs to enable low-latency, high-throughput streaming execution. Furthermore, multi-asset benchmarks across varying temporal resolutions show that a compact model can remain competitive for market forecasting: TailDART matches the predictive fidelity of substantially larger baselines while demonstrating superior error resilience in high-volatility regimes.

papers.title: Isometric Classification of Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the norm obtained by summing the $L^1$ norms of all weak derivatives through order $k$, including the function itself, determines both $n$ and $k$ on the real Sobolev space $W^{k,1}(\R^n)$. Every surjective linear isometry for this norm is given by a translation, a signed permutation of the coordinates and multiplication by a fixed sign $c\in\{-1,1\}$.

papers.title: Generalized and Classical Harnack Inequalities for semilinear equations on Carnot Groups
papers.abstract: We prove generalized and classical Harnack inequalities for non-negative smooth solutions of divergence-form semilinear subelliptic equations on Carnot groups. The proof combines smooth horizontal Gauss--Green and coarea formulas, energy estimates for level sets, a Vitali covering argument, and a horizontal Keller--Osserman barrier. The companion paper, Reference [10], develops the geometric foundations and extends the estimates to weak solutions with nonsmooth data.

papers.title: Medical Radioisotopes: Clinical Demand, Production Physics, and Untapped Pathways
papers.abstract: Over 40 radioisotopes are currently in use or under development across virtually all fields of modern medicine. Their availability relies on a complex interplay of nuclear physics, radiochemistry, and nuclear medicine. This review provides an isotope-by-isotope map of medically important radioisotopes from the perspective of these disparate yet complementary fields. We address the landscape grouped into three tiers: the established clinical core, including, familiar workhorses such as Tc-99m, F-18, Lu-177; an under-leveraged middle tier including Re-186, Re-188, and Sm-153, and the emerging frontier, radioisotopes with demonstrated but underutilised clinical promise such as Ac-225, At-211, Cu-67, and Sc-47. We discuss the properties of these radioisotopes with respect to clinical applications and their production pathways, as well as the associated nuclear and radiochemical challenges. We synthesise these disparate perspectives to identify situations in which alleviating production-side bottlenecks may improve access and patient outcomes.

authors.name: David McClain
authors.institution: United States Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases

papers.title: Medical Radioisotopes: Supply-chain Resilience, Distributed Production, and Access
papers.abstract: Over 50 million diagnostic procedures involving medical radioisotopes are performed per year and the number of therapeutic and theranostic agents continues to climb. Yet, the global supply chain is far from stable and many regions are underserved. This is the second of a Series of two review papers providing a comprehensive overview of the landscape of medically relevant radioisotopes. This paper focuses on the supply chain. It presents a critical overview of the 2025-2026 status quo, case studies of acute stressors and disruptions they caused, and methods in place to secure a stable supply. A literature-based analysis is paired with expert interviews. We argue that the ageing fleet of nuclear reactors currently used for the centralised production of many isotopes should be complemented by regional accelerator-based centres, alleviating single-point failures and cross-border logistics complications, and increasing access to short-lived isotopes in harder-to-reach regions and low- and middle-income countries.

authors.name: David McClain
authors.institution: United States Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases

papers.title: Laser-Direct-Written polymer WGM microring laser integrated on a fiber tip for refractive index sensing
papers.abstract: Whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) microlasers are promising for refractometric sensing, but their practical implementation can be limited by the need for stable resonator-coupler alignment. Here, we demonstrate a Rhodamine B-doped polymer WGM microring laser directly fabricated on an optical-fiber tip, eliminating the external resonator-fiber coupling interface at the sensing head. Micro-droplet coating and UV laser direct writing are combined for fabrication, while finite-difference time-domain simulations guide the microring laser design. The microlasers operate in air and water with thresholds of 0.224 uJ and 0.458 uJ, respectively. Refractometric measurements in aqueous glucose solutions yield a bulk refractive index sensitivity of 364.95 nm/RIU and a detection limit of 2.47 x 10^(-4) RIU. Water-induced polymer changes and photobleaching are also investigated. This fiber-tip architecture provides a basis for probe-based refractometric sensing in environmental and biochemical applications.

papers.title: As Easy as Rank One: Optimal Algorithms for Matroid Secretary and Single-Sample Matroid Prophet
papers.abstract:
We resolve the matroid secretary conjecture in its strong form and the single-sample matroid prophet inequality problem, achieving competitive ratios $e$ and $2$, respectively. Both ratios are optimal, even for rank-one matroids.
  For matroid secretary, our ordinal algorithm accepts the elements of the canonical optimum independently, each with probability $1/e$. It needs only the number of elements in advance and uses an expected polynomial number of independence queries on arrived elements. For single-sample matroid prophet inequalities, our algorithm uses one sample per independent value distribution and $O(n^2)$ independence queries on a known $n$-element matroid. It works for every arrival order fixed independently of the samples, values, and algorithmic randomness. The selected elements and their values have exactly the joint distribution obtained by independently retaining each element--value pair in the canonical optimum of a fresh product draw with probability $1/2$.
  Our main algorithms maintain a reference state whose greedy solution contains every accepted element. Its updates, made even after rejections, preserve exact distributional invariants. A short reversible-update argument gives a $4$-probability-competitive secretary algorithm, already resolving the original conjecture; a related invariant gives the optimal single-sample prophet inequality. For secretary, we characterize the distributions achievable by ordinal algorithms through a finite polytope. A continuous-time formulation then lets us design an accepted-set distribution achieving the optimal ratio $e$ and realize it efficiently. We also obtain guarantees for matroid intersections.

papers.title: Navigating Complexity: A User-Centered Evaluation of Project Management Tools
papers.abstract: In the age of digital transformation, companies are increasingly relying on specialized software to manage the complexity of projects. However, when selecting tools, features and costs often take precedence over user experience (UX), leading to low adoption rates, user frustration, and project delays. This study empirically evaluates the user experience of leading project management tools (Jira, Trello, Monday.com, Asana, and Microsoft Project) across various project scales using a mixed methods approach. The System Usability Scale (SUS) was used as the primary quantitative instrument, with data collected from 141 experienced professionals via online questionnaires. The results reveal a significant trade-off between functionality and usability. Trello achieved the highest SUS score (77.5), indicating a superior user experience for small projects and agile teams, while Microsoft Project scored the lowest (51.2), suggesting significant usability challenges despite its robust features. Jira demonstrated a balanced profile, offering powerful features with manageable complexity. Statistical analyses confirmed that the choice of the optimal tool is highly context dependent, with team size and project complexity influencing UX outcomes. The findings underscore that UX is not a secondary feature but a critical success factor for software acceptance and project effectiveness. This study provides an evidence-based framework for aligning tool selection with the project context, offers practitioners actionable insights, and identifies design opportunities for software developers.

papers.title: Consensus-Constrained Dual-Federated Optimization with Client-Side Dynamic Weighting for Distributed Android Device Threat Defense
papers.abstract: Smartphones, smart-home hubs, and wearables are increasingly exposed to sophisticated Android malware, while centralized threat-detection pipelines raise privacy and scalability concerns. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training without collecting raw client data, but partial participation and variation in local model quality can destabilize global optimization. In this article, we propose DW-FedADMM, a federated optimization framework that combines primal-dual coordination with performance-dependent client-side weighting. The dynamic coefficient modulates each participating client's local state before the augmented-Lagrangian update, while the dual variables regulate disagreement between local and global model states. We evaluate DW-FedADMM on three Android malware benchmarks, namely Drebin, Malgenome, and TUANDROMD, with 5, 10, and 15 clients holding IID data shards, partial client participation, and communication budgets of 5 and 10 rounds. Each configuration is repeated with ten random seeds. DW-FedADMM obtains the highest seed-averaged accuracy on Drebin (97.64% +/- 0.20%) and the best mean accuracy in 9 of the 18 dataset-client-round configurations, including 7 of the 9 configurations with a 10-round budget. Pooled over all configurations, it reaches 95.42% accuracy, 94.62% F1-score, 96.06% precision, and 99.45% AUC, compared with 95.32%, 94.51%, 95.56%, and 99.41% for FedADMM, while also giving the lowest mean false-positive rate and the smallest client update norm among the six compared methods. Both primal-dual methods are well ahead of the averaging- and proximal-based baselines on Malgenome and TUANDROMD, where the latter often remain at the majority-class solution when clients are fragmented. The gain of dynamic weighting over FedADMM is most pronounced on Drebin and with the longer communication budget, where it also reduces the variation across seeds.

papers.title: Autonomous Whole-body Loco-manipulation Using a Snake Robot
papers.abstract: Snake robots can leverage their hyper-redundant morphology for both locomotion and manipulation through distributed body contact but whole-body loco-manipulation is particularly challenging since the entire body serves simultaneously as propulsive mechanism and manipulation tool Prior work on wheeled legged and snake robot platforms has decoupled these functions through dedicated appendages body segmentation or grippers We present closed-loop loco-manipulation with our snake robot COBRA without this distinction such that any part of the body may make contact We develop a contact-implicit dynamic model unifying robot-ground robot-object and object-ground interactions within a Moreau-Jean time-stepping framework and formulate a trajectory optimization over the full-order dynamics guided by a geometric planner and nominal proportional controller to autonomously push an object to a goal location during sidewinding We validate the planner and controller on hardware across varied configurations and present simulation results for a simplified trajectory optimization that resolves robot-object and object-ground contacts

papers.title: Residential Vehicle-to-Grid Deployment: A United States-Based Stakeholder Perspective
papers.abstract:
The integration of vehicle-to-grid (V2G), in which electric vehicle (EV) owners can send electricity from their vehicles back to the grid, is an emerging solution to enhance grid resilience. However, V2G deployment in the United States lags behind many other countries. This can be attributed to a broad range of factors, and to investigate them, this study analyzes semi-structured interviews with stakeholders using inductive-deductive qualitative coding. Results from the interviews are coded across financial, technical, social, political, and organizational dimensions in order to understand the three main deployment factors of drivers, benefits, and barriers of V2G. Once coded, the relationships between these factors are used to construct a cognitive map to identify actions that will most effectively drive V2G deployment.
  The results indicate that grid resilience and decarbonization are seen as the main benefits of V2G. User willingness to participate, a lack of technological readiness and standardization, prohibitive costs, and unsupportive laws and policies are among the most frequently cited barriers. Connections in the cognitive map indicate that the most closely related drivers for mitigating these barriers are user compensation for battery degradation, community outreach, the creation of grid interconnection standards and protocols, and supportive grants and policy frameworks for V2G piloting and adoption.

authors.name: Nora Agah
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

authors.name: Javad Mohammadi
authors.institution: Ahvaz Jundishapur University of Medical Sciences

papers.title: StarLoc: A Practical Approach to Encoding Geographic Locators in IPv6 for Starlink
papers.abstract: LEO satellite networks such as Starlink provide Internet connectivity across continents, oceans, and airspace. IP geolocation providers map Starlink's IPv6 prefixes to locations mainly through its self-published GeoFeed. However, users may be far away from their assigned Points of Presence (PoPs), one label covers an entire prefix, and labels and PoP mappings can change while addresses stay the same. We characterize Starlink's IPv6 addressing using 925 historical GeoFeed snapshots (2024--2026), one year of PoP mappings, and over 7.9 million observed IPv6 addresses. Our findings reveal that customer prefixes lack clear geographic structure, prefix labels lie a median of 540km from their PoPs, and relabeling a single /40 can affect the reported locations of up to 65,536 possible /56 delegations. To address these challenges, we propose StarLoc, a geographic Locator--Identifier separation scheme that embeds terminal location into IPv6 addresses using a resolution-adaptive H3 Locator while preserving existing Starlink prefixes, /56 delegations, and stable Endpoint Identifiers. To balance accuracy and privacy, StarLoc reveals only cells with at least a certain number of terminals, and operators can cap resolution in sensitive regions or withhold location entirely. Unlike topology-based schemes, StarLoc encodes physical location and lets Locators follow moving users.

authors.name: Jinwei Zhao
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Alignment by Confident Debate: Preference Learning from Multi-Agent Debate
papers.abstract: Post-training language models for reasoning typically rely on gold answers, task-specific verifiers, or learned reward models, limiting scalability when such signals are scarce. Multi-agent debate offers a self-supervised alternative, but converting debate into reliable training supervision remains challenging: majority voting weights agreeing responses equally, lacks a principled tie-breaking rule, and is ill-defined for open-ended tasks without a canonical answer; likelihood-based scoring can conflate fluency with correctness; and homogeneous committees may reinforce correlated errors. We introduce Alignment by Confident Debate (AbCD), which converts debate traces into preference data without gold answer labels. A sampling-diverse committee debates each problem, after which final answers are clustered by task-level semantic equivalence. We use verifiable tasks (mathematical reasoning, multiple-choice quantitative QA, and executable code-generation) as a controlled test bed: their answer keys or executable checkers let us evaluate the quality of debate-derived supervision against ground truth, even though the oracle itself never uses gold labels. Post-training on the resulting preferences outperforms inference-only ensembling and debate, as well as SFT on the same traces, across five model families spanning 1B to 8B parameters and four datasets, improving consensus accuracy, with a maximum gain of $21.5_{pp}$. Ablations show that the approach transfers to a larger model and to code generation, while also revealing limitations of heterogeneous committees and agreement-based weighting. Overall, the results suggest that debate traces can yield useful preference supervision when answer equivalence is combined with confidence-weighted disagreement.

papers.title: From Procedures to Permissions: Learning Precise Subagent Authorization from Agent Skills
papers.abstract: As language agents tackle increasingly complex tasks, they increasingly rely on multiple agents to coordinate specialized work, requiring decisions not only about what each subagent should do but also which tools and workspace resources it should access. Existing agent systems provide mechanisms for controlling tools and execution environments, but do not directly specify the resources required by each delegated subtask. Moreover, task outcomes and execution trajectories alone provide limited supervision for determining whether a subagent has received appropriate permissions. We observe that Agent Skills encode procedural knowledge describing the operations, tools, and files required at each step, providing a natural source of supervision for authorization. Building on this observation, we synthesize tasks and step-by-step procedures from Skills, execute them through subagent delegation in interactive environments, and use verified trajectories to construct training data for task execution and authorization. On ClawArena-Team, our method improves tool permission precision by 13.4 percentage points and workspace permission precision by 24.1 percentage points, while increasing overall task success by 11.6 percentage points for Qwen3.5-35B-A3B. On Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SkillsBench, our method remains competitive with existing agent data synthesis approaches. These results show that the procedural knowledge embedded in Agent Skills provides a source of supervision for precise subagent orchestration that task outcomes alone cannot provide.

authors.name: Wentao Zhang
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Two-Layer Evolutionary Scheduling for Machine Learning Jobs in Multi-Cluster Environments
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of large-scale machine learning (ML) workloads has led to unprecedented demands on GPU cluster scheduling systems. However, existing heuristic schedulers struggle to handle the complexity and dynamics of multi-cluster GPU environments, often leading to load imbalance, long queuing delays, and poor alignment to business objectives. This paper formulates the ML scheduling problem in multi-cluster GPU environments as online multi-objective optimization that minimizes the average and maximum weighted queuing times while maximizing GPU time utilization. To solve this optimization problem, we propose EVO-GP, a two-layer evolutionary online scheduling method that decouples global job-to-cluster allocation from intra-cluster GPU resource allocation. At the job-to-cluster allocation layer, an evolutionary algorithm assigns arriving jobs to feasible clusters to promote load balance across clusters. At the resource allocation layer, a priority function automatically learned offline via genetic programming is used to rank jobs and guide GPU allocation within each cluster. Extensive experiments on both real-world data and simulated workloads demonstrate that the proposed EVO-GP method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, while maintaining superior adaptability and scalability.

authors.name: Xin Yao
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Auditing Grasp Feasibility Predictors with Planner-Verified Counterfactuals
papers.abstract: Grasp-feasibility predictors report near-perfect accuracy on Task and Motion Planning benchmarks, but high accuracy on these benchmarks does not verify that a predictor uses the collision geometry that the motion planner checks. We propose a planner-verified counterfactual (CF) test: holding the grasp pose fixed, we insert a solid obstacle into the approach corridor, add its points to the model input, and let a planner re-derive the label, which flips from feasible to infeasible. Across eight predictors spanning point clouds, voxels, depth, and object tokens, CF-pair AUROC falls from high natural AUROC (0.920-0.996) to chance (0.470-0.504), and the flip holds across four planners, two arms, and a real-object obstacle. Predictors fail at different resolutions, from a bounding box to a 12.5 cm voxel. In the point-cloud models we dissect, the obstacle either moves the representation in a direction unrelated to whether it blocks the grasp or is not registered at all. A clearance-aware read of the corridor points, trained on the unmodified benchmark with no counterfactual scenes, reaches 0.983 CF-pair AUROC, but it remains bound to its trained obstacle placements; a placement-invariant clearance representation is still open. We release the counterfactual labels, metrics, datasheet, and relabeling pipeline at https://github.com/codewithsajid/graspfc-cf.

authors.name: Girish Varma
authors.institution: International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad

papers.title: The Localization Scale of the Block Anderson Model in One Dimension at Arbitrary Coupling and Volume
papers.abstract: We study the one-dimensional block Anderson model with independent $W\times W$ Gaussian unitary ensemble potentials and deterministic nearest-neighbor hopping, with hopping-to-disorder ratio $g$. The system consists of $L$ blocks, with total dimension $N=WL$. As $W\to\infty$, we identify the bulk localization length, up to an arbitrarily small power of $W$, with $\min\{N,\max\{W,W^2g^2\}\}$, uniformly for deterministic couplings $g\ge0$ and cycle lengths $L\ge3$. For every fixed $D>0$ and all sufficiently large $W$, the expected fraction of eigenvectors in the selected energy interval satisfying these bounds is at least $1-W^{-D}$. In polynomial volume the bounds hold simultaneously for all eigenvectors in that interval with probability at least $1-W^{-D}$. The localization length is the number of coordinates in the shortest cyclic interval containing at least half of an eigenvector's mass.

authors.name: Jun Yin
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning: A Multi-Objective Framework for Learning Local Distance Functions in Nearest Neighbor Classification
papers.abstract: Nearest neighbour classifiers inherit the geometry of their distance function. Fixed distances and globally learned metrics apply the same geometry throughout the input space, although relevant feature directions may vary across regions. We propose EAML (Evolutionary Adaptive Metric Learning), a framework that learns instance-dependent positive-definite metrics through a low-dimensional parameterization. Each local metric combines an input-dependent diagonal scaling, generated by softmax interpolation between anchor points, with a global low-rank correlation component. A real-coded elitist genetic algorithm optimizes the parameters using a scalar objective combining leave-one-out prediction error, robustness, metric smoothness, and regularization. We establish positive definiteness, metric equivalence, existence of an optimal solution, and Lipschitz continuity of the metric field. We further investigate prediction stability, generalization bounds, and evolutionary convergence under explicit assumptions. Experiments on synthetic data with region-dependent feature relevance show that EAML can recover local metric variations and outperform global metrics. Evaluation on thirteen public datasets using nested 5-fold cross-validation reveals a more nuanced picture: EAML improves performance on selected datasets but does not significantly outperform global metric baselines overall. Additional experiments show that global diagonal metrics can be preferable under nuisance features and test-time noise. These findings identify the conditions under which evolutionary local metric learning is beneficial and highlight its practical limitations.

papers.title: Surrogate Quality Score: A Novel Composite Performance Metric for Model Selection
papers.abstract: The growing reliance on high-fidelity, state-of-the-art machine learning based models for engineering decision-making necessitates robust and systematic approaches for model selection. While high predictive accuracy at untrained points is a necessary trait in the final model, other attributes such as model complexity, forecastability, explainability, scalability, and physics-awareness may be equally important or relevant criteria depending on application context and user requirements. In this work, we propose a novel composite performance metric, Surrogate Quality Score (SQS) for model selection based on predictive accuracy and model complexity simultaneously. SQS heuristically integrates these two attributes through a weighted product of normalized measures, yielding a unified score to reflect overall model quality. A user-specified parameter in SQS enables explicit control over the accuracy-complexity trade-off, thereby incorporating human judgement and preference in the model selection process. We extensively discuss and justify the formulation of SQS and demonstrate its utility through an illustrative example. By combining predictive accuracy and model complexity, SQS offers a systematic and objective approach for model selection based on both attributes.

papers.title: FasterRW: An Efficient Prior-Assisted Random Walk Solver for Thermal Analysis
papers.abstract: Thermal simulation is becoming increasingly critical in modern IC design and manufacturing. Feynman--Kac random walk methods can estimate localized temperatures without solving the global field, but in practical settings without Dirichlet boundaries they require very long paths to control the truncation residual. This paper presents FasterRW, a continuation-value framework for accelerating Feynman--Kac thermal random walks. We prove a stopping-time residual identity showing that the expected tail after truncation equals the current attenuation weight multiplied by the temperature at the stopping location. This identity enables a prior-corrected single-point estimator: a cheap, noisy prior replaces the unknown continuation value, making the truncation bias scale with prior error rather than absolute temperature and yielding an error-controlled threshold-selection rule. For multi-point queries, FasterRW further converts cross-query pass-through tails into pseudo-samples and refines the resulting observations in prior-error coordinates through kriging. Compared with prior state-of-the-art methods, FasterRW achieves up to $28\times$ acceleration while maintaining accuracy. Our code is open-sourced at https://github.com/ShiningSord/FastRW.

authors.name: Zixiao Wang
authors.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

authors.name: Tianshu Hou
authors.institution: Chengdu University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: ResQAdam: Residual-Preserving Adaptive Optimization for Memory-Efficient Quantization Aware Training
papers.abstract: Quantization-aware training (QAT) is the most reliable way to obtain accurate low-bit large language models (LLMs), but training with AdamW keeps two dense FP32 states for every weight matrix. We find that low-rank memory-efficient optimizers such as GaLore and LDAdam degrade substantially in QAT. A considerable part of the QAT momentum lies outside its top-r singular subspace, and projection-based methods discard this part at every step. We further observe that this residual remains useful when only its sign is kept. Based on these observations, we propose ResQAdam. It keeps a single BF16 momentum, applies Adam only to the r x r coordinates of the principal subspace, and adds a normalized sign update computed from the residual. We evaluate ResQAdam with two from-scratch QAT methods and three QAT fine-tuning pipelines, with weights quantized down to 2 bits. It reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW, stays close to AdamW in most settings, and lowers training throughput by less than 2%.

authors.name: Shengkun Tang
authors.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

authors.name: Lin Zhao
authors.institution: Northwest Institute of Eco-Environment and Resources

papers.title: Resolvent-Diagonal Energy of Isospectral Jacobi Matrices
papers.abstract: We study the minimum squared resolvent diagonal among Jacobi matrices with prescribed eigenvalues. For the zeros of $P_n^{(\alpha,\beta)}$, we construct a canonical realization and bound its asymptotic cost against the optimum. Its rescaled inverse converges to the Green operator of a reflection-symmetric singular Schr\"odinger operator with Bessel-zero spectrum. A Green-coordinate identity places this construction and all finite realizations in the same density framework. Mass-constrained spectral problems then give computable lower bounds. The bounds meet at $\alpha=1/2$, with optimal energy $2/15$, and have first-order contact with derivative $-13/75$. We classify the constrained extremal profiles and the three endpoint geometries of the canonical density. Two polynomial families with the same limiting edge spectrum have different limiting optimal energies. For Nesterov momentum $(s-1)/(s+1)$, the optimal leading endpoint Hessian-drift gain among nonnegative-link Jacobi realizations is $\sqrt{2}$ times the original gain. An explicit isospectral flow strictly improves the standard one-sided realization for $\alpha>-1/2$, $\alpha\ne1/2$.

authors.name: Dmitry Pasechnyuk-Vilensky
authors.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

authors.name: Martin Takac
authors.institution: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Erratum to: Monotonicity of Ursell functions in the Ising model
papers.abstract: In this note, we correct an error in the proof Theorem 1 of Comm. Math. Phys. 401 (2023), 2459-2482.

papers.title: CucumberVision at the Edge: Accuracy, Throughput, and Energy of RGB-D Cucumber Sizing on Jetson Orin Nano and Raspberry Pi 4
papers.abstract: Non-contact fruit sizing from RGB-D imagery reaches sub-centimetre accuracy on workstation hardware, but in-field grading requires the same pipeline to run on a low-power single-board computer, and the cost of that transition is rarely reported. We deploy a curvature-aware cucumber length-measurement pipeline (YOLO26n detection, prompt-based segmentation and a medial arc spline estimator) on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano and a Raspberry Pi 4, and characterize both against an RTX 3050 Ti workstation by replaying 50 identical greenhouse captures of 7 specimens, with specimen-level cluster-bootstrap statistics. Accuracy is preserved: mean absolute error (MAE) is 0.58 cm (95% CI 0.46-0.69) on both the workstation and the Jetson at matched precision, with a paired difference of zero. TensorRT FP16 compilation cuts Jetson detection latency 2.57x, giving two operating points on one board: 72 ms per fruit at 0.84 cm, or 2.74 s at 0.64 cm. Four ablations map the design space. For prompted segmentation backends, measurement accuracy is fixed by the backend and reproduces across platforms to within 0.01 cm, while its cost is fixed by the platform and varies 214x, so the two choices are separable. Whole-graph INT8 quantization of the NMS-free detection head fails structurally, returning no detections, because one output tensor carries both pixel coordinates and confidences; we show that no calibration strategy can avoid this. Excluding the head restores function at 1.37x. Energy per fruit is 42.2 J on the Jetson, and its 7 W mode consumes 73% more than its 15 W mode. The Raspberry Pi with MobileSAM costs 2.5x more per fruit than the Jetson with SAM despite drawing 47% less power, and it runs without thermal throttling under sustained load. The results define an accuracy-throughput-energy envelope with three non-dominated configurations and give rules for selecting among them.

authors.name: Rajmeet Singh
authors.institution: Khalifa University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. Because population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, we focus on mitigating the downstream effects of finite-rollout variation. We propose \emph{Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO)}, which conditions within-prompt robust reweighting on observed vote reliability to make updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative. We further introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce self-supervised forgetting during online adaptation. Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.
