Building on this insight, we propose Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention (HASA), a training-free sparse attention framework that jointly adapts selection resolution along these two dimensions. Along the feature dimension, the singular spectrum of each head's query-key operator determines an effective rank, yielding a compact, head-specific response space. Along the sequence dimension, neighboring regions are progressively merged according to the directional coherence of their token responses in this same space, while heterogeneous regions remain separate. Exact attention is then computed using the original full-dimensional KV states of the selected regions. HASA captures 88.1% of dense-attention mass and, compared with UNIQUE, a strong recent sparse-attention baseline, improves accuracy by up to 3.47 and 2.57 points on RULER and LongBench-Pro, respectively, and accelerates self-attention by up to 1.32x, while achieving up to 14.07x speedup over dense attention.

authors.name: Yu Wen
authors.institution: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China

papers.title: ReKV: Overlapping Quantized KV Transfer and Suffix Recomputation
papers.abstract: Prefill--decode disaggregation moves a prompt's key--value (KV) cache between workers before the first token can be generated. Reducing this handoff to either cache compression or recomputation misses a useful choice: which layers to transmit, at what precision, and which layers to execute again on the decode worker. ReKV transfers a quantized prefix KV cache and one BF16 boundary state, then reconstructs a contiguous suffix while the prefix is in flight. In a model-shaped synthetic benchmark on cross-node H100s, the Q8 configuration meeting separately evaluated quality criteria reduces 8K handoff latency by $2.36\times$, $2.84\times$, and $3.65\times$ over BF16 transfer for Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-3B, and Qwen3-8B. It is also faster than the best measured transfer-only or recompute-only action at those points. A separate real-weight BF16 recomputation experiment reduces prefill-to-token-return time by $1.16$--$1.63\times$. The preferred action changes with prompt length and link bandwidth.

papers.title: Dynamics of subcritical threshold solutions for the three-dimensional energy-critical NLS
papers.abstract: We extend the radial threshold classification of Duyckaerts and Merle on the lower kinetic branch to nonradial solutions of the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation in \(\dot H^1(\mathbb R^3)\). At the ground state energy and with initial gradient norm strictly below that of the ground state, every solution is global and either scatters in both time directions or is a symmetry transform of the special solution \(W^-\), possibly after conjugate time reversal. The proof combines Su and Zhao's below-threshold scattering theorem with a coercivity estimate for the interaction form at threshold under a kinetic gap and a local analysis near the ground state orbit.

papers.title: Regular multi-types and the Bloom conjecture II
papers.abstract: Let $M\subset\mathbb{C}^n$ $(n\geq2)$ be a smooth pseudoconvex real hypersurface. We prove that, for every $1\leq s\leq n-1$, the regular $s$-contact type, the $s$-commutator type, and the $s$-Levi type coincide at every point of $M$, thereby resolving Bloom's conjecture in any dimension. The solution in dimension three was obtained in 2021 by the second and the third authors. Moreover, for any smooth rank $s$ subbundle $B\subset T^{1,0}M$, we establish the equality of the commutator type and the Levi type associated with $B$, giving an affirmative answer to the generalized D'Angelo conjecture.

papers.title: PRISM: Primitive Routing via In-context Skill Mixing for Retentive VLA Adaptation
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models promise a single language-conditioned policy adaptable to many manipulation behaviors, yet deployment additionally requires skill retention and long-horizon composition: a policy must retain previously acquired skills and reuse them inside composite tasks whose behavior changes across phases. The standard recipe absorbs every new task into one shared update, which provides neither a parameter-level locus for reusable skills nor a mechanism for invoking each skill along the trajectory. We observe that this missing structure is latent rather than absent: per-skill low-rank updates of a pretrained VLA occupy a robustly distinguishable, low-dimensional subspace, and a single composite-task LoRA concentrates roughly half of its Frobenius energy in this subspace, against a near-zero matched random-rotation control. Building on this geometry, we introduce PRISM, which represents reusable skills as parameter-level primitives: each skill family is stored as a dedicated low-rank action-expert adapter in a primitive bank, primitives are augmented with skill-specific low-rank residuals and composed at inference by a per-chunk VLM-conditioned router that reads the prefix representation to track task progress, and the router is supervised by per-chunk labels from a deterministic, task-conditioned, action-derived oracle. During composite training, the vision encoder, the language LoRA, the skill residuals, the router, and the shared action projections and time MLP are updated; every primitive is held frozen, so the base per-skill action-expert adapters are preserved by construction. On RoboCasa365, PRISM achieves 56.43% atomic-skill success and reaches 20.00% on long-horizon composite tasks, while a standard $\pi_{0.5}$-LoRA two-stage fine-tune reaches 17.86% atomic and 17.50% composite success. We additionally validate PRISM on an AgileX PIPER real-robot setup.

authors.name: Jiachen Tao
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Upper bound on the size of subgraphs avoiding cycles of girth length in graphs
papers.abstract: A graph $G$ is said to be $H$-free if it contains no copy of $H$. The generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$, a natural extension of the classical Tur\'{a}n number, is defined as the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free spanning subgraph of $G$. Although $\mathrm{ex}(G, H)$ has been extensively studied for various specific graphs $G$, such as hypercubes, complete transposition graphs, and doubled Johnson graphs, very few results are known for general graphs. For a graph $G$ of girth $g$, let $C_{g}$ denote the cycle of length $g$. In this paper, we investigate the generalized Tur\'{a}n number $\mathrm{ex}(G, C_{g})$ for graphs $G$ in which every edge is contained in a fixed number of $g$-cycles, and establish a general upper bound on it. This bound generalizes the classical results on hypercubes and provides a unified approach for general graphs. Furthermore, we apply this bound to derive explicit upper bounds for several specific graphs, including $K_{n,n,\ldots,n}$, $K_{n}\times K_{n}$, $C_{m}\times C_{n}$, $S_{n}$, $AG_{n}$, $CT_{n}$ and $J(n;k,k+1)$.

papers.title: A Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull characterization of inner-product spaces via Birkhoff--James orthogonality
papers.abstract: The classical location problem posed by Weber [\"Uber den Standort der Industrien,T\"ubingen: J. C. B. Mohr, 1909] has motivated various geometric characterizations of inner-product spaces. Ben\'itez, Fern\'andez and Soriano [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{354} (2002), 5027--5038] characterized real inner-product spaces through the convex-hull property of Fermat--Torricelli medians.Pakhrou [J. Funct. Anal. \textbf{285} (2023), 110078] further established a characterization using $\gamma$-centers and equilateral triangles. Building on these results, we show that the Fermat--Torricelli convex-hull criterion remains valid when restricted to triples satisfying a one-sided Birkhoff--James orthogonality condition.The proof combines norming functionals, radial rescaling,Alexandrov differentiability, and the area formula.No completeness, smoothness, or strict convexity assumptions are required.

papers.title: A hybrid model for zero-inflated proportion data
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a hybrid model for analyzing zero-inflated proportion data by distinguishing two types of zeros. The first type arises from sampling variability, whereas the second reflects intrinsically unsuitable covariates. Accordingly, the hybrid model combines a regression component for suitable observations with an estimator of the suitability region that identifies unsuitable covariates. Using a debiasing technique, we establish the consistency of both the regression and classification components, together with the asymptotic normality of the regression coefficient and a convergence rate for the support estimator. Comprehensive simulation studies verify our theoretical findings. We further apply the model to two real datasets, where it outperforms most competing methods.

papers.title: On two examples of topological gyrogroups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct an infinite-dimensional topological gyrogroup that fails to be strongly topological. We equip the countable direct sum of the complex unit disk with a carefully weighted infinite series of component seminorms. By dividing the infinite-dimensional operation into a finite core and a bounded infinite tail, we rigorously prove the joint continuity of the M\"obius addition, confirming the space is a valid topological gyrogroup. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the gyroautomorphisms exhibit unbounded expansion under this real seminorm topology, explicitly preventing the existence of an invariant neighborhood basis at the identity. This provides a clear, analytic counterexample separating general topological gyrogroups from strongly topological ones. Moreover, we construct a topological gyrogroup which is not strongly topological but it contains a non-trivial strong subgyrogroup.

authors.name: Meng Bao
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Architecture and Technology

papers.title: Polarization calibration of fisheye cameras using skylight in the wild
papers.abstract: Skylight polarization provides directional cues for robotic navigation, but fisheye lens effects and analyzer imperfections can degrade polarization measurements across the field of view. We present a joint lens-analyzer calibration method that explicitly models incidence-dependent lens transmission together with analyzer gains and angular offsets in a unified eight-parameter formulation. Given known geometric calibration, rotations between camera frames can be estimated using visual features and cross-frame directional polarized light consistency can be used for polarization calibration. Therefore, our calibration approach requires only a short handheld outdoor sequence under natural skylight, without dedicated polarization calibration equipment or a predefined sky polarization model. On real-world outdoor sequences, the proposed method achieves a weighted cross-frame angle-of-linear-polarization (AoLP) mean absolute error below 0.5{\deg} across all incidence angles, with a 73.4% reduction in the 80{\deg}-90{\deg} incidence angle region, and generalizes to an independent sequence with an overall mean absolute error of 0.466{\deg} without refitting. Preliminary solar-azimuth experiments using a camera mounted on a quadruped robot further show improved alignment with the visible solar center, supporting the potential of calibrated AoLP measurements for relative-heading estimation and future polarization--inertial navigation. The calibration software tool will be released upon acceptance of this paper.

papers.title: A virtual element exterior calculus framework
papers.abstract: We develop a conforming virtual element framework for differential forms on general polytopal meshes in arbitrary dimension and at arbitrary order. Recursive local Hodge-Laplace boundary value problems define a trimmed virtual de Rham complex, from which moment constraints yield a complete subcomplex. The local spaces of these two complexes contain the trimmed and complete polynomial spaces of differential forms, respectively, and admit unisolvent degrees of freedom and computable polynomial projections. The canonical interpolants commute with the exterior derivative, and both complexes have cohomology isomorphic to that of the continuous de Rham complex. For both virtual families, we establish negative-norm inverse estimates and mesh-uniform norm equivalences in all form degrees. We further derive canonical interpolation error bounds and discrete Poincar'e inequalities. As an application, we obtain an inf-sup stable mixed Hodge-Laplace method with harmonic variables and optimal-order convergence under sufficient regularity. Moreover, the two conforming complexes are cochain isomorphic to their fully discrete counterparts (J. Eur. Math. Soc., 2025, doi:10.4171/JEMS/1602), and the norm equivalences provide a key analytical bridge between the conforming and fully discrete formulations.

papers.title: An Explicit Equation for the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Character Variety of $\mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$
papers.abstract: Let $N$ denote the closed non-orientable surface of Euler characteristic $-1$, i.e. the connected sum of three real projective planes $N = \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2 \# \mathbb{RP}^2$, with fundamental group presented as $\langle A,B,C \mid A^2 B^2 C^2 = I \rangle$ via the standard symmetric cross-cap model. Building on the classical trace-coordinate methods of Fricke, Vogt, and Goldman for free groups, and on the qualitative study of representation varieties of non-orientable surfaces by Benyash-Krivets and Chernousov, we give an explicit affine equation for a dense open piece of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ GIT character variety $X(N)$. We prove that the trace coordinates $a = \mathrm{tr}(A)$, $b = \mathrm{tr}(B)$, $c = \mathrm{tr}(C)$, $p = \mathrm{tr}(AB)$ satisfy the polynomial relation $c^2 = abp - a^2 - b^2 + 4$, that this hypersurface is smooth and irreducible, and that on the open locus $c \neq 0$ it is isomorphic to the image of $X(N)$ under the trace map, with the remaining trace coordinates $\mathrm{tr}(BC)$, $\mathrm{tr}(CA)$, $\mathrm{tr}(ABC)$ recovered as regular functions on this locus. We further identify the boundary locus $c = 0$ with representations satisfying the matrix identity $A^2 B^2 = -I$, and describe its representation-theoretic structure, while leaving a complete global classification along this locus as an open problem. All key trace identities are proved from Cayley-Hamilton first principles and independently checked numerically against explicit matrices.

authors.name: Yinxi Chen
authors.institution: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University

papers.title: DKWBC: Decoupling Motion Tracking and Balancing for Humanoid Whole-Body Control
papers.abstract: Humanoid whole-body control requires a robot to track diverse reference motions while maintaining balance under gravity, torque limits, contact switching, and external disturbances. Existing reinforcement-learning-based trackers typically learn control outputs that jointly address motion tracking and balance. However, similar reference poses can correspond to substantially different dynamic demands, requiring a unified policy to learn motion-dependent control requirements alongside balance corrections. This can complicate learning and lead to high-frequency fluctuations in control outputs. We propose DKWBC, a dynamics-informed whole-body control framework that combines explicit model-based tracking with a learned balancing residual. Inspired by the model-based and environmental-wrench contributions to joint torques in floating-base dynamics, DKWBC uses inverse-dynamics feedforward and joint PD feedback to supply tracking torques, while a residual policy learns additional joint-torque corrections for balanced execution. By explicitly accounting for motion-dependent torque demands, this structure simplifies the policy's learning task. Experiments in simulation and on real hardware demonstrate that a single learned balancing policy generalizes across motion datasets while maintaining accurate motion tracking and balance across ground support, attached payloads, and physical interaction. Project page: https://robbyant-research.github.io/DKWBC/.

authors.name: Xueyang Wang
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xing Zhu
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Quantum Matter

papers.title: How balloons lose their charge by collecting ions from the air
papers.abstract: The air we breathe contains radioactive particles. Each time one of these particles decays, it creates hundreds of thousands of ionized air molecules. These ions make the air conductive, which is one reason insulated surfaces lose charge over time. Here we observe the discharge of two statically charged balloons by measuring the repulsive force between them over time. The initial rates of charge loss are relatively large, especially at higher humidities. This large rate of charge loss is likely dominated by the emission of water ions from the balloons surface. Approximately 1 hour after charging, the charge loss rates are much smaller and agree with predictions calculated from the radon concentration in the air and the size of the room, for reasonable aerosol concentrations.

papers.title: Segmenting Geometric Textures of 3D Meshes
papers.abstract: Recognizing geometric texture patterns on 3D models is critical for applications such as heritage protection, model editing, and 3D printing. Existing 3D model segmentation methods predominantly focus on identifying high-level semantic parts, thereby failing to capture middle-level textures. While recent Vision-Language Models can perform image segmentation with appropriate text prompts, they still struggle to recognize 3D geometric textures. In this work, we present a method that segments 3D mesh models based on middle-level geometric textures. We further introduce a new geometric texture segmentation benchmark and fine-tune SAM3 accordingly. The segmented texture regions are then clustered based on DINO feature similarity and lifted from 2D to 3D. Additionally, we develop an interactive tool to enable both 3D model editing based on our segmentation results and model retrieval from the dataset based on geometric and texture similarity. Experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing methods in segmenting geometric textures and can facilitate various applications.

authors.name: Shihao Feng
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: P\'osa-type resilience for Hamilton Berge cycles in random hypergraphs
papers.abstract:
We prove a degree-sequence resilience theorem for Hamilton Berge cycles in random uniform hypergraphs. For every fixed integer $k\ge3$ and every $\gamma>0$, there exists $C=C(k,\gamma)>0$ such that if $C\log n/n^{k-1}\le p\le1$, then asymptotically almost surely every spanning subhypergraph of $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with increasing vertex-degree sequence $g_1\le\cdots\le g_n$ satisfying
  \[
  g_i\ge\left(\left(\frac{i}{n}\right)^{k-1}+\gamma\right)
  \binom{n-1}{k-1}p
  \qquad(1\le i<n/2)
  \]
  contains a Hamilton Berge cycle.
  The term $(i/n)^{k-1}$ agrees with the normalized asymptotic degree bound in Salia's deterministic P\'osa-type theorem. Our result gives a hypergraph analogue of the random-graph theorem of Condon et al. and strengthens the sharp Dirac-type resilience theorem of Chen and Zhang at the same logarithmic probability order. The deletion-resilience formulation has optimal probability order up to constant factors. The coefficient $1$ of $(i/n)^{k-1}$ cannot be replaced by a smaller constant. The proof controls adaptive rotations and representative-edge incidences uniformly. It also gives an endpoint-growth estimate under nonuniform deletion bounds.

authors.name: Qinghai Liu
authors.institution: Xuan Wu Hospital of the Capital Medical University

papers.title: MobiInfer: Accelerating On-Device GUI Agents with Workload-Aware Inference
papers.abstract: Mobile GUI agents assist users in executing phone tasks through iterative observe-reason-act loops. However, deploy ing multimodal GUI agents directly on smartphones is challenging due to strict end-to-end latency requirements and significant memory overhead. We observe that GUI-agent work loads exhibit recurring workflows and structured I/O: their prompts contain reusable context, while their outputs follow fixed schemas with phase-dependent predictability. Based on this observation, we present MobiInfer, a workload-aware inference engine for on-device multimodal GUI agents. MobiInfer combines trajectory-aware prefix reuse, phase-indexed vocabulary specialization, and schema-guided speculative decoding to eliminate redundant prefill computation and reduce structured-generation overhead. We implement MobiInfer on top of MNN and evaluate it on AndroidWorld and a real world dataset using three real Android devices. Across the four model-benchmark settings, MobiInfer achieves average speedups of 2.6x in prefill and 2.5x in decoding, reduces end-to-end task latency by 2.4x on average, and cuts total deployment storage by 30%, while limiting task-success degradation to less than one percentage point.

authors.name: Siming Chen
authors.institution: Beijing Academy of Agriculture and Forestry Sciences

papers.title: Domain-uniform integration lower bounds and local information
papers.abstract: We study deterministic numerical integration on open subsets of $\mathbb R^d$ of volume one. Let $e_n$ be the minimal worst-case error using at most $n$ function values. For twice continuously differentiable functions with the normalized Lipschitz bounds proposed by Novak, we prove $e_n\geq v_d^{-2/d}n^{-2/d}/(4(d+2))\geq(8\pi\mathrm e)^{-1}n^{-2/d}$, where $v_d$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball. This resolves Novak's conjecture: the lower-bound constant is independent of the dimension and the shape of the domain. A midpoint rule on the cube has the same rate, up to an absolute constant. The proof uses smooth functions that vanish near the sample points and are large elsewhere. The bound therefore remains valid when each sample supplies all local information about the function. For scalar linear targets continuous in the uniform norm, we prove a second result on the global smooth class with prescribed function, gradient, and Hessian bounds: adaptive local information has the same minimal error as values and gradients at points chosen in advance. We give extensions to function recovery, finite integration measures, and anisotropic derivative bounds.

papers.title: Transformer-Based Characterization of Criticality in Directed Percolation
papers.abstract: Directed percolation (DP) provides a canonical framework for studying nonequilibrium phase transitions into absorbing states, yet extracting critical behavior directly from high-dimensional spatiotemporal configurations remains challenging. Here, we investigate (1 + 1)- and (2 + 1)-dimensional bond DP using a supervised Transformer encoder. Supervised learning results demonstrate that the Transformer can distinguish between the active and absorbing phases of directed percolation with high accuracy. The critical point and critical exponents estimated from the model's classification probabilities align closely with reference values from existing literature, indicating that the model not only achieves phase classification but also yields outputs containing information related to critical scaling behavior. To probe the model's internal representation, we employ attention rollout and define an attention center that quantifies the temporal centroid of the cumulative attention distribution. The attention patterns and the attention center reorganize systematically near the critical region and exhibit pronounced finite-size dependence. Finally, we examined the model's transferability between configurations generated from fully occupied initial states and those from single-seed initial states. The results indicate the presence of transferable information between the two types of data, though the transfer performance exhibits directional asymmetry. Furthermore, when using an equal amount of target-domain data, fine-tuning yielded only a marginal improvement in accuracy compared to training from scratch.

papers.title: Entropic Martingale Optimal Transport with Wasserstein Relaxed Marginal Constraints
papers.abstract: Martingale optimal transport (MOT) is a fundamental framework in robust finance, yet its stability under marginal perturbation no longer holds in high dimensions $d\geq 2$. In this paper, we introduce Wasserstein-relaxed entropic martingale optimal transport (WEMOT), which combines Wasserstein relaxation of the second marginal with entropy regularization. This formulation ensures stability under perturbations of the marginals, thereby facilitating numerical implementation. We establish strong duality and dual attainment for WEMOT, which leads to efficient Sinkhorn-type algorithms. We further prove a convergence rate of WEMOT to MOT as regularization parameters vanish, and also the quantitative stability of WEMOT with respect to marginal perturbations.

papers.title: Energy-Aware Vertically Layered Pinching-Antenna System Design with Probabilistic LoS Availability
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a vertically layered pinching antenna (PA) system, in which dielectric waveguides deployed at different heights provide additional vertical spatial degrees of freedom for line-of-sight (LoS)-favorable PA placement. We consider a practical energy model that captures in-waveguide attenuation, base station-to-feed-point optical-fiber loss, and PA repositioning energy, along with a statistical LoS-availability model that depends on elevation and distance. We then jointly optimize the transmit beamforming, PA positions, time allocation, and transmission rates to maximize the expected successfully delivered frame-effective sum rate under per-user outage and quality-of-service constraints. To avoid enumerating the exponentially many LoS states, we derive a certified conditional-moment outage envelope for outage-guaranteed rate selection and a differentiable safe approximation of the chance constraints to facilitate tractable optimization. Building on these results, a block coordinate descent algorithm with a penalty-aided majorization-minimization procedure attains a high-quality suboptimal solution. Simulation results confirm the gains of vertical layering and reveal a fundamental energy-LoS tradeoff: LoS-favorable PA placement generally enhances both performance and reliability, although it incurs higher attenuation, path loss, and energy costs.

papers.title: Mind the Divergence: Divergence-Guided Reliability-Aware Fusion and Adaptive LLM Prompting for Conversational Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition in conversations (MERC) integrates textual, acoustic, and visual cues to identify utterance-level emotions. However, existing approaches generally do not explicitly adapt multimodal processing to the degree of inter-modal predictive disagreement. In real conversations, semantic incongruity, concealed emotion, noisy observations, and ambiguity can affect modality-specific emotional evidence differently, while the reliability of individual modalities varies across samples. Rather than identifying each source of inconsistency separately, we model their common consequence for emotion recognition as predictive disagreement among unimodal emotion distributions over the same emotion-label set. Such disagreement makes indiscriminate fusion prone to propagating unreliable or competing evidence. Inspired by the Brunswik Lens Model, we propose MiD-ERC, a divergence-centric framework that quantifies inter-modal predictive disagreement using a normalized divergence score and estimates sample-specific modality reliability. MiD-ERC uses these signals to coordinate divergence-guided cross-modal gating, divergence-modulated reliability weighting, and divergence-conditioned adaptive LLM prompting. The framework is trained end-to-end using only standard emotion annotations, without requiring additional conflict labels, auxiliary data construction, or external retrieval modules. Experiments on IEMOCAP and MELD demonstrate that MiD-ERC achieves state-of-the-art performance, with particularly pronounced improvements on high-divergence samples.

authors.name: Yuhang Qian
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

authors.name: Yuyin Wang
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation
papers.abstract: A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels. On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate $[n+s_+^2/(m^{-1}+\tau^2)]^{-1}$ in the transferable strength $s_+$ and the tilt $\tau$, separating source sampling uncertainty ($m^{-1}$) from relation uncertainty ($\tau^2$). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown $s_+$ and $\tau$ up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.

authors.name: Aoran Chen
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: MotionCore: A Latent Neural Simulator for Video Generation with Rigid-Body Dynamics
papers.abstract: Video generation models can produce highly realistic videos while generating physically inconsistent object motion. This limitation suggests that visual modeling alone may not provide a transferable representation of physical dynamics. We introduce MotionCore, a framework for learning physical dynamics via a learnable partial differential equation solver and focuses on rigid-body motion. We introduce a latent neural simulator learning to predict the evolution of object-level physical states from observed motion. Its predictions are then converted into spatially aligned latent controls for a controllable video diffusion model. The generator serves as a visual interface: it provides appearance and scene detail, while the learned dynamics model specifies the physical trajectory. To preserve this trajectory through the interface, MotionCore combines a diffusion-matching objective with a low-capacity decodability constraint on object identity and position. We evaluate MotionCore on public physical-consistency benchmarks and on paired data with known trajectories. Results indicate that MotionCore improves physical consistency and trajectory obedience in the evaluated rigid-body settings, while maintaining comparable visual quality. A controlled ablation protocol compares learned dynamics with an analytic prior and studies the choice of latent evolution processor.

authors.name: Zheng Wang
authors.institution: State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine of the People's Republic of China

authors.name: Yuanzhi Liang
authors.institution: Beijing Academy of Quantum Information Sciences

papers.title: Tidal Braking Does Not Dominate Open-Cluster Slow Rotators
papers.abstract: Extended main-sequence turn-offs (eMSTOs) observed in open clusters younger than $2~\mathrm{Gyr}$ are commonly attributed to a spread in stellar rotation rates. Tidal synchronization in close binary systems has been proposed as a possible mechanism for producing slowly rotating stars. To test this hypothesis, we measured the radial-velocity (RV) dispersions of slow-rotator samples associated with the eMSTOs of eight open clusters using ESO VLT/GIRAFFE and SALT/RSS spectroscopy. We extended the analysis to 40 open clusters using Gaia DR3 RV measurements. The observed cluster RV dispersions are generally substantially smaller than those predicted for binary populations dominated by close systems with orbital periods for which tidal synchronization is expected to be effective. In particular, all 40 clusters in the Gaia sample have RV dispersions below the prediction of the $P=10$ d binary-population model. These results suggest that close, tidally synchronized binaries are unlikely to be the dominant origin of slow-rotator populations in young and intermediate-age open clusters, although a contribution from undetected or wider binary systems cannot be excluded.

papers.title: DRAFT-Bench: Evaluating Frontier Agents Across the Professional Design Lifecycle
papers.abstract: Can frontier general-purpose agents understand client intent, explore creative directions, execute revisions, and prepare production deliverables? We introduce DRAFT-Bench (Design Reliability Across Feedback and Tasks), a lifecycle-oriented evaluation of requirement elicitation, creative exploration, constrained editing, iterative revision, and production handoff. Its Requirement-to-Artifact framework links evolving requirements, protected properties, artifact versions, and delivery obligations. We compare native Codex/Astra and Claude Code across 35 design briefs under 43 conditions, alongside a separate 40-scenario RFQ track. Astra completes 43/43 design conditions and Claude 35/43. All scored core runs receive full structural credit, yet on the 28 core conditions scored for both systems, semantic checks flag violations in 11 for Astra and 5 for Claude; these are model judgments, not expert-confirmed failure rates. RFQ coverage is high, but success ordering changes across cohorts. SKU expansion, revision dependencies, and White ink files expose ambiguity among unmet obligations, missing inputs, and evaluator interpretations. These findings separate execution, requirement compliance, and professional acceptance. Unpaired tracks and different tools preclude claims of RFQ-to-delivery success, factory acceptance, or a pure model ranking.

papers.title: RevoSim: Scalable Multimodal Tactile Simulation for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.abstract: We present RevoSim, a scalable and high-fidelity multimodal tactile simulator for the BrainCo Revo3 hand that jointly models 285 piezoresistive taxels and five visuotactile fingertips. RevoSim efficiently generates synchronized pressure, depth, RGB, and marker-displacement observations; on a single RTX 5090, its depth-conditioned marker-displacement configuration supports up to 4,096 parallel environments. We train in-hand manipulation and grasping policies entirely in simulation, establishing a foundation for future sim-to-real transfer. Project page: https://braincotech.github.io/RevoSim-web/.

authors.name: Lixin Xu
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

authors.name: Renjing Xu
authors.institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

papers.title: Global Sinkhorn Convergence and Spectral Stability of Matrix Scaling
papers.abstract:
We give a global spectral bound for the Sinkhorn--Knopp (SK) algorithm. Let $A$ be a row-stochastic nonnegative $n\times n$ matrix admitting a finite doubly stochastic scaling $B$. Define \[
  g=1-s_2(B)^2>0,
  \qquad
  D=\min\left\{\|(u,v)\|_\infty:
  B=\operatorname{diag}(e^u)A\operatorname{diag}(e^{-v})\right\}. \] From the standard initialization, SK achieves total marginal $\ell_1$ error $\varepsilon$ in \[
  O\!\left(\frac{D+\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)}{g}\right) \] iterations. A scale-invariant potential contracts globally according to the spectrum of $B$. The linear dependence on $D$ is necessary in the fixed-gap regime: we construct strictly positive inputs with constant input and endpoint spectral gaps, $D=\Theta(n)$, and an $\Omega(n)$ iteration lower bound at error $n^{-2}$. Our upper bound gives $O(n)$ iterations on this family.
  We next give spectral certificates for scalability and short scaling distance. For a row-stochastic input $A$ with positive column sums $c_j$, set \[
  K=\frac{\max_jc_j}{\min_jc_j},\qquad
  \sigma=s_2\!\left(A\operatorname{diag}(c)^{-1/2}\right). \] The input-only condition $\sqrt K\,\sigma<1$ certifies exact scalability and polynomial scaling distortion, with $D=O(\log n)$ for fixed $K$ and a fixed positive spectral margin. Given a finite scaling $B$, the weaker condition $\sqrt K\,\sigma s_2(B)<1$ gives the same structural bounds. With a constant endpoint gap, these bounds imply logarithmic SK iteration complexity. Boundary constructions show that the strict spectral inequalities cannot uniformly be replaced by nonstrict ones.

papers.title: Twisted Verlinde Formula for Finite Cyclic Orbifolds of Vertex Operator Algebras
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be a simple, rational, $C_2$-cofinite and self-dual vertex operator algebra of CFT type, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic automorphism group of $V$. We establish a twisted Verlinde formula for cyclic groups of arbitrary finite order, expressing fusion coefficients among twisted $V$-modules in terms of the $S$-matrix in the orbifold theory. As an application, we compute fusion rules among twisted modules for the permutation orbifold $\left(V^{\otimes k}\right)^{\langle g\rangle}$ associated with a $k$-cycle $g=(1\,2\,\cdots\,k)$.

papers.title: Symmetry-Gated Sliding: Decoupling Interlayer Translation from Polarization Reversal in Boron Nitride Ferroelectrics
papers.abstract: Electric-field-driven polarization switching in sliding ferroelectrics depends on how local interlayer motion is accommodated by the surrounding structure. Yet the relationship between sliding, domain-wall (DW) propagation, and collective domain evolution under changing vector fields remains unclear. Here, we show that local symmetry governs the coupling between field-induced forces and interlayer sliding, while DW connectivity determines how local motion contributes to net domain conversion. These effects are examined across three structural scales, from monodomains and isolated DWs to reconstructed moire networks. We investigate bilayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) using molecular dynamics with a machine-learning interatomic potential that incorporates field-dependent electric enthalpy. An initially monodomain bilayer switches through directional wrinkling and interlayer sliding, while the barrier along a constrained flat path remains finite. Pre-existing DWs propagate with velocities governed by their shear and tensile character, and an additional in-plane field tunes wall velocity and width according to its orientation. In reconstructed triangular moire networks, shared junctions and boundary curvature mediate domain evolution and recovery after field removal or reversal. Most strikingly, a rotating in-plane field translates the layers and displaces the moir\'e nodes by approximately 1 AA yet leaves the AB/BA domain-area ratio without detectable change, because threefold connectivity cancels the contributions of individual walls. We term this response polarization-silent sliding. These results distinguish local sliding, DW translation, and net domain conversion as different responses to electric fields and establish how local structural symmetry and DW connectivity shape their selective control.

papers.title: The dynamics through the first two Lagrange necks in the small-mass restricted three-body problem
papers.abstract: We study the planar circular restricted three-body problem (PCR3BP) for sufficiently small mass ratios, from low energies to slightly above the second Lagrange value. We show that retrograde orbits around the primaries and Lyapunov orbits at the necks form the binding of a finite energy foliation. We construct these foliations using the theory of pseudoholomorphic curves in symplectizations developed by Hofer, Wysocki and Zehnder. Slightly above the second Lagrange value, the dynamics is transverse to families of disks bounded by the retrograde orbits, and cylinders connecting the retrograde orbits to the Lyapunov orbits, forming a $3-2-3-2$ foliation. The proof uses the rotating Kepler problem and Hill's lunar problem to control the singular limit as the mass ratio $\mu \to 0$. As a consequence of the foliation, both Lyapunov orbits have infinitely many homoclinic orbits.

authors.name: Pedro A. S. Salomao
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
papers.abstract: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.

authors.name: Long Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Grounding-Aware Judge Reward Reinforcement Learning for Out-of-Domain Face Anti-Spoofing
papers.abstract: Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) must distinguish genuine faces from presentation attacks. A unified Multimodal Large Language Model (MLLM) is an attractive solution: it detects physical attacks (print, replay, mask) in one model and produces interpretable forensic evidence via Chain-of-Thought (CoT). A central obstacle to post-training such a model with reinforcement learning is that FAS reasoning has no rule-verifiable ground truth: only the binary verdict is checkable, while the reasoning chain cannot be verified by any hand-crafted rule. Optimizing the verdict alone is therefore a sparse, hackable signal. The model can reach the correct answer through a shortcut such as a false-rejection bias, which does not generalize. We address this with a grounding-aware judge reward. A 32B vision-language judge scores each reasoning chain against the image on evidence anchoring, logical coherence, and domain knowledge, turning the image itself into the verification signal. The reward is applied in a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) stage after CoT supervised fine-tuning. It is the judge, rather than the RL objective, that supplies the process supervision a verdict-only reward cannot. Our study starts from a model that already performs well In-Domain (ID) after CoT-based supervised fine-tuning and asks how to improve its Out-of-Domain (OOD) generalization. We find that grounding-aware rewards are an effective means to that end. We validate the method on OOD generalization, where the reward reduces ACER on two physical benchmarks (LCC-FASD 0.288 to 0.273, MSU-MFSD 0.431 to 0.409) while preserving ID accuracy (CelebA-Spoof 0.033 to 0.035). Against ResNet-50/101 and CLIP-ViT-B/16 baselines, the MLLM dominates ID and matches or surpasses the strongest baseline OOD. To our knowledge this is the first use of LLM-as-judge process supervision for FAS.

authors.name: Xiaoyong Yu
authors.institution: Heilongjiang Center for Tuberculosis Control and Prevention

papers.title: Characterization of Attenuated V-Line Transform and Direct Reconstruction from Samples
papers.abstract: The V-line transform (V-LT), a generalized Radon transform (RT), is widely used in Compton scattering imaging (CSI). The central mathematical problem of CSI is to reconstruct a function from its V-LT. Unlike V-LT, the attenuated V-line transform (AV-LT) accounts for the medium-induced loss of intensity, and has been demonstrated to improve image quality. The present paper makes two main contributions. (1) We establish the fundamental characterizations for AV-LT including operator properties ($L^2$-boundedness, operator norm etc.), a necessary and sufficient condition for the preservation of compact support, and sharp estimation of Sobolev smoothness. These characterizations remain unexplored, and they reveal essential differences among AV-LT, RT and V-LT. (2) We develop a direct reconstruction method based on AV-LT samples that does not require solving any equation. Our sampling formula gives exact reconstruction for band-limited functions. We also provide approximate reconstruction for functions in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with $s>2$.

papers.title: BrainCoT: A Multi-Task Zero-Shot Brain Signal Foundation Model with Neurometric-Anchored Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.abstract: Brain signals exhibit substantial multi-center heterogeneity, strong inter-subject variability, and highly diverse task settings, which makes it difficult to build models that generalize beyond a single task. While recent brain signal foundation models leverage large-scale pretraining to learn generalizable representations, they often fall short in practice because they still require target-data-specific supervised adaptation, lack multi-task zero-shot capability, and rarely provide verifiable evidence to support their predictions. In this work, we present BrainCoT, a multi-task zero-shot Brain signal foundation model with neurometric-anchored Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. BrainCoT unifies heterogeneous tasks into an instruction-driven framework so that, after pretraining, a single model can be directly applied to multiple tasks in zero-shot settings without additional adaptation. It further introduces neurometric-anchored chain-of-thought grounded in neurometric evidence for verifiable reasoning, and adopts Decision-Consistent Rationale Training to keep process learning aligned with correct predictions. Across extensive evaluations, BrainCoT achieves an average ACC of 67.41% and AUC of 74.33% in zero-shot classification without downstream training data, outperforming the strongest linear-probing baseline trained with 1% labeled downstream data by 3.85% in ACC and 5.97% in AUC.

papers.title: Strong phonon-coupled trion emission in Janus homobilayer
papers.abstract: Janus transition metal dichalcogenides with broken mirror symmetry provide a novel platform for exploring many-body effects mediated by spin-valley-phonon interactions. Strong electron-phonon coupling demands a precise match between a strong effective dipole moment and nanometer-scale charge confinement. Here, we report thermally robust and enhanced trion emission in a symmetric bilayer WSeS with an S/S stacking configuration. The inward-pointing antiparallel built-in electric fields induce a strong electron confinement effect at the interface, driving dominant trion emission at cryogenic temperatures. Furthermore, a massive electron-phonon coupling strength (3.9) resonant with the optical phonon A_1^2 energy (51 meV) contributes to the thermal stability of this trion emission at elevated temperatures. By tailoring the interfacial architecture in Janus WSeS homobilayers, this study overcomes the thermal decoherence limits inherent to traditional semiconductor systems, offering novel insights into room-temperature many-body interactions.

authors.name: Tianyishan Sun
authors.institution: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University

authors.name: Dingkun Bi
authors.institution: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University

authors.name: Hiroto Ogura
authors.institution: Institute for Materials Research, Tohoku University

authors.name: Yanlin Gao
authors.institution: Beijing Center for Disease Prevention and Control

authors.name: Shiro Entani
authors.institution: National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology

papers.title: Group Invariance of Statistical Models and Associated Statistical Manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the group invariance of a parameterized statistical model that is closed under push-forward sample transformations given by a group action. We prove that the group action on the sample space induces an isometric action on the associated statistical manifold. Furthermore, it preserves the Fisher-Rao metric as well as the Amari-Chentsov tensor. Moreover, we establish that this isometric action is compatible with equivariant and sufficient statistics in the spirit of the Hall-Wijsman-Ghosh generalized Stein's theorem. This compatibility leads to a novel reduction of the original group-invariant model, where its Fisher information loss is explicitly quantified via conditional expectation. As an application, we apply this framework to a generalized cardioid distribution in circular data analysis, illustrating how the reduced model facilitates estimation and hypothesis testing for relative parameters.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
papers.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $9.6\times10^{-42}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $\alpha\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.

authors.name: Lei Feng
authors.institution: Ministry of Public Security of the People's Republic of China

papers.title: PAGSL: Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning for explainable scholar recommendation
papers.abstract: Explainable scholar recommendation aims to identify potential scholars of interest and provide reasonable explanations for the recommendations. However, existing frameworks struggle with optimization-induced noise and "hub node bias", yielding trivial explanations that lack hierarchical depth and personalization. To this end, we propose a novel explainable scholar recommendation model, Path-Augmenting Graph Structure Learning (named PAGSL). PAGSL combines representation learning and semantic path knowledge to ensure recommendation performance while providing interpretable results from two perspectives. Specifically, it activates latent academic paths among entities through graph augmentation and employs a path-based neural network to encode these paths for recommendation. A masking mechanism with path score optimization is designed to generate concise and informative explanations. We evaluate PAGSL on three academic datasets (Scholat, AMiner, and ResearchGate), comprising approximately 49,000 authors and over 330,000 interaction records. Experimental evaluations validate that PAGSL outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving significant improvements of 6.31\% in F1-score, 6.29\% in Accuracy and 5.95\% in AUC for recommendation. Crucially, in terms of explainability, we provide quantitative results and visualization effects. Furthermore, ablation studies validate the effectiveness of our heterogeneous convolution and path representation learning. PAGSL achieves strong performance in both recommendation accuracy and explainability.

authors.name: Jiale Xu
authors.institution: Shandong University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

authors.name: Mingshu Ai
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Strong convergence rates for numerical approximations of the stochastic Burgers equation with additive rough noise
papers.abstract: We establish strong convergence rates for a fully discrete method of the one-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation driven by additive rough noise. Using the Cole-Hopf transformation, the equation is converted into a linear stochastic heat equation, which is discretized by a spectral Galerkin method in space and an accelerated exponential Euler method in time. A numerical approximation of the original solution is then reconstructed through a regularized inverse Cole-Hopf transformation. The analysis combines strong Sobolev error estimates with the positivity and inverse-moment bounds for the transformed solution. For additive space-time white noise, the numerical method achieves mean-square convergence rates arbitrarily close to 1/2 in space and 1/4 in time. The rates are slower when the noises are rougher.

authors.name: Ziyi Lei
authors.institution: Academy of Mathematics and Systems Science

papers.title: Campana points on quadrics with hyperplane boundary
papers.abstract: Let $Q\subset\mathbf P^{d+1}_k$ be a smooth quadric of dimension $d\ge2$ over a number field, and let $H_i=Q\cap\Pi_i$ be hyperplane sections for $1\le i\le d$. For every integer $m\ge2$, we prove Campana strong approximation for the pair $\bigl(Q,(1-1/m)(H_1+\cdots+H_d)_{\mathrm{red}}\bigr)$.

papers.title: $\mathrm{X}$-evolution flows/foliations for cluster algebras: partial Bongartz (co-)completions and acyclicity
papers.abstract: We first generalize the notion of $\mathrm{X}$-foliation on cluster complexes to the context of cluster algebras. This is a continuous generalization of Keller's green mutation, which was previously introduced in the prequel within a categorical setting. We show that the wall-crossing structure (of possibly higher co-dimension) is encoded by $\mathrm{X}$-supports, which form a partial version of Cao-Gyoda-Yurikusa's Bongartz (co-)completions for cluster algebras. Moreover, we prove that for any cell transversed nontrivially by a fixed $\mathrm{X}$-leaf, its rank is an invariant bounded below by the rank of $\mathrm{X}$. Finally, we prove the acyclicity conjecture for $\mathrm{X}$-foliation, which also implies the compactness conjecture for any $\mathrm{X}$-foliation in finite type cases.

papers.title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI
papers.abstract: Edge applications increasingly combine CNN-based perception with edge-deployable Transformer-based language models, but deploying such heterogeneous workloads on resource-constrained devices is challenging because inference latency varies with both input difficulty and runtime hardware state. Early-exit inference reduces computation by terminating at intermediate stages, yet existing methods are often model-specific and rely on static latency profiles that become stale under dynamic edge conditions. This paper presents UniExit, a unified latency-aware early-exit runtime for heterogeneous edge AI. UniExit abstracts CNN blocks and Transformer layers as ordered stages and applies a common latency-aware routing policy while retaining model-specific quality mechanisms. It predicts the cost of reaching the next exit from runtime state and inference progress to make budget-aware continue-or-exit decisions. UniExit combines runtime-state-aware latency prediction, cache-based prediction reuse, trend-aware fallback, and CNN-specific exit stabilization to provide low-overhead and robust online control. We implement UniExit on multiple edge and edge-cloud platforms and evaluate it with representative CNN and Transformer-based language-model workloads. Across single-workload, concurrent heterogeneous, and edge-cloud settings, UniExit consistently improves deadline satisfaction and latency-accuracy trade-offs over existing progressive inference baselines, while reducing redundant exit-module computation and task-level energy consumption.

authors.name: Xiaomin Ouyang
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Lefschetz-Thimble Method to the Sign Problem in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev Model
papers.abstract: The sign problem in path integrals severely limits the application of quantum Monte Carlo methods to strongly correlated systems, whereas the Lefschetz-thimble method offers a rigorous framework to mitigate this issue. In this paper, we establish a numerical framework based on the Lefschetz thimbles for the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. By introducing continuous auxiliary fields via the Hubbard-Stratonovich transformation, the partition function is formulated as a high-dimensional complex integral. We employ the complex Langevin equation to explore the saddle-point distribution of the effective action in the complex plane. Monte Carlo integration is then performed to compute the partition function and Green functions. Our numerical results exhibit excellent agreement with high-temperature expansions, infrared-limit solutions, and determinantal quantum Monte Carlo (DQMC) simulations, confirming the validity of our framework. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our complex Langevin search successfully captures the relevant dominant saddle points governing the SYK model in the large-N limit. Our work deepens the understanding of the sign problem in the SYK model and provides a viable non-perturbative avenue for addressing sign problems in more complex strongly correlated systems.

authors.name: Yin-Hao Fang
authors.institution: Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

papers.title: The multiplier step size in classical two-block ADMM: convergence and counterexamples
papers.abstract: How large can the multiplier step be in the classical two-block alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM)? We keep the penalty fixed and use the usual primal updates. We consider finite-dimensional problems with closed proper convex objectives. We assume that a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point exists and that each block subproblem attains its minimum at every step. Under these assumptions, the constraint images and the multiplier converge for a range of factors that extends beyond the golden ratio. The constraint matrices may be rank deficient. For larger steps, we construct two fixed compact polytopes and give an explicit threshold below two. The polytopes admit an infeasible periodic orbit for every factor at or above this threshold. At that threshold, ADMM can cycle even for smooth strongly convex objectives. This gives a negative answer to Glowinski's question about the full interval from zero to two. A different pair of piecewise-quadratic objectives gives geometrically growing residuals. For the general convex class, we locate the endpoint of the uniform convergence interval near 1.88688256. A convergence certificate on the unit circle gives the lower bound, while a separate periodic orbit gives the upper bound. Exact arithmetic verifies that the two bounds differ by less than 0.000000174.

papers.title: FIND: Frequency Invariance Disentanglement for Test-Time Adaptation in LiDAR 3D Detection
papers.abstract: LiDAR-based 3D Object Detection (L3OD) is a fundamental 3D perception task, yet its performance is often compromised by domain shifts arising from diverse sensor configurations and environmental conditions. Existing Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) methods primarily leverage self-supervision in the spatial domain, yet they frequently confound semantic content with domain style due to the sparse, non-Euclidean nature of point clouds. To overcome this limitation, we propose FIND (Frequency INvariance Disentanglement), a novel TTA framework that precisely disentangles domain-invariant content from domain-specific interference within the frequency domain. Our methodology utilizes B-Spline fitting to construct locally adaptive filters integrated into a dual-stream architecture: an Invariant Stream extracts robust features to guide pseudo-labeling, while a Specific Stream enforces consistency against domain perturbations. By combining invariance-driven alignment with stability-guided regularization, our approach dynamically extracts robust domain-invariant features while suppressing domain-specific interference. Extensive experiments on cross-dataset adaptation and robust corruption benchmarks demonstrate that FIND significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/llldx03/FIND.

authors.name: Dongxiao Li
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Zixuan Hu
authors.institution: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

papers.title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss. Hua and Toda showed that this deformation exists, and Jelisiejew and Smoktunowicz proved its uniqueness in types A and D. The key step in our proof is that the centre of $A_{\rm{con}}$ has dimension $n_1 + \dots + n_l$. To prove this, we lift the contraction algebra of the universal flop to the Cartan subalgebra, where it becomes a corner of a deformed preprojective algebra. We show that the universal contraction algebra and its zeroth Hochschild homology are free over a polynomial ring, with presentations whose determinants are products of roots. Pulling these presentations back along the arc that classifies the flop gives the count, and recovers Toda's formula for $\dim A_{\rm{con}}$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.

papers.title: Zero-Query Transferable Pretend Benign Attacks with Amortized Online Generation for Cooperative Perception
papers.abstract: Cooperative perception enables an ego agent to acquire information from collaborators beyond its own sensors' reach. Yet, the most beneficial messages are often the hardest to verify from local observations. Pretend Benign (PB) exploits this asymmetry by targeting regions with weak local verifiability and applying multi-objective perturbations, making harmful feature changes appear to be benign assistance. However, PB is victim-dependent: selecting regions and optimizing perturbations require the victim model's architecture, parameters, and gradients, limiting transfer to unseen victims. A transferable attack must capture properties shared across cooperative detection models rather than those specific to one network. We address this by building a victim-agnostic attack from a heterogeneous ensemble of surrogate models and encoding its capabilities in a reusable dictionary to reduce per-message generation cost. Specifically, Transferable Pretend Benign (TrPB) transfers PB's region selection criterion and multi-objective perturbation strategy across heterogeneous surrogates to construct an offline attack. We further propose RT-TrPB, which encodes transferable regions and perturbation patterns into a region predictor and reusable perturbation dictionary, amortizing per-message attack generation. Experiments on widely used cooperative perception benchmarks show that RT-TrPB bypasses the consensus-based defenses ROBOSAC and FLD with success rates approaching 100% and generates each perturbation in under 56 ms. To counter PB-style attacks masquerading as benign collaboration, we also propose STTrust, which verifies received messages using spatial and temporal consistency and incorporates identity-level trust. STTrust detects over 90% of PB-style attacks and restores perception performance to near the attack-free level.

authors.name: Cheng Wang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

papers.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
papers.abstract: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. The Bayes factor in favor of a hierarchical triple merger origin over the non-association hypothesis is $110$. However, after accounting for the priors odds, the corresponding odds ratio decreases to $0.1$, indicating that the current evidence is insufficient to favor the hierarchical triple merger scenario. GW230720\_0823 show no detectable signatures of orbit eccentricity or line-of-sight acceleration. The inferred properties of these two gravitational wave events suggest a dynamical formation channel, such as few-body scattering or gas-assisted mergers, while a primordial triple origin is disfavored. Among the proposed dynamical environments, the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus provides the most plausible site. We further derive constraints on the local rate of hierarchical triple mergers rate under both the null and candidate scenarios. Under the assumption of no detected hierarchical triple mergers, the most stringent $90\%$ confidence upper limit is $4.2\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ for $t_{\rm max}=10$ years using the GWTC-4 catalog.

papers.title: Period bounds for Bergman kernel variation and the Suita defect
papers.abstract: The periods of holomorphic differentials give an explicit lower bound for the curvature of Bergman evaluation matrices. We prove this bound along the Green sublevels of a smooth plane domain. For scalar evaluation at the Green pole, equality at one regular level holds precisely when that sublevel is simply connected. For complete jets at the Green pole, the matrices have continuous first derivatives, including at critical levels, and their logarithmic determinant defects are integrals of nonnegative curvature densities. A further estimate bounds the accumulated period energy by the determinant defect, with a constant independent of the jet order. On a multiply connected domain, all these defects vanish up to the first critical Green value and become strictly positive above it.

papers.title: A Structural Lower Bound for the Ramsey Number of the Petersen Graph
papers.abstract: In this note, we investigate the diagonal Ramsey number of the Petersen graph, denoted by \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P})\). To the best of our knowledge, the dynamic survey \textit{Small Ramsey Numbers} (Revision \#18, 2026) records the lower bound as 19, established by Harborth and Krause. We construct a novel 2-coloring on the complete graph \(K_{20}\) that avoids any monochromatic Petersen graph. By defining the blue graph as the complement of the red graph, we utilize a specific join graph structure \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_2}\). We rigorously prove its Petersen-free property, thereby improving the previously documented lower bound to \(R(\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}) \ge 21\). Furthermore, we demonstrate the limit of this structural family by showing that the natural extension \(K_{9,9} \vee \overline{K_3}\) contains a Petersen subgraph.

papers.title: Fluctuations of heat kernels and exit times on random graphs and application to the critical long-range percolation
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a graph equipped with random conductance. We give sufficient conditions for the Markov chain on $\mathcal{G}$ to exhibit large scale fluctuations in its on-diagonal heat kernel and in exit times. The conditions also imply non-tightness of the height process w.r.t. the quenched measure, while it is tight w.r.t. the annealed measure. As an application of the general theory, we prove large scale fluctuations for the simple random walk on $1$-dimensional critical long-range percolation.

papers.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Policy entropy is widely used to diagnose exploration and collapse in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), yet its magnitude does not consistently track reasoning performance across optimization objectives. We argue that this ambiguity arises because global token entropy conflates uncertainty in successful and failed trajectories, diversity across correct solution strategies, and variation among realizations of the same strategy. We introduce \textbf{Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA)}, a hierarchical diagnostic framework that separates complete-trajectory entropy from average token entropy, conditions uncertainty on verifier outcome and process validity, measures correct-solution-mode retention, and connects these population-level quantities to local covariance-driven updates. In controlled sweeps over six RLVR objectives at two model scales, entropy trajectories do not induce a stable ordering of reasoning accuracy. Token entropy is higher for verifier-failed than successful trajectories under both broad separately aggregated estimates and a common-question paired analysis, whose confidence intervals exclude equality at 10 of 12 displayed endpoints. A local covariance approximation predicts the direction of adjacent-checkpoint entropy change in 95.5\% of nonfailed transitions; a reward-stratified endpoint proxy further shows that positive chosen-token covariance is more tail-concentrated within failed prefixes. Every reportable trained endpoint exhibits some contraction in independently audited correct-solution-mode breadth, whose positive association with large-\(k\) coverage remains exploratory. These results show that entropy collapse should be diagnosed by which uncertainty is removed, rather than by global entropy alone.

authors.name: Song Yu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Zhenming Wu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Oncology in South China

papers.title: StockASkill: A Local-First AgentSkill for Intelligent Stock Selection
papers.abstract: Quantitative equity selection and portfolio construction in emerging and cross-border markets frequently suffer from computational bottlenecks, remote API fragility, survivorship bias, and rigid execution constraints such as discrete board lots and investor-mandated drawdown limits. In this paper, we present StockASkill, a local-first, full-data-driven AgentSkill engineered as a specialized Quant Co-Processor for autonomous AI agents and quantitative researchers. Tailored for agile portfolios (10^5 ~ 10^7 RMB) where discrete lot execution and capital protection are mandatory, StockASkill embeds a columnar DuckDB OLAP engine over 42.44 million historical price records and 186,432 financial disclosures spanning 26 years across China A-shares, Hong Kong, US equities, and ETFs. By eliminating ad-hoc network dependencies during analysis, StockASkill reduces cross-sectional screening latency across 5,400+ equities from over 25 seconds to sub-0.5 seconds (a 95%+ reduction). We formalize an end-to-end mathematical pipeline integrating a 7+1 factor alpha model, an SLSQP convex optimizer under smooth CVaR drawdown surrogates with exact path projection, dynamic 100-share board lot integer quantization, and an autonomous thesis lifecycle finite-state machine. Furthermore, we provide a zero-disk, strongly-typed JSON streaming interface designed for high-throughput LLM tool-calling. Open-sourced at https://github.com/axjing/stockaskill, comprehensive empirical benchmarks from 2018 to 2024 demonstrate that the architecture achieves annualized Sharpe ratios exceeding 1.48 and Calmar ratios up to 2.17, while reducing max drawdown by up to 85% relative to benchmark indices.

papers.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications
papers.abstract: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.

authors.name: Xueting Zhao
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Permutation polynomials from quadratic and linear forms
papers.abstract: We investigate a family of permutation polynomials of finite fields using the theory of quadratic and linear forms. For an odd prime power $q$, consider polynomials over $\mathbb F_{q^n}$ of the form $\sum_{0\le i\le j<n}a_{ij}x^{q^i+q^j}+L(x)$, where $a_{ij}\in\mathbb F_{q^n}$ and $L$ serves as an $\mathbb F_q$-linear endomorphism of $\mathbb F_{q^n}$. In this paper, we begin with a general treatment over arbitrary fields of characteristic not $2$, and then provide explicit characterizations for several classes of such permutation polynomials.

papers.title: Multipole Decomposition of Moving Sources
papers.abstract: Cartesian multipole moments are widely used to analyze and engineer radiation, but the usual relations for their radiated fields assume a wavevector-independent source frequency. For moving sources, Doppler shifts make the frequency depend on the wavevector, so the radiated fields predicted from the moments generally carry errors proportional to v/c. From charge conservation in the laboratory frame, we derive a multipole decomposition of moving sources that retains the usual moments but evaluates their contributions at Doppler-shifted wavenumbers and adds a convection-current term. Requiring no rest frame, it applies to moving matter and to excitation patterns in synthetic motion through media at rest, including superluminal ones. The decomposition also extends to nonuniform translation and to nonrigid patterns with curved spectral supports. Exact calculations for moving electric, magnetic, and toroidal dipoles confirm the decomposition and attribute the different radiation of a dipole in moving matter and in synthetic motion to the laboratory moments that each kind of motion induces. For an anapole, these moments decide whether it radiates. An anapole carried by uniformly moving matter remains nonradiating, whereas an excitation pattern with the same electric and toroidal dipoles radiates in synthetic motion. The decomposition thus makes multipolar analysis available for moving matter and for excitation patterns in synthetic motion, and it opens the way to designing their radiation.

authors.name: Yutong Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Dual Architecture Fusion Vehicle Lidar 3D Target Detection
papers.abstract: In this paper, a 3D backbone network (SpconvTransformer) based on the fusion of convolutional architecture branch and Transformer architecture branch is proposed. The convolution branch uses 3D sparse convolution and submanifold convolution to learn local voxel features and semantic information, and the Transformer branch uses the self-attention mechanism to model the remote relationship between voxels, uses the broad receptive field to capture rich context information, and complementing the advantages of the two architectures by fusing the local features extracted from the two branches and the global features solves the problem of limited receptive fields of 3D convolutional neural networks. The experimental results show that the average accuracy of SpconvTransformer in 3D object detection and bird's-eye view detection tasks reaches 81.45% and 88.09%, respectively, and the average directional similarity reaches 91.10%, which is significantly better than other existing algorithms.

authors.name: Muyun Li
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Luminescent Materials and Devices

papers.title: Online Causal Configuration for Networked Systems via Doubly Robust Steady-State Learning
papers.abstract: Measurement exploration reveals how interacting local controllers behave but can alter the steady-state regime a network operator seeks to optimize. Exploratory rewards may therefore fail to identify a configuration's no-exploration value: under full exploration, identical logged distributions can conceal different target values. Identification requires accounting for both action-law mismatch and shifts in the steady-state context distribution. We introduce CAUSAL-UCB, which selects configurations using optimistic bounds on target causal values. Its interference-aware clipped doubly robust evaluator produces predecision certificates separating statistical variation from calibrated identification, transport, and temporal-dependence errors. For any finite horizon and predetermined schedule of measurement-exploration rates $\{\eta_t\}$, we prove lower bounds of $\Omega((1+\sum_t\eta_t)^{-1/2})$ on minimax inference error and $\Omega(\sum_t\eta_t)$ on measurement-induced deployment loss in a stationary, potentially slow-mixing family. We bound regret under valid certificates and selected-information growth, and establish an anytime finite-sample certificate with a shared radius for estimation, selection, and reporting in a restricted known-local-interference model. In a high-mismatch benchmark with 24 paired seeds and 200 rounds, CAUSAL-UCB attains target regret of $1.732$ versus $6.326$ for certified IPS-UCB, with deployment gaps of $30.607$ and $23.217$, respectively. Independent-audit coverage tests and trace-driven semi-synthetic studies further assess certificate coverage and deployment trade-offs.

papers.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding
